findings.title: `--record` setup receipts satisfy check_apply's "the gate ran and passed" requirement, so the claim-provenance gate can be skipped entirely with exit 0
findings.what_is_wrong: `check_apply.PASSING_VERDICTS = ("pass", "recorded")`. Two of its five REQUIRED_GATES have a `--record` mode that is pure setup and writes verdict `"recorded"`: `check_claims.py:151` (fingerprint the master at mode entry) and `check_render_freshness.py:65` (hash the inputs before dispatch). Both are run at the START of apply mode per modes/apply.md:195-218. If the model then never runs the actual verification pass — the second, identical-looking `python3 scripts/check_claims.py --workspace <ws>` at modes/apply.md:210 — check_apply reads the setup receipt, sees a passing verdict, and exits 0. Worse: even after check_claims genuinely FAILS, a later `--record` (a resume, a re-entry, round 2) becomes `receipts[-1]` and clears the failure. This is verbatim the failure check_apply's own docstring exists to prevent: "a skipped script produces no output and no output is exactly what a clean run looks like." None of check_apply's five required gates ever writes `"recorded"` as a clean-CHECK verdict — parse_verdicts and lint_cv write only pass/fail/could_not_run, check_personal_data likewise — so `"recorded"` in that tuple buys nothing and costs the whole composition guarantee.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: check_apply is the gate that is supposed to report exactly this. It cannot, because it compares a verdict STRING and the setup path spells its verdict the same way a clean run does. The test suite cannot report it either: `scripts/tests/test_check_apply.py::_good_workspace` forges all five receipts with `journal.receipt(ws, gate, {}, "pass")` and never invokes a real gate, so the record-vs-verify distinction never enters a fixture. And nothing pins the token in either direction — patching `PASSING_VERDICTS` to `("pass",)` leaves 793/793 green, which means no test proves "recorded" is needed and no test proves the hole it opens.
findings.reproduction:
$ D=.../scratchpad/audit/dead-gates/bypass; WS=$D/acme-engineer-2026-08-16; S=/Users/donghanglyu/code_project/job-hunt/scripts
$ # master profile lists only Python + a Research Engineer role
$ python3 $S/enter_mode.py --workspace $WS --mode apply --skill-root /Users/donghanglyu/code_project/job-hunt
$ python3 $S/check_claims.py --workspace $WS --record --master $D/profile.yaml     # exit 0, verdict "recorded"
$ # tailored-profile.yaml now adds Kubernetes, "10 years of clinical PACS integration",
$ #   "AWS Certified Solutions Architect"; there is NO claims.yaml
$ python3 $S/check_render_freshness.py --workspace $WS --round 1 --record $WS/cv.md   # exit 0, verdict "recorded"
$ # the other three receipts forged exactly the way the repo's own fixture does; round 1 = PASS; interview-brief.md present
$ python3 $S/check_apply.py --workspace $WS --skill-root /Users/donghanglyu/code_project/job-hunt
check_apply exit=0        <-- no output, package "may be delivered"

$ # what the skipped gate would have said:
$ python3 $S/check_claims.py --workspace $WS
UNSOURCED: "Kubernetes" appears in tailored-profile.yaml:skills.languages, is absent from profile.yaml, and has no claims.yaml row. ...
UNSOURCED: "10 years of clinical PACS integration" appears in tailored-profile.yaml:skills.languages, ...
UNSOURCED: "AWS Certified Solutions Architect" appears in tailored-profile.yaml:certifications[0], ...
exit=1

$ # and the failure is erasable by the documented setup command:
$ python3 $S/check_claims.py --workspace $WS --record --master $D/profile.yaml
$ python3 $S/check_apply.py --workspace $WS --skill-root /Users/donghanglyu/code_project/job-hunt
check_apply exit=0

$ # nothing pins the token:
$ sed -i '' 's/PASSING_VERDICTS = ("pass", "recorded")/PASSING_VERDICTS = ("pass",)/' scripts/check_apply.py   # on a COPY
$ python3 -m pytest scripts/tests -q --deselect scripts/tests/test_install.py
793 passed, 4 deselected
findings.fix: scripts/check_apply.py: set `PASSING_VERDICTS = ("pass",)` (leave check_assessment.py's tuple alone — "recorded" is the legitimate clean verdict for consistency.py / count_coverage.py / check_evidence_refs.py / evidence_blocks.py, which are check_assessment's upstreams, not check_apply's). Then give the setup paths a verdict that cannot be mistaken for a check: `scripts/check_claims.py:151` and `scripts/check_render_freshness.py:65` should write `"baseline_recorded"`. Belt-and-braces in check_apply's loop: for check_claims require the last receipt's `inputs` to name `tailored-profile.yaml` (the record receipt names `profile.yaml`), which catches the case even if a verdict string drifts back. Add two tests: (a) record-only workspace → check_apply exits 1 with `MISSING_RECEIPT`/`UPSTREAM_FAILED: check_claims`; (b) real fail followed by a re-record → still exits 1.

findings.title: The test that promises SKILL.md and modes/*.md shared paragraphs are byte-identical asserts only that the intersection is non-empty — drift makes it easier to pass, never harder
findings.what_is_wrong: `scripts/tests/test_skill_structure.py:264` `test_the_paragraphs_layer_1_shares_with_a_mode_file_are_byte_identical` computes `shared = set(skill) & set(_paragraphs(mode_file))` and asserts `shared or mode_file.name != "apply.md"`. The intersection of two sets of strings is byte-identical BY CONSTRUCTION. A paragraph that has drifted simply drops out of the intersection — it is invisible to the assertion, and every drop makes the set smaller, i.e. moves toward the only condition the test checks (non-empty). The 40-line comment block above it (lines 235-246) states the exact regression it is guarding: "SKILL.md said 不是对面试或录用概率的预测 while check_assessment.py looks for the literal 不是对结果的预判 ... Nothing caught that." This test would not have caught it either.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: The test is green, its name and docstring assert the strong property ("The copies that exist must match exactly"), and nothing else in the tree compares layer 1 against layer 1.5. check_skill_lossless.py cannot help: it joins the whole corpus into one string and asks whether each BASELINE line is findable anywhere, so a paragraph drifting between two current files leaves every baseline line still present — it reported LOSSLESS 1317/1317 on the mutated tree.

$ python3 - <<'PY'   # append " (drifted paraphrase)" to 15 of the 16 paragraphs SKILL.md shares with modes/apply.md
... drifted paragraphs: 15
PY
$ python3 -m pytest scripts/tests/test_skill_structure.py -q
56 passed in 0.16s
$ python3 -m pytest scripts/tests -q --deselect scripts/tests/test_install.py
793 passed, 4 deselected in 7.17s
$ python3 scripts/check_skill_lossless.py --baseline 864ad7f
LOSSLESS: 1317/1317 baseline lines accounted for across 31 files, 20 waived
findings.fix: scripts/tests/test_skill_structure.py: pair paragraphs by NEAR-match, not by equality, then assert byte-equality of each pair. Concretely, normalize each paragraph (casefold + collapse whitespace + strip markdown emphasis/backticks) into a key; for every key present in both SKILL.md and a mode file, assert the two RAW paragraphs are equal, and report the diff. Keep the existing non-empty check for apply.md as a separate test so "the duplication was deleted" and "the duplication drifted" fail with different messages. Verify the new test by re-running the 15-paragraph drift above — it must go red.

findings.title: scripts/tests/check_assess_anchors.sh — the only guard on the ~40 literals check_assessment.py greps for in modes/assess.md — is run by nothing, and hardcodes an absolute path so a clone audits the original repo
findings.what_is_wrong: check_assessment.py keys on literal strings that only modes/assess.md teaches the model to write: `## 硬性阻断项` / `## Hard blockers` (DISQUALIFIER_HEADINGS), `## 那该怎么办` / `## What to do instead` (STRATEGY_HEADINGS), `验收标准` / `Acceptance criterion` / `输出物` / `Deliverable` (ACCEPTANCE_COLUMNS), `已过复核期` (STALE_BANNER), and the five STRATEGIES tokens. The file written to pin them, `scripts/tests/check_assess_anchors.sh`, is (a) not a pytest file, (b) not in the Makefile, (c) not in .github/workflows/checks.yml, (d) referenced nowhere outside docs/superpowers/plans/, and (e) begins `cd /Users/donghanglyu/code_project/job-hunt && python3 -c "..."` — so when it IS run, from anywhere, it audits that one absolute path rather than the tree it lives in. Rename those headings in modes/assess.md and the whole check suite stays green while the model, following layer 1.5 verbatim, writes a card that check_assessment.py rejects with NO_DISQUALIFIER_SECTION / NO_STRATEGY_SECTION / NO_ACCEPTANCE_COLUMN. This is the disclaimer-paraphrase regression the repo already fixed once, still live for four more heading pairs.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: `test_skill_structure.py::test_a_literally_matched_gate_string_appears_verbatim_in_layer_1` is parametrized over exactly two phrases (不是对结果的预判, not a forecast of the outcome) and only reads SKILL.md — it never reads modes/assess.md. `test_check_assessment.py` uses those literals inside its own synthetic fixtures, never against the shipped mode file. There is no test_mode_assess_doc.py (discover and interview both have one). And the shell script that would report it passes on a mutated clone, because it `cd`s away from the tree under test before looking.

findings.fix: Delete scripts/tests/check_assess_anchors.sh and replace it with scripts/tests/test_mode_assess_doc.py, modelled on the existing test_discover_mode_doc.py, that resolves the tree with `pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]` (never a literal path) and asserts every needle currently in the .sh appears in modes/assess.md. Generate the needles FROM the module rather than re-typing them — iterate `check_assessment.DISQUALIFIER_HEADINGS + STRATEGY_HEADINGS + STRATEGIES + (STALE_BANNER,) + VERDICT_MARKERS + DISCLAIMER_ANCHORS` and every element of `ACCEPTANCE_COLUMNS` — so adding a literal to the gate automatically becomes a required anchor instead of a silently unguarded one. findings.title: The self-check guards test only that a filename appears somewhere between `## Self-check` and EOF, so a read-when trigger line can be deleted with the suite green
findings.what_is_wrong: `test_skill_structure.py::_self_check_section()` matches `^## Self-check.*?(?=^## |\Z)`. `## Self-check` is the LAST heading in SKILL.md (line 651 of 741), so the "section" is everything to end of file. `test_the_self_check_names_every_reference_file` / `_agent_file` / `_mode_file` / `_script` then assert only `f"references/{f.name}" in section` — a bare substring, with no requirement that the mention be a `- [ ]` checklist item or a read-trigger at all. So the checklist line that tells the model to read a layer-2 file can be removed outright, provided the filename survives anywhere in the last 90 lines — including in prose, an HTML comment's neighbouring sentence, or a future appended block. This is the same section-boundary defect the project already found once ("a block appended after '## Self-check' was swallowed by that section's regex"); the swallowing is now permanent because the section runs to EOF.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: The guard IS the reporter, and it passes: the name is still in the string it searches. `test_every_path_the_self_check_names_exists` checks the other direction (named paths exist) and also passes. check_skill_lossless.py cannot see it — `references/cv-craft.md` is new content, not a baseline line, and the file itself is untouched, so it still reports 1317/1317. The layer-2 file then simply never gets read at runtime, which is the silent-omission failure the self-check exists to prevent.

findings.fix: scripts/tests/test_skill_structure.py: extract the self-check as CHECKLIST ITEMS, not as a text blob. Parse the section into the lines matching `^\s*- \[ \] `, join those, and assert the reference/agent/mode/script name appears in THAT string. Additionally bound the section explicitly — `^## Self-check.*?(?=^## |\Z)` should be paired with an assertion that SKILL.md's last heading is `## Self-check` (so the boundary is a stated invariant rather than an accident), or terminate the section at a sentinel line such as `<!-- end self-check -->`. Verify with the mutation above: deleting the cv-craft.md checklist line must go red.

findings.title: check_claims sources a tailored term by raw substring over the whole master file, so a fabricated skill is "sourced" by any longer word that contains it
findings.what_is_wrong: `scripts/check_claims.py:193` — `if len(key) < 2 or key in master_text: continue`, where `master_text` is the ENTIRE profile.yaml NFKC-folded, lowercased, punctuation-squashed into one string. The test is a raw substring, not a token match, so any fabricated atomic term that happens to be a substring of any word anywhere in the master is silently accepted. `Java` is sourced by `JavaScript`. A fabricated certification `MSc` is sourced by the degree `MSc Computer Science`. The module docstring says the opposite — "a closed set of short atomic fields ... each is a string that compares exactly" — so the implementation contradicts its own stated contract, and this is the skill's self-described "highest-value rule".
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: The whole-file substring IS deliberate for one purpose, and there is a good test pinning that purpose: `test_a_term_the_master_mentions_only_in_a_bullet_is_sourced` (PyTorch appears in a master bullet, surfacing it into Skills is honest reframing). But that case needs whole-file scope, not sub-token matching — a word-boundary match satisfies it identically. No test in test_check_claims.py uses a term that is a proper substring of a master word, so the extra looseness is untested in both directions: nothing proves it is needed, and nothing catches what it lets through. Downstream, check_apply only reads the receipt verdict, which is "pass".
findings.reproduction:
$ D=.../scratchpad/audit/dead-gates/substr
$ cat $D/profile.yaml
summary: "Research engineer working on JavaScript tooling and image reconstruction."
skills: {languages: [JavaScript, Python]}
education: [{degree: MSc Computer Science}]
$ python3 scripts/check_claims.py --workspace $D/ws --record --master $D/profile.yaml
$ cat $D/ws/tailored-profile.yaml
skills: {languages: [Java, "C"], cloud: [Ruby]}
education: [{degree: PhD}]
certifications: ["MSc"]
$ python3 scripts/check_claims.py --workspace $D/ws
UNSOURCED: "Ruby" ...
UNSOURCED: "PhD" ...
exit=1
# Java (fabricated, sourced by "JavaScript") and the certification "MSc"
# (sourced by the DEGREE "MSc Computer Science") pass silently.
findings.fix: scripts/check_claims.py: replace `key in master_text` with a token-boundary containment test. Build the master side once as a token sequence (`master_tokens = normalize_term(master.read_text()).split()`) and accept a claim only when its normalized token list appears as a contiguous SUBLIST of `master_tokens`. That keeps the PyTorch-in-a-bullet case green (it is a whole token in the master) and rejects Java/JavaScript and MSc/MSc-Computer-Science. Add two tests: the Java-vs-JavaScript firing case, and the PyTorch quiet case (already present) re-run against the new matcher. Also fix the docstring, or make it true.

findings.title: 20 of 174 finding branches can be deleted with the suite green — including both master-profile-integrity branches and five of check_conventions' CI findings
findings.what_is_wrong: Branch-kill mutation (replace the `findings.append(...)` statement with `pass`) leaves 793/793 green for these 20: check_apply.py:134 INCOMPLETE_STOP (the no-reason half; only the no-evidence half at :136 is driven); check_assessment.py:188 ROW_UNSOURCED (the no_evidence-carries-refs half), :230 BAD_VERDICT, :298 CONVENTION_TABLE_MISSING; check_claims.py:100 and :107 BAD_CLAIM_ROW, **:167 MASTER_MUTATED (master profile deleted)**, **:179 MASTER_TOUCHED**; check_conventions.py:118 and :134 MISSING_FIELD, :148 BAD_MARKET, :156 BAD_ID, :193 BAD_DATE — five findings of the script `make check` runs as the CI lint; check_evidence_refs.py:80 DROPPED_REF (stated_conditions half); check_letter.py:88 COMPANY_MISMATCH (no recipient.company half); check_mock.py:299 QUESTION_LOG_UNPARSEABLE; check_pages.py:109 UNREADABLE_PDF (the LETTER half — the CV half at :96 is driven, which is the exact asymmetry that produced the render_letter regression); check_shortlist.py:103 NO_SOURCE_ID, :137 BAD_ROW, :244 SOURCE_REPORT_CONTRADICTS_JOURNAL (the no-matching-adapter_call half; only the classification half at :251 is driven). I verified by hand that these are reachable, not impossible — so they are untested, not dead. Separately, `check_conventions.check_file` raises an uncaught `ValueError: month must be in 1..12` on `review_by: 2026-13-45`: `_ISO_DATE` accepts it (`^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$`) and line 195 hands it straight to `datetime.date.fromisoformat`, aborting the table loop and discarding every finding already collected, instead of emitting BAD_DATE.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: Nothing is supposed to — this is the gap between "a code exists" and "a code has ever executed". Several tests assert the CODE generically (`assert "INCOMPLETE_STOP" in out`, `assert "SOURCE_REPORT_CONTRADICTS_JOURNAL" in codes(...)`) while their fixture only drives one of the two branches that emit it, so the sibling branch inherits a pass. Five of the twenty live in the script CI runs on every push, where an unexercised branch is exactly the one that will be wrong when a maintainer edits a market table. The date crash exits 1, which the script's own docstring reserves for "a table is bad" and distinguishes from 2 = "could not run" — so a could-not-run is reported with the wrong exit code and a traceback instead of a finding.

findings.title: Four checks can be made to fire on every input without any test noticing
findings.what_is_wrong: Forcing each finding's guard to `True` (so the check fires unconditionally) kills 167 of 171 mutants — the quiet-case discipline in this repo is genuinely strong. The four that survive have no test pinning that they stay silent on good input: check_assessment.py:226 REFUSAL_WITH_VERDICT (a non-refusal assessment carrying a verdict marker must NOT be reported), check_evidence_refs.py:80 DROPPED_REF (a stated_condition whose ref resolves), check_mock.py:504 CLAIMS_UNPARSEABLE, check_word_limits.py:73 NO_CRITERIA.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: A cry-wolf regression is invisible to a test suite that only ever feeds these four the input that should fire — and by the repo's own stated rule ("a check that cries wolf gets ignored"), the quiet case must be pinned as hard as the firing case. REFUSAL_WITH_VERDICT is the one worth caring about: it is scoped by `if refusing:` around an inner loop, so a future edit that flattens that guard would report every ordinary assessment as a refusal-with-verdict and no test would go red.

verdicts.verdict:
## VERDICT: STANDS (critical)

I tried to refute it and could not. The reproduction is exact — with only `--record` receipts for `check_claims` and `check_render_freshness` (`recorded`) plus the three forged `pass` receipts the repo's own fixture uses, `check_apply.py` exits 0 while `check_claims` run for real prints three `UNSOURCED:` findings and exits 1; a subsequent `--record` after a genuine fail restores exit 0. Patching `PASSING_VERDICTS = ("pass",)` on a copy left **793 passed, 4 deselected**, so nothing pins the token in either direction. It is not a recorded limit: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-09-1-migration-and-p0-fixes.md:30` documents the *decision* ("`recorded` is for a run that reports or records rather than gates (`check_render_freshness --record`, `check_claims --record`)") without noticing that those two scripts **both** record and gate — and the spec at `docs/…/2026-08-09-job-hunt-skill-design.md:242` states the guarantee this breaks verbatim: `tailored-profile.yaml 里每个不在 profile.yaml 中的词条都能在 claims.yaml 找到；渲染哈希新鲜`. Severity is not inflated: it is reachable through the documented resume path (`SKILL.md:315` / `modes/apply.md:12` → re-entry re-runs the `--record`), the two commands at `modes/apply.md:202` and `:212` are visually identical, and the self-check at `SKILL.md:686` lists `check_claims` with no record-vs-verify note at all.

Verified the one-line half of the fix end-to-end: patched `check_apply` gives `UPSTREAM_FAILED: check_claims` / `check_render_freshness` exit 1 on the bypass workspace, and exit 0 on an honest workspace that ran record→verify for both. Only `check_claims` and `check_render_freshness` ever write `"recorded"`, and only on the setup path; `check_assessment`'s `UPSTREAM_GATES` (`evidence_blocks, count_coverage, consistency, check_evidence_refs, lint_no_prediction`) is disjoint, so leaving its tuple alone is correct.

**What the finding got wrong about the fix**
- Part (b), renaming to `"baseline_recorded"`, is not free. It breaks two tests that pin the string — `scripts/tests/test_check_claims.py:162` and `scripts/tests/test_check_render_freshness.py:85` (`assert verdicts == ["recorded", "pass", …]`); reproduced as **792 passed, 1 failed**. It also introduces a fifth receipt verdict outside the closed set declared in `scripts/journal.py:77`, plan 1 line 30 and plan 2 line 75, which reads as a failure to `check_assessment.PASSING_VERDICTS`. Doable, but it is a 3-file + 2-doc change, not a 2-line one; part (a) alone already closes the hole.
- The one-liner's message is itself misleading: `UPSTREAM_FAILED: check_claims verdict=recorded (no findings recorded)` tells the reader the gate *failed* when it was merely never verified. It needs its own code (`NOT_VERIFIED: check_claims — only the --record setup receipt exists`), or the fix trades a silent pass for a wrong diagnosis.
- The belt-and-braces `inputs` check works for `check_claims` (record writes `{"profile.yaml": …}`, verify writes `{"tailored-profile.yaml": …}` — confirmed in a journal dump) but would **not** work for `check_render_freshness`: its record and verify receipts both carry the same rel→hash dict (`['cv.md']` in both). The verdict string is the only discriminator there, so that gate has no second line of defence.

**Disclosure:** a `cd` into my scratchpad copy failed mid-command (a parallel agent had deleted the shared path), so one `sed` landed on the real `/Users/donghanglyu/code_project/job-hunt/scripts/check_render_freshness.py:65`. I reverted it with Edit immediately; `git status --short` now shows only the pre-existing untracked `docs/superpowers/research/2026-08-16-audit-findings.json`, and `pytest scripts/tests/test_check_render_freshness.py -q` → 8 passed. No git write commands were run.

finding.title: The test that promises SKILL.md and modes/*.md shared paragraphs are byte-identical asserts only that the intersection is non-empty — drift makes it easier to pass, never harder
finding.what_is_wrong: `scripts/tests/test_skill_structure.py:264` `test_the_paragraphs_layer_1_shares_with_a_mode_file_are_byte_identical` computes `shared = set(skill) & set(_paragraphs(mode_file))` and asserts `shared or mode_file.name != "apply.md"`. The intersection of two sets of strings is byte-identical BY CONSTRUCTION. A paragraph that has drifted simply drops out of the intersection — it is invisible to the assertion, and every drop makes the set smaller, i.e. moves toward the only condition the test checks (non-empty). The 40-line comment block above it (lines 235-246) states the exact regression it is guarding: "SKILL.md said 不是对面试或录用概率的预测 while check_assessment.py looks for the literal 不是对结果的预判 ... verdicts.verdict:
**VERDICT: STANDS-WITH-LOWER-SEVERITY (medium, not high)**

The reproduction is exact. On a copy, the finding's 15-paragraph drift gives `56 passed` / `793 passed, 4 deselected`; I also ran a *realistic* drift (`repo3`: SKILL.md alone reworded to "**Three independent judges** must **a majority** return `PASS`" and "If two or more are `REJECT`, the round is a `REJECT`", while `modes/apply.md` still says all-three/any) and got `793 passed`, `LOSSLESS: 1317/1317 baseline lines accounted for across 31 files, 20 waived`, and `check_conventions.py --ci` exit 0 — i.e. all of `make check` green on a layer 1 that contradicts layer 1.5 on the judge loop. Both files are in context simultaneously (`SKILL.md:383` "then read `modes/<mode>.md` in full"), so the contradiction is live in a real run, and nothing else in the tree compares the two files.

Severity is inflated, though, because the duplication is not unguarded: 8 of the 16 shared paragraphs contain a `required_inline.json` anchor enforced by `test_every_layer1_rule_is_inline_in_skill_md` (including the literal "Combined verdict: PASS only if ALL THREE judges return"), the disclaimer regression the comment cites now has its own dedicated test (`test_a_literally_matched_gate_string_appears_verbatim_in_layer_1`), and `parse_verdicts.py` mechanically ANDs the three judges no matter what the prose says. The genuinely unbacked residue is the prose-only half — the workspace path template, "paste the **full text** of `agents/ats-screener.md`", the profile check/save steps, the final-message contents. Not already-recorded: the header comment's "an exact-match scan only sees the pairs that have not drifted yet" is offered as the *motivation* for the new tests, and commit 9809599 claims "Four tests now hold the line: shared paragraphs must be identical" — the limitation was described and then rebuilt into the guard (the same message says "All **three** failure modes mutation-tested", i.e. this fourth test likely never was).

**What the finding got wrong about the fix:** the proposed fix does not work, and it fails its own stated acceptance test. I implemented it verbatim (`/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-donghanglyu/d1ca171b-6798-42dc-9582-87e4635be401/scratchpad/audit/refute/proposed_fix.py`: casefold + collapse whitespace + strip `*_\`~` → key, then assert raw equality on shared keys) and it prints `GREEN (0 drifted pairs reported)` on the pristine tree, on the 15-paragraph drift, *and* on the semantic "majority" drift — because any drift worth catching changes the normalized key too, so the pair still vanishes. Normalized-equality pairing detects only formatting drift, the one class that doesn't matter; the motivating regression (不是对面试或录用概率的预测 vs 不是对结果的预判) would also sail through it. Real near-match needs fuzzy similarity, and that has its own cost: `difflib` ratio ≥ 0.80 goes **red on the clean tree today** with 3 legitimate near-pairs (layer 1 shows `--workspace <ws> --mode <mode>`, each mode file shows its concrete `--mode assess|discover|interview`), so it needs a waiver file or a placeholder-aware normalizer or it will be tuned into uselessness. The cheap fix the finding missed: pin the shared count instead of its non-emptiness — 16 today, 1 under their drift, 14 under mine — which goes red on both drift and deletion, is deterministic, and needs no threshold.

verdicts.verdict:
## VERDICT: STANDS-WITH-LOWER-SEVERITY (high → medium)

The reproduction is exact. On a copy at `9809599` with the four heading pairs renamed in `modes/assess.md` (`## 硬性阻断项`×3, `## Hard blockers`, `## 那该怎么办`, `## What to do instead`): `793 passed, 4 deselected`, `LOSSLESS: 1317/1317 baseline lines accounted for across 31 files, 20 waived`, `check_conventions.py --ci exit=0`, and `bash scripts/tests/check_assess_anchors.sh` → `all anchors present / exit=0` from inside the gutted tree; re-pointing its `cd` at the mutated tree raises `AssertionError: 硬性阻断项`, so the needle list is sound and only the hardcoded path plus the absent runner neuter it. `grep -rn check_assess_anchors` hits only the plans and `.git/index`; `Makefile:23` runs `test lossless conventions` and `checks.yml` runs the same three.

Severity drops because the harm the finding actually describes is a **loud** failure, not this repo's signature silent pass. I built the drifted card and ran the real gate (`/private/tmp/.../scratchpad/audit/refute-anchors/runtime.py`): in-step → `(no findings)`; drifted → `NO_DISQUALIFIER_SECTION: … there is no '## 硬性阻断项' / '## Hard blockers' section` + `NO_STRATEGY_SECTION: … no strategy from ('apply_anyway', …)`. The message names the exact spellings it wants, so drift costs one recoverable iteration. Nothing has drifted today, and plan Task 12's "Enforced by" table (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-09-2-assess-mode.md:4170-4177`) deliberately assigns those heading/column/banner literals to the *runtime* findings — it names the anchor script as enforcer for exactly one row, the twelve-name field list, which is a different finding. The `.sh` header and plan Step 2 (line 4532) record it as a one-shot TDD red/green copy-paste command, and its `cd /Users/donghanglyu/code_project/job-hunt` is the plans' universal convention (194 occurrences across four plan files) — so (e) is by-design for what the file *was*, and the defect is that it was committed into `scripts/tests/` where it looks like a test.

### What the finding got wrong about the fix

1. **It names the wrong needles as the harm, and thereby argues its own severity down.** The genuine pass-while-wrong is the one it omits: an **English card carrying the Chinese headings** — what a mode file that lost `Hard blockers` / `What to do instead` / `Acceptance criterion` would teach — passes the gate with `(no findings)` (`runtime2.py`, case C). Same class: `STALE_BANNER` (cannot fire before the first `review_by`, `2026-11-09`) and `insufficient_evidence` / `how_to_close`, which no gate keys on. Those, not `NO_DISQUALIFIER_SECTION`, are what the new test earns its keep on.
2. **"Generate the needles FROM the module rather than re-typing them" would re-create the bug `9809599` fixed** for the disclaimer specifically: importing `DISCLAIMER_ANCHORS` means an edit that changes the constant and the mode file the same wrong way still passes — that commit's whole point was that the test *pinned* the paraphrase. Hardcode the two disclaimer literals the way `test_skill_structure.py:279-288` already does; import is fine for `STRATEGIES` / `STRATEGY_HEADINGS` / `DISQUALIFIER_HEADINGS` / `ACCEPTANCE_COLUMNS` / `STALE_BANNER`, where mode file and gate need only agree.
3. **The last sentence of the fix is already done.** `scripts/tests/test_discover_mode_doc.py:11,50,182` imports `check_shortlist`, iterates `cs.DISCLOSURE_LABELS`, and asserts `cs.PROVISIONAL_STAMP` against `modes/discover.md`.
4. Deleting the `.sh` must also amend `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-09-2-assess-mode.md:4174`, or the plan keeps naming a deleted file as an enforcer under a preamble that says "a claim here that no gate makes true is visible as a blank".

finding.title: The self-check guards test only that a filename appears somewhere between `## Self-check` and EOF, so a read-when trigger line can be deleted with the suite green
finding.what_is_wrong: `test_skill_structure.py::_self_check_section()` matches `^## Self-check.*?(?=^## |\Z)`. `## Self-check` is the LAST heading in SKILL.md (line 651 of 741), so the "section" is everything to end of file. `test_the_self_check_names_every_reference_file` / `_agent_file` / `_mode_file` / `_script` then assert only `f"references/{f.name}" in section` — a bare substring, with no requirement that the mention be a `- [ ]` checklist item or a read-trigger at all. So the checklist line that tells the model to read a layer-2 file can be removed outright, provided the filename survives anywhere in the last 90 lines — including in prose, an HTML comment's neighbouring sentence, or a future appended block. This is the same section-boundary defect the project already found once ("a block appended after '## Self-check' was swallowed by that section's regex"); the swallowing is now permanent because the section runs to EOF.
finding.why_nothing_reports_it: The guard IS the reporter, and it passes: the name is still in the string it searches. `test_every_path_the_self_check_names_exists` checks the other direction (named paths exist) and also passes. check_skill_lossless.py cannot see it — `references/cv-craft.md` is new content, not a baseline line, and the file itself is untouched, so it still reports 1317/1317. The layer-2 file then simply never gets read at runtime, which is the silent-omission failure the self-check exists to prevent.

verdicts.verdict:
## VERDICT: STANDS

**It reproduces byte-for-byte, and the realistic variant is worse than the one filed.** Running the given mutation on a copy (`/private/tmp/.../audit/refute-lens-x9/mutant`): `793 passed, 4 deselected`, `LOSSLESS: 1317/1317 baseline lines accounted for across 31 files, 20 waived`, `conventions exit=0`. I also built the vector this repo has actually already hit — a new layer-2 file registered only in an appended `###` block (`/private/tmp/.../audit/refute-lens-x9/plan5`: `references/salary-negotiation.md` + a prose block after `## Self-check`) — and got `793 passed`, with `salary-negotiation swallowed? True / is it on a checklist line? False`. That is precisely the accident commit `54b20fc` describes ("passing for discovery-sources.md and source-policy.md BY ACCIDENT — their names sit in the block's trigger paragraphs"); that commit fixed the *position* of one block and never installed a guard against recurrence, and `cross.md:327` tells every future plan to append to this exact section, so the escape hatch sits directly on the live path.

**Not recorded as an accepted limit.** The only prose acknowledging the behaviour is `reaudit-3.md:83` ("they search the whole section"), used there to argue an unrelated fix was safe — an observation, not a decision. `54b20fc`'s message asserts Self-check "is meant to be last" but no test pins that, and no ANCHOR in `test_skill_structure.py` pins any read-when trigger line.

### What the finding got wrong about the fix
1. **The fix as literally written breaks the correct repo.** "Parse the section into the lines matching `^\s*- \[ \] `, join those" drops wrapped continuation lines. Run against the *unmutated* repo it reports 17 false missing entries — `references/interview-shapes.md`, all five `references/market-conventions/*.yaml`, `agents/hiring-manager.md`, `scripts/render_rirekisho.py`, `scripts/check_assessment.py` and 9 more — because those names live on indented continuation lines, not on the `- [ ]` line itself.
2. **The corrected form works and is clean.** An item parser (a `- [ ]` line plus its following indented lines, joined) gives `pristine: items=42 missing=[]`, `mutant: missing=['references/cv-craft.md']`, `plan5: missing=['references/salary-negotiation.md']` — green where it should be green, red on both mutations.
3. **Keep the boundary assertion anyway, but for a different reason than stated.** With an item parser the EOF boundary stops mattering for prose, but an appended block containing its own `- [ ]` lines would still hand out free passes — so "assert `## Self-check` is SKILL.md's last heading" is still worth having, as the invariant `54b20fc` stated in a commit message and never encoded. The sentinel-comment alternative is strictly worse: a sentinel can be moved without any test noticing.
4. Minor: the reproduction's compensated mutation understates the guard slightly — deleting line 662 *alone* does go red (`FAILED test_the_self_check_names_every_reference_file`, 1 failed / 55 passed). The defect needs the name to survive in the tail; the plan5 case is the one that gets there without anyone intending it.

finding.title: check_claims sources a tailored term by raw substring over the whole master file, so a fabricated skill is "sourced" by any longer word that contains it
finding.what_is_wrong: `scripts/check_claims.py:193` — `if len(key) < 2 or key in master_text: continue`, where `master_text` is the ENTIRE profile.yaml NFKC-folded, lowercased, punctuation-squashed into one string. The test is a raw substring, not a token match, so any fabricated atomic term that happens to be a substring of any word anywhere in the master is silently accepted. `Java` is sourced by `JavaScript`. A fabricated certification `MSc` is sourced by the degree `MSc Computer Science`. The module docstring says the opposite — "a closed set of short atomic fields ... each is a string that compares exactly" — so the implementation contradicts its own stated contract, and this is the skill's self-described "highest-value rule".
finding.why_nothing_reports_it: The whole-file substring IS deliberate for one purpose, and there is a good test pinning that purpose: `test_a_term_the_master_mentions_only_in_a_bullet_is_sourced` (PyTorch appears in a master bullet, surfacing it into Skills is honest reframing). But that case needs whole-file scope, not sub-token matching — a word-boundary match satisfies it identically. No test in test_check_claims.py uses a term that is a proper substring of a master word, so the extra looseness is untested in both directions: nothing proves it is needed, and nothing catches what it lets through. Downstream, check_apply only reads the receipt verdict, which is "pass".
finding.reproduction:
$ D=.../scratchpad/audit/dead-gates/substr
$ cat $D/profile.yaml
summary: "Research engineer working on JavaScript tooling and image reconstruction."
skills: {languages: [JavaScript, Python]}
education: [{degree: MSc Computer Science}]
$ python3 scripts/check_claims.py --workspace $D/ws --record --master $D/profile.yaml
$ cat $D/ws/tailored-profile.yaml
skills: {languages: [Java, "C"], cloud: [Ruby]}
education: [{degree: PhD}]
certifications: ["MSc"]
$ python3 scripts/check_claims.py --workspace $D/ws
UNSOURCED: "Ruby" ...
UNSOURCED: "PhD" ...
exit=1
# Java (fabricated, sourced by "JavaScript") and the certification "MSc"
# (sourced by the DEGREE "MSc Computer Science") pass silently.
finding.fix: scripts/check_claims.py: replace `key in master_text` with a token-boundary containment test. Build the master side once as a token sequence (`master_tokens = normalize_term(master.read_text()).split()`) and accept a claim only when its normalized token list appears as a contiguous SUBLIST of `master_tokens`. That keeps the PyTorch-in-a-bullet case green (it is a whole token in the master) and rejects Java/JavaScript and MSc/MSc-Computer-Science. Add two tests: the Java-vs-JavaScript firing case, and the PyTorch quiet case (already present) re-run against the new matcher. Also fix the docstring, or make it true.

verdicts.verdict:
**VERDICT: STANDS** (severity high is correct — arguably understated)

The reproduction ran verbatim and matched exactly (`Ruby`/`PhD` fire, `Java`/`MSc` pass, exit=1). I could not find any recorded limit: the plan's own rationale at `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-09-1-migration-and-p0-fixes.md:2711` says the closed set is used precisely *because* "each is a string that can be compared **exactly**", which agrees with the docstring and contradicts the code — so this is drift, not a documented trade-off. The path is reachable in every real apply run and nothing downstream re-checks it; `check_apply` reads only the receipt verdict.

It matters more than the finding claims, and the finding gets two things wrong.

**1. The leak is not limited to contrived fixtures — the shipped template triggers it.** `master_text` is the whole *raw file*, including YAML comments and schema documentation, so the candidate's own data is not what sources the claim. Against `assets/profile.example.yaml` unmodified (the canonical schema `modes/apply.md:16` points every user at), with no fabrication-friendly editing:

```
'PhD': SOURCED by ...'sensible default a current phd/researcher or a c'
'AI' : SOURCED by ...'ept meta.name and contact.email. meta name jane '
'GAN': SOURCED by ...'ence roles you held at an organisation employer l'
'Go' : SOURCED by ...'riendly label e.g. linkedin google scholar # hyp'
```

A fabricated **`PhD` degree** — one of the four named fabrication classes — passes silently, sourced by a comment explaining section-ordering defaults. The finding's own repro had `PhD` firing; against the real template it does not. `AI` is sourced by the word `email`, which is a *required* field, so on any profile in this schema `AI` is permanently unsourceable-in-principle.

**2. The proposed fix is right in direction but wrong as written — it would cry wolf on honest reframing.** `_PUNCT` (`check_claims.py:50`) deliberately preserves `. - / + #`, so a naive `master_tokens = normalize_term(...).split()` sublist test glues terminal punctuation into the token. It passes all 11 existing tests, then breaks three realistic honest cases:

| master bullet | shipped | proposed fix |
|---|---|---|
| `Rebuilt the recon pipeline in PyTorch.` | quiet | **CRIES WOLF** (`pytorch.`) |
| `Shipped a PyTorch-based recon pipeline.` | quiet | **CRIES WOLF** (`pytorch-based`) |
| `Wrote kernels in C++/CUDA.` → `CUDA` | quiet | **CRIES WOLF** (`c++/cuda.`) |

The existing `test_a_term_the_master_mentions_only_in_a_bullet_is_sourced` stays green only because its bullet happens to put `PyTorch` mid-sentence — the test pins a lucky arrangement, exactly the pattern this project is auditing for. The fix must match on a boundary that treats preserved punctuation as a *separator* on the master side while keeping it *inside* the claim token (so `C++` and `CI/CD` still compare intact) — e.g. regex `(?<![\w+#/.-])<escaped-key>(?![\w+#-])`, or strip trailing `.`/`-`/`/` from master tokens before the sublist test. Whichever is chosen, the three rows above belong in the test file alongside the Java-vs-JavaScript firing case, or the fix trades a silent miss for a gate people learn to skip.

findings.title: modes/assess.md defines only the `requirements` rows, not the top-level fit-assessment.yaml schema three scripts read — so the coverage card prints invented facts and the work-authorization detector is dead code
findings.what_is_wrong:
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-09-2-assess-mode.md:101 carries "The `fit-assessment.yaml` schema (authoritative copy — Task 12 writes this into `modes/assess.md`)" and lists `market`, `verdict`, `provisional`, `effort`, `level_direction`, `declared_work_status`, `stated_conditions`, `requirements`, `actions`. Only the `requirements` sub-block reached modes/assess.md (§6, "This schema is defined here and nowhere else"). The other keys are read by shipped code with no definition anywhere in layer 1 or layer 1.5:

(a) count_coverage.render_block reads `assessment.get("level_direction", "unclear")` and `assessment.get("effort", "not_closable")` — TOP-LEVEL keys. The strings `level_direction` and a top-level `effort:` appear in zero of SKILL.md, modes/, references/, agents/. A run that follows modes/assess.md exactly therefore ships a card telling the user `effort to close the gaps: not_closable` / 「可补缺口所需投入：补不上」 — a maximally pessimistic verdict on their whole situation — as an assessed fact, when nothing assessed it.

(b) consistency.py's `overall_authorization_alignment` reads `stated_conditions` and `declared_work_status`. Both appear ZERO times in the entire skill tree outside scripts/ and docs/. So NOTICE_WORK_AUTH_CONFLICT and NOTICE_WORK_AUTH_VERIFY — advertised in SKILL.md's Gates table ("work-authorization conflicts") and the only checks that catch "this job is legally impossible for you" — can never fire in a run that follows the mode file. modes/assess.md §4 tells the model to ask the user about work authorization but names no field to record the answer in.

(c) The two readers of `effort` disagree about a missing value: count_coverage defaults it to `not_closable` and prints that, while consistency.verdict_effort_conflict does `assessment.get("effort")` with no default and sees None. So the card can say `apply verdict: strong_apply` and `effort to close the gaps: not_closable` in the same fenced block — the exact contradiction NOTICE_VERDICT_EFFORT exists to catch — and consistency.py prints nothing.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: check_assessment's COUNT_MISMATCH compares fit-assessment.md against `coverage.render_block(...)` — the same function, with the same defaults, on both sides. Its NOTICE_NOT_ATTACHED loop iterates `consistency.notices(assessment)`, which returns [] when the fields are absent, so "no notice fired" and "the notice could not fire" are the same silence. And the field names are absent from the mode file, so a model following layer 1.5 verbatim never writes them — the input that would wake the checks up is one the instructions never ask for. check_assess_anchors.sh (see the next finding) does not list these keys either, and no pytest reads the real modes/assess.md at all.

findings.what_is_wrong: SKILL.md:684 heads a ten-item list with "Ran, with a receipt in `journal.jsonl` — `scripts/check_apply.py` requires each of these:". check_apply.REQUIRED_GATES is `(check_personal_data, check_claims, check_render_freshness, parse_verdicts, lint_cv)`, plus `check_letter` only when letter.yaml exists. `check_pages`, `check_word_limits` and `check_mock` are listed under that heading and are not required in any branch — check_apply never looks at cv.pdf, never reads posting.yaml, and never mentions check_mock. The claim is falsified by SKILL.md's own next paragraph: "Every line above says what evidence it leaves, and the headings differ for a reason: a checklist that promises a receipt where none can exist teaches its reader that one of its lines is decorative, and the reader cannot tell which one." Three of the ten lines are decorative, and the file has just told the reader they are not.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: test_skill_structure.py's self-check tests are all presence tests — test_the_self_check_names_every_script asserts every script name appears somewhere in the section, and test_every_path_the_self_check_names_exists asserts the paths resolve. Neither compares the bullets under a heading against the tuple the heading claims for them, and no test imports check_apply.REQUIRED_GATES at all. So the checklist and the gate can say different things forever. The failure mode this creates is the paper one the repo is built against: a model that trusts the heading assumes check_apply's exit 0 covered the PDF page count, the word limits and the mock round, stops looking, and reports a package as gated when three of its gates never ran.

verdicts.verdict:
## VERDICT: STANDS — critical, with claim (b) overstated and the proposed fix broken in two ways

**It reproduces, all three parts, unmodified.** A faithful assess run whose `fit-assessment.yaml` contains only keys `modes/assess.md` names ships this card with all five gates at exit 0:

```
must-haves strongly evidenced:   3 of 3   (partial 0, gap 0, no evidence 0)
core responsibilities demonstrated: 1 of 2
level match:                     unclear
effort to close the gaps:        not_closable
apply verdict:                   strong_apply
```

`count_coverage exit=0 / consistency exit=0 / check_evidence_refs exit=0 / lint_no_prediction exit=0 / check_assessment exit=0`. The only row with a real gap (R5) carries per-row `effort: evening` with a `how_to_close`, so `not_closable` is not merely undefined — it is contradicted by the file it was printed from. The asymmetry is exactly as described: `count_coverage sees effort = 'not_closable'` / `consistency sees effort = None` / `verdict_effort_conflict = False` / `notices() = []`. And `grep -rn "stated_conditions\|declared_work_status\|level_direction" SKILL.md modes/ references/ agents/` → `exit=1`.

**Not a recorded limit — the opposite.** Nothing in the spec, the allowlist, or any docstring justifies the defaults; the plan states the contrary principle at `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-09-2-assess-mode.md:1926` — *"Substituting a value instead of dropping the row would put a claim we invented into the model's mouth: `no_evidence` is a finding about the CV, not a default."* One thing the finding gets factually wrong about provenance: `modes/assess.md` is **byte-identical to Task 12 Step 1's embedded content** (`diff` clean), so this is not implementation drift — the plan contradicts itself between line 101 and line 4187, and the executor followed the literal block. That makes it more likely to recur, not less.

**Claim (b) is materially overstated and I'd carve it out.** "The only checks that catch 'this job is legally impossible for you'" is false. §4's disqualifier machinery is the primary path and it is a live hard gate — on the Philips no-sponsorship posting with R6 as `screening: knockout, match: no_evidence`, omitting the section gives `NO_DISQUALIFIER_SECTION: 1 knockout requirement(s) are not met... / check_assessment exit=1`. Plus `nl-recognised-sponsor-gate` in the NL convention table fires on `applies_when` and tells the reader to check the IND register. The two notices are dead (confirmed: adding the two keys to that same workspace produces `NOTICE_WORK_AUTH_CONFLICT` and `NOTICE_NOT_ATTACHED ... exit=1`), but they are a redundant code-side cross-check on a fact the model must already row-ify, not the last line of defence. Severity survives on (a)+(c) alone.

### What the finding got wrong about the fix

1. **It breaks the §8 refusal floor.** I applied the fix verbatim to a copy. A legitimate "posting was a sign-in wall" run — `verdict: insufficient_evidence`, `requirements: []`, no coverage block, exactly what §8 mandates — goes from `exit=0` on pristine to:
   `UPSTREAM_FAILED: count_coverage verdict=fail (MISSING_EFFORT...; MISSING_LEVEL_DIRECTION...) / exit=1`.
   Because `check_assessment.py:208-209` does `findings += counts["invalid"]` **before** computing `refusing`, the new findings are unreachable-by-design on the one path where `effort` and `level_direction` are meaningless. The check must be scoped to `verdict != vocab.REFUSAL`.
2. **"Drop the fallbacks in `render_block`" misses half of them.** There are four, not two: `LEVEL_DIRECTION_ZH.get(direction, '不明')` and `EFFORT_ZH.get(effort, '补不上')` are separate. Patched as written, the **default** `--lang zh` card still prints `职级匹配：不明 / 可补缺口所需投入：补不上` — I reproduced this. It only fails loudly because `counts["invalid"]` is non-empty; the printed lie is untouched.
3. **"Align `consistency.py` to read `effort` the same way" points the wrong direction.** `consistency.py`'s bare `.get("effort")` is the correct read; `count_coverage` is the deviant. Giving consistency the `not_closable` default would make `NOTICE_VERDICT_EFFORT` cry wolf on every file missing the key.
4. Minor: `coverage(rows)` has no access to the assessment, so the fix needs a signature change threaded through `check_assessment.py:208` and ~13 test call sites (`test_count_coverage.py::test_only_strong_counts_as_strong` fails under the patch), and the plan pins `coverage(rows) -> dict` at lines 1917/4588.
5. One addition the fix should make first: `level_direction`'s value set exists only as the keys of `LEVEL_DIRECTION_ZH` **inside `count_coverage.py`** (`vocab.py` has no `LEVEL_DIRECTION`), and `declared_work_status`'s five values and `stance` exist in no code at all. Writing them straight into `modes/assess.md` creates the second spelling `vocab.py`'s docstring exists to prevent — add them to `vocab.py` first, then have the mode file name them.

Corroborating dead-backstop facts: `make check` = `test lossless conventions`; `grep -rn check_assess_anchors Makefile scripts/` returns nothing, so `scripts/tests/check_assess_anchors.sh` never runs, and no pytest reads the real `modes/assess.md` (`test_check_assessment.py:98` writes a synthetic one).

# VERDICT: STANDS-WITH-LOWER-SEVERITY (high → low)

Every factual claim reproduces exactly. `grep -rn "check_assess_anchors" . --include="*.py" --include="*.yml" --include="Makefile" --include="*.sh"` returns nothing; a copy at `/private/tmp/.../audit/refute-assess-anchor/repo` with the disclaimer paraphrased back to `不是对面试或录用概率的预测`, `salary_range`/`application_type` deleted from §3, and `Hard blockers`/`Acceptance criterion` renamed gave `2 failed, 795 passed` — byte-identical to the untouched control copy (`/private/tmp/.../control`, same 2 `test_install` failures, a copying artifact) — plus `LOSSLESS: 1317/1317 … exit=0`, `check_conventions --ci exit=0`, and `bash scripts/tests/check_assess_anchors.sh` → `all anchors present / exit=0` from inside the gutted tree. So yes: `modes/assess.md` has no CI guard, and the `cd /Users/donghanglyu/code_project/job-hunt` on line 4 does produce a false green for anyone who runs it from a clone.

But the severity is inflated, because this is not a pass-while-wrong defect — it is a missing regression test whose failure mode is loud. I checked all 18 literals `check_assessment.py` greps for against the real mode file: **all present today** (`apply verdict:` and `likely_screen_out` are the only absentees, and neither is hand-written by the model — the first comes out of `count_coverage.render_block`, the second is read from `fit-assessment.yaml`). The four with the worst consequence — `DISCLAIMER_ANCHORS` and `VERDICT_MARKERS`, both spellings — are **already pinned in SKILL.md** by `test_a_literally_matched_gate_string_appears_verbatim_in_layer_1` and `test_layer_1_shows_both_language_shapes_of_the_advice_block`, i.e. by the very commit 9809599 the finding says "did not pin" the anchor; and `salary_range`/`application_type` are pinned in SKILL.md via `required_inline.json`. Since layer 1 loads on every assess trigger, drift in the mode file does not remove the correct spelling from the model's context. For the 14 literals that genuinely live only in `modes/assess.md`, I ran the gate on a workspace where a model faithfully copied drifted spellings (`/private/tmp/.../refute-assess-anchor/drift_runtime.py`): every one fails red **and quotes both correct spellings back** —

```
[A-correct] findings=NONE
[B-heading-drifted] NO_DISQUALIFIER_SECTION: … no '## 硬性阻断项' / '## Hard blockers' section …
                    NO_STRATEGY_SECTION: … ('apply_anyway', 'reposition', 'skill_sprint', 'side_door',
                    'change_track') … under '## 那该怎么办' / '## What to do instead' …
[C-column-drifted] NO_ACCEPTANCE_COLUMN: … no '验收标准' / 'Acceptance criterion' column …
                   NO_ACCEPTANCE_COLUMN: … no '输出物' / 'Deliverable' column …
```

That is a self-repairing failure, the opposite of the 9809599 story the finding invokes (`NO_DISCLAIMER` is the one message that names no string — and the disclaimer is the case already pinned in layer 1). Note also this is a **duplicate**: the same defect, with the same fix, is already filed at `docs/superpowers/research/2026-08-16-audit-findings.json:31` under the dead-gates lens; the owner should not pay for it twice.

### What the finding got wrong about the fix

- **As specified, the new test is red on an untouched repo.** Four of the seven extra keys it says to add do not exist in `modes/assess.md` today: `level_direction`, `declared_work_status`, `stated_conditions`, `provisional` are all ABSENT (`effort`, `actions`, `market` are present). Whether the mode file *should* name those `consistency.py` fields is a separate content finding; bundling it into the anchor test means the test lands failing and gets weakened or deleted.
- **"Import the constants rather than retyping" must exclude two of them.** Iterating `VERDICT_MARKERS` fails on `apply verdict:` and `OTHER_HALF_VERDICTS` fails on `likely_screen_out`, neither of which the mode file needs. The six the finding actually names (`STRATEGIES`, `DISQUALIFIER_HEADINGS`, `STRATEGY_HEADINGS`, `ACCEPTANCE_COLUMNS`, `DISCLAIMER_ANCHORS`, `STALE_BANNER`) are all satisfied — that list is safe; the sibling finding's "iterate everything" version is not.
- **The strongest drift is one no anchor list catches.** `NO_DISQUALIFIER_SECTION` only fires when `fit-assessment.yaml` already marks a `knockout` row unmet; if a rewrite of §4's *prose* stopped the model asking about disqualifiers at all, the section is legitimately absent and nothing fires — grepping `硬性阻断项` would not have helped. Worth saying in the fix so the test is not mistaken for full coverage of the file.

verdicts.verdict:
## VERDICT: STANDS

Reproduced exactly, with my own workspace rather than the original auditor's script: five REQUIRED_GATES receipts + `cv.pdf` + `posting.yaml: application_type: structured` → `check_apply.py` exits 0, empty stdout/stderr, receipts `['check_apply','check_claims','check_personal_data','check_render_freshness','lint_cv','parse_verdicts']`, and `check_pages`/`check_word_limits`/`check_mock` absent. No exemption is recorded anywhere — I grepped the spec, all five plans, and the three scripts' docstrings; the only "does not require" note in SKILL.md is line 707 for the discover gates, which proves the author writes the exemption when they mean it. Nothing downstream catches the consequence, and the two scripts' own docstrings say so in as many words: `check_pages` — *"Nothing else in the pipeline measures the artifact that is actually submitted"*; `check_word_limits` — *"the one artifact that is actually marked had no reader at all."* `modes/apply.md` has zero `- [ ]` lines, so SKILL.md:684–694 is the only checklist these two appear on, and it is read at exactly the moment ("before reporting the package as done") where a false requiredness claim converts "I skipped it" into "check_apply covered it".

## What the finding got wrong

- **The "falsified by its own next paragraph" argument is wrong.** That paragraph is about whether a line *leaves a receipt* — and all ten do, including the three disputed ones (I ran `check_pages` and `check_word_limits` on the repro workspace; both wrote `could_not_run` receipts). The false statement is only the heading's em-dash clause. The real internal contradiction is line 707, which uses the same heading slot to say "`scripts/check_apply.py` does not require these" — same author, same construction, correct there and wrong at 684.
- **`check_mock` is over-scoped.** It does have a live backstop: `modes/interview.md:347` forbids reporting a round without quoting the `check_mock` receipt, and `:379` self-checks it, both in a file loaded unconditionally on entering interview mode. Listing it under an apply-gate heading is a factual error, not a silent-failure vector. `check_pages` and `check_word_limits` carry the whole severity; the finding would be stronger, not weaker, for saying so.
- **The code half of the fix has a condition mismatch that re-creates the same species of drift.** `check_pages` exits 2 with a `could_not_run` receipt when `tailored-profile.yaml` is missing, not just `cv.pdf` (`scripts/check_pages.py:135-140`), and `could_not_run` is not in `PASSING_VERDICTS`. Gating `check_apply` on `(ws/'cv.pdf').exists()` alone means check_apply's trigger condition is not check_pages' trigger condition. Gate on both inputs, or accept that a missing tailored profile now hard-fails apply.
- **Low breakage risk, and there is direct precedent for the "make it true" branch.** The 20 tests in `scripts/tests/test_check_apply.py` create neither `cv.pdf` nor `posting.yaml`, so a conditional widening breaks none of them; `scripts/tests/test_skill_structure.py` passes 56/56 today and never imports `REQUIRED_GATES`. And `docs/superpowers/research/2026-08-09/audit-1.md:38-39` found this identical drift for `parse_verdicts` — the repo fixed it by adding the gate to `REQUIRED_GATES`, not by rewording the checklist.

Downstream, the omission of `application_type` is silent by construction: check_word_limits computes `structured = posting.get("application_type") == "structured"`, so an absent key means False, which means NO_CRITERIA and NO_LIMIT_DECLARED cannot fire, which means the gate exits 0 on an unlabelled essay for a criterion-scored form. And check_apply does not require a check_word_limits receipt at all (finding 3), so nothing downstream notices either. Only `company` fails loudly, via check_letter's NO_COMPANY_IN_POSTING — and only if a letter was requested.

verdicts.verdict:
## VERDICT: STANDS-WITH-LOWER-SEVERITY (high → low)

The mechanics reproduce exactly — `check_word_limits.py` exits 0 on the nine-key posting and exits 1 with `NO_CRITERIA` the moment `application_type: structured` is appended, and the census prints `salary_range SKILL=3 assess=4 apply=0`. But three of the finding's load-bearing claims are wrong. **(a) "It is the copy that runs when apply is used standalone" is false**: `SKILL.md:383` says "then read `modes/<mode>.md` in full" — the mode file is read *after* layer 1, so SKILL.md's own twelve-name fence (`SKILL.md:222-228`), including the sentence naming this exact defect, is always in context; and `modes/apply.md:35` unconditionally orders `references/job-posting-extraction.md`, whose schema table carries `salary_range` and `application_type` (11 of 12), with `SKILL.md:664` naming that same file again in the layer-1 self-check. **(b) "It shipped again" is false**: `grep -n "Extract the structured object" ~/.claude/skills/job-application/SKILL.md` returns `71:` — `modes/apply.md:36` *is* baseline `SKILL.md:71`, the very line SKILL.md:228's warning is about, migrated byte-for-byte under the lossless discipline; plan 1:5689 and plan 2:89 both state the list deliberately lives in exactly two copies (SKILL.md + `modes/assess.md`), which makes "three copies" a design decision, not a regression. **(c) The harm chain is thinner than claimed**: `apply.md:37` — the very next bullet — spells the structured-detection rule out in full prose and routes to `structured-applications.md`, which mandates `### <Criterion>` headings; and with headings present, `OVER_LIMIT` and `EMPTY_CRITERION` fire *without* `application_type` (reproduced: exit=1 on a posting with zero `application_type` hits). Only `NO_CRITERIA` and `NO_LIMIT_DECLARED` go quiet, and `NO_CRITERIA` can only matter in a run that also ignored the adjacent bullet.

What survives is a real but low-severity doc inconsistency: layer 1.5 states a shorter list than layer 1's "exactly these twelve names in this order", and nothing tests it.

**What the finding got wrong about the fix — it breaks `make lossless`.** "Replace the inline nine-name sentence at `modes/apply.md:36`" deletes a tracked baseline line:

```
$ python3 scripts/check_skill_lossless.py --baseline 864ad7f     # before
LOSSLESS: 1317/1317 baseline lines accounted for across 31 files, 20 waived
# after replacing line 36 with the twelve-key YAML fence:
LOST: SKILL.md:71: - Extract the structured object: `role_title`, `seniority`, ...
CONTENT LOST: 1316/1317 baseline lines accounted for across 31 files, 20 waived
```

The fix must be **additive** — leave line 36 byte-for-byte and add a new line after it — which I verified keeps 1317/1317:

```
- And the three that bullet omits, from `SKILL.md`'s twelve-name list: `company`, `salary_range`, `application_type`.
→ LOSSLESS: 1317/1317 baseline lines accounted for across 31 files, 20 waived
```

The `POSTING_FIELDS`-in-`vocab.py` half of the proposal is sound and cheap; asserting all twelve names appear in `modes/apply.md` would then pass on the appended line. findings.title: Cyrillic/Greek/Hebrew/Arabic and astral-CJK text is silently deleted from the submitted PDF; render_cv and check_pages both exit 0
findings.what_is_wrong: render_pdf() runs the LaTeX engine with subprocess.run(cmd, check=True, capture_output=True) (scripts/render_cv.py:1160) and throws the captured output away. The engine's "Missing character" warnings are exit-0 warnings, so a compile in which every glyph of the candidate's name, employers and bullets failed to typeset returns True and prints "Wrote …pdf". _has_cjk() (scripts/render_cv.py:941-946) only recognises U+3000–U+9FFF, Hangul and Thai, so anything outside Latin-1+CJK+Hangul+Thai — Cyrillic, Greek, Hebrew, Arabic, and CJK Extension B (U+20000+, which occurs in real Chinese personal names) — is routed down the Latin/lmroman path where those glyphs do not exist. The .md and .docx renders are correct; only the PDF, the artifact that is actually submitted, is destroyed.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: check_pages.py is the only gate that reads the PDF, and it reads it as bytes for a page tree, not for glyph coverage — its own docstring says "render_cv.py reports success on any compile that returns 0" and then closes only the length half of that hole. UNREADABLE_PDF needs a missing page tree; this PDF has a perfectly good one-page tree. The three judges read cv.md, which is intact, so they see the text the recruiter will never see. render_cv writes nothing to journal.jsonl at all (SKILL.md:700 "Ran, leaving nothing in the journal — they render; they do not judge"), so there is no receipt anyone could inspect. No test renders a non-Latin, non-CJK profile to PDF.

findings.title: check_shortlist passes a wholly fabricated shortlist row: a 4-character source_id plus an empty url short-circuits both provenance checks
findings.what_is_wrong: scripts/check_shortlist.py:99-130 is the gate's whole point ("each row's identifier appears VERBATIM in a raw capture … because that is the one thing a fabricated row cannot do"). Two independent holes defeat it. (a) MIN_SOURCE_ID_LEN = 4 (line 56) is far below the threshold its own comment describes: `2026` is 4 characters and appears in every 51job card via `issueDate`, so the verbatim substring search resolves for an id that identifies nothing. (b) The URL check is guarded by `if url:` (line 123) — an empty string skips URL_NOT_FROM_ADAPTER entirely, and unlike title/why_matched/retrieved_at/source_site there is no non-empty check for `url`. A row whose company, title, salary and raw_text are pure invention therefore passes, and it passes with an empty url, which also means the user cannot apply to it.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: The count-conservation checks (_check_sources) only fire when the shortlist claims MORE rows than the journal recorded — in the ordinary shape, where the adapter returned 25 cards and the run shortlists 3, there is nothing to conserve. The tests exercise the far side of both cliffs and never the near side: test_a_short_source_id_is_rejected_before_the_substring_search uses `"17"` (2 chars, comfortably under the floor) and test_an_invented_url_fires supplies a non-empty invented url. No test uses a 4-char id that IS a substring, and no test blanks the url. Nothing checks title/company/raw_text against the capture at all.

findings.title: The no-prediction lint misses every natural Chinese way of stating an interview probability, and all full-width digits
findings.what_is_wrong: scripts/lint_no_prediction.py:67-74 bans `%` (ASCII only), `\b\d+\s*/\s*\d+\b` (ASCII digits and slash only) and a word list that in Chinese covers only 概率/通过率/命中率/录取率. It does not cover 可能性 ("likelihood"), 机会 ("chance"), 百分之N (the standard Chinese way to write a percentage), 成 (tenths), Chinese numerals, or the full-width forms ％ ／ ０-９ that a Chinese IME produces by default. The Chinese-language card is a first-class output of this skill (count_coverage renders zh by default; SKILL.md:390 says the card follows the user's language), and SKILL.md:429 states the rule as "No percentages of fit" — 百分之六十 is a percentage of fit.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: check_assessment.py re-derives the lint by calling prediction.scan_text (line 197), so the composition layer inherits the same blind spot rather than covering it — both the gate and its belt-and-braces re-derivation use one regex set. The lint's 218-line test file contains no full-width character and no Chinese probability phrasing; the tests exercise the four zh tokens that ARE in the pattern and the masking carve-outs around them, which makes the Chinese coverage look tested. The skill's own description promises it "never predicts an interview or offer probability", so in Chinese that promise currently rests entirely on prose.

4. 面试机会：６０％。

# PERCENT: fit-assessment.md:5: '%' …
# SCORE_PATTERN: fit-assessment.md:5: '8/10' …

Extend _PERCENT to `[%％]`, _SCORE to accept full-width digits and ／, and add to _WORDS the Chinese probability idioms that carry a number: 百分之, `[0-9零一二三四五六七八九十]成`, 可能性 and 机会 when adjacent to a quantity, plus 打分/评分 with a 分 score. Add a test file of Chinese phrasings — the current suite's silence in Chinese is what made this invisible.

findings.title: slugify() empties any Cyrillic/Greek/Hebrew/Arabic/emoji name: two different employers collide on one workspace, and such a user's profile lands at the root of job-profiles
findings.what_is_wrong: scripts/paths.py:30-37 keeps ASCII alphanumerics plus kana/CJK/Hangul and maps everything else to a separator. Every other script — Cyrillic, Greek, Hebrew, Arabic, Devanagari — and every astral character therefore slugifies to the empty string, and accented Latin loses the accent (Océ → 'oc', Zürich → 'z-rich', Nestlé → 'nestl'). Two consequences the module's own docstring says must not happen: workspace() produces the identical path `<profile>/applications/--2026-08-16` for two different employers, so the second application overwrites the first's posting.yaml and cv.md and appends to the first's journal.jsonl; and profile_dir() returns PROFILES_ROOT itself (pathlib treats `root / ""` as root), so a user named e.g. "Иван Петров" gets master_profile at ~/.claude/job-profiles/profile.yaml and answer_bank at ~/.claude/job-profiles/answer-bank.md — shared with every other such user, and siblings of everyone else's profile directory.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: workspace() validates only the date ("date is validated rather than slugified"); an empty company or role slug raises nothing. Nothing anywhere asserts a slug is non-empty. The test suite names the exact failure mode and then tests one script: `test_slugify_keeps_cjk_so_a_chinese_employer_does_not_become_an_empty_name` covers 字节跳动, and the parametrised cases are all ASCII. The docstring's stated risk — "collapse two different companies onto the same directory" — was fixed for CJK and left open for the class.

findings.title: check_word_limits counts 300 Hangul characters as 1 word (and 300 astral CJK as 1), so a Korean statement 3x over the limit passes
findings.what_is_wrong: scripts/check_word_limits.py:45-52 counts a token's CJK characters via `"぀" <= ch <= "鿿"` (U+3040–U+9FFF). That range covers kana and CJK Unified + Ext A but excludes Hangul (U+AC00–U+D7A3), CJK Extension B and beyond (U+20000+), and CJK Compatibility Ideographs (U+F900+). Because `_WORD = [^\W\d_]+` treats an unbroken Hangul run as one token with zero in-range CJK characters, the whole run counts as 1 word. SKILL.md:164 names Korea among the markets this skill serves, and the limit regex explicitly accepts 字 as a unit, so CJK-script statements are in scope by design.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: OVER_LIMIT can only fire when the count exceeds the limit; a 300x undercount guarantees it never does, and the gate exits 0 with verdict "pass". EMPTY_CRITERION does not fire either, because the count is 1, not 0. test_check_word_limits.py contains no CJK or Hangul character, so both the working Chinese path and the broken Korean path are untested.

findings.title: Malformed or wrongly-shaped YAML, a read-only workspace, or a workspace that is a file make gates traceback with exit code 1 — the 'findings' code — and leave no receipt
findings.what_is_wrong: Only check_shortlist.py wraps yaml.safe_load in try/except YAMLError (lines 457-473). The other 20 call sites do not, and none of them checks that the parsed document is a mapping before calling .get on it. An unclosed scalar, a top-level list, or JSON-shaped input therefore raises out of main(), and Python exits 1 — which in this skill's contract means "gate ran, here are the findings on stdout", not "could not run" (2). Worse, the receipt is never written, so the one state the journal exists to make visible ('risk-register #12: a gate that was skipped produces no output, and no output looks exactly like a clean run') is exactly the state that produces no journal line. The same shape appears for a chmod 0500 workspace (PermissionError out of journal.append / coverage.json write) and for a workspace path that is a regular file (FileExistsError out of `workspace.mkdir(exist_ok=True)`).
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: Each gate's cannot_run() helper is careful and well documented, and every test drives main() through it with a MISSING file — none feeds a file that exists and is unparsable or the wrong shape. Downstream composition partly saves assess mode (check_assessment's MISSING_RECEIPT catches a crashed count_coverage), but check_assessment itself has the same unguarded load at line 140, and the discover/apply/interview gates that crash this way are the last thing in their chain. A caller that branches on the exit code — which SKILL.md:531 explicitly tells the model to do — reads a traceback as findings.

findings.fix: Give every gate the same entry guard check_shortlist already has: wrap the load in try/except yaml.YAMLError -> cannot_run(...), and follow it with an isinstance(doc, dict) check -> cannot_run(...). Better, put it in one place — a `paths.load_mapping(path)` or a small `gate.load_yaml(workspace, path, GATE)` helper — since 20 hand-written copies is how the next one gets forgotten. Wrap main() bodies so OSError/PermissionError also routes to cannot_run and exit 2 rather than an exit-1 traceback. Add a shared parametrised test that feeds every gate an unclosed scalar and a top-level list and asserts exit 2 plus exactly one could_not_run receipt.

findings.title: enter_mode.py silently creates a workspace that does not exist — the one thing every gate deliberately refuses to do
findings.what_is_wrong: enter_mode.py calls journal.append() unconditionally, and journal.append does `workspace.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` (scripts/journal.py:22). So `enter_mode.py --workspace <typo>` materialises the typo'd directory, writes a mode_entry into it, prints "entered mode assess" and exits 0. Four gates (check_word_limits:106, check_pages:129, check_personal_data:58, lint_cv:90, check_apply:67) carry the identical comment explaining why they must NOT do this — "a gate that creates the workspace it is auditing has manufactured its own evidence" — and paths.py's module docstring says the same about path builders. enter_mode is the first command every mode runs, so it defeats the guard for everything downstream: after it, every gate has a directory to write receipts into whether or not the user's real workspace exists.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: Exit 0 and a success message; the mode_entry record it writes is exactly what the mode gates look for, so the run looks correctly entered. The gates' 'workspace does not exist -> exit 2' branch, which is the intended alarm, is unreachable once enter_mode has run. test_check_apply has test_a_missing_workspace_is_exit_2_and_creates_nothing for check_apply, but no equivalent for enter_mode.

Alternatively give journal.append a `create=False` default and pass create=True only from the one place that is supposed to bootstrap. Add the test the other gates already have.

findings.title: mock_blocks.quote_is_in drops ellipsis segments under 8 characters instead of checking them, so an assessor quote can flip 'the team' to 'I' and still resolve
findings.what_is_wrong: scripts/mock_blocks.py:153 `long_enough = [s for s in segments if len(s) >= MIN_SEGMENT]` discards the short segments rather than requiring them, and quote_is_in then asserts only the survivors are in the transcript. Any fragment of 7 characters or fewer that the assessor places around a real quote is therefore unverified — and 7 characters is enough for 'I', 'I alone', 'we lost', 'not the'. check_mock.py:133 uses this for QUOTE_NOT_IN_TRANSCRIPT, and lines 477/521 use it for the answer-bank and walk-back matching, so an attribution inflation — the exact over-claim agents/mock-assessor-provenance.md exists to tag — passes as a sourced quote.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: The tests bracket the hole without hitting it: test at test_mock_blocks.py:126 pins the ellipsis tolerance with two long segments (both checked), and the test at line 135 pins 'we did' — a wholly-short quote, where quote_segments falls back to `[whole]` and the drop does not apply. The mixed case, one long segment plus one short invention, is the only shape where the drop bites and it is untested.

finding.title: Cyrillic/Greek/Hebrew/Arabic and astral-CJK text is silently deleted from the submitted PDF; render_cv and check_pages both exit 0
finding.what_is_wrong: render_pdf() runs the LaTeX engine with subprocess.run(cmd, check=True, capture_output=True) (scripts/render_cv.py:1160) and throws the captured output away. The engine's "Missing character" warnings are exit-0 warnings, so a compile in which every glyph of the candidate's name, employers and bullets failed to typeset returns True and prints "Wrote …pdf". _has_cjk() (scripts/render_cv.py:941-946) only recognises U+3000–U+9FFF, Hangul and Thai, so anything outside Latin-1+CJK+Hangul+Thai — Cyrillic, Greek, Hebrew, Arabic, and CJK Extension B (U+20000+, which occurs in real Chinese personal names) — is routed down the Latin/lmroman path where those glyphs do not exist. The .md and .docx renders are correct; only the PDF, the artifact that is actually submitted, is destroyed.
finding.why_nothing_reports_it: check_pages.py is the only gate that reads the PDF, and it reads it as bytes for a page tree, not for glyph coverage — its own docstring says "render_cv.py reports success on any compile that returns 0" and then closes only the length half of that hole. UNREADABLE_PDF needs a missing page tree; this PDF has a perfectly good one-page tree. The three judges read cv.md, which is intact, so they see the text the recruiter will never see. render_cv writes nothing to journal.jsonl at all (SKILL.md:700 "Ran, leaving nothing in the journal — they render; they do not judge"), so there is no receipt anyone could inspect.
