verdicts.verdict:
## VERDICT: STANDS — and the finding understates its own trigger while proposing a fix that would miss the realistic case

**1. Reproduction — exact, verbatim, reproduces.**

```
$ python3 scripts/render_cv.py $A/render/cyr.yaml --format pdf --out $A/render/cyr.pdf
Wrote .../cyr.pdf (LaTeX source alongside it: .../cyr.tex)
render_cv EXIT=0
$ pdftotext -q $A/render/cyr.pdf -
ivan@example.com • Berlin

Summary
.

Experience
,
•

2019-01 – present
40 .
$ python3 scripts/check_pages.py --workspace $A/ws     # cv.pdf + tailored-profile.yaml
check_pages EXIT=0
$ cd $A/render && tectonic -o . cyr.tex 2>&1 | grep -ci "missing character"
234          # tectonic exit=0, all 234 discarded by capture_output=True
```

**2. It matters far more than the finding says — the trigger is not "exotic scripts", it is anything above U+00FF.** The pipeline's own preferred engine is tectonic (`find_latex_engine`, scripts/render_cv.py:910, non-CJK candidates `("tectonic", "pdflatex")`, and modes/apply.md:80 recommends installing tectonic), which is XeTeX-based — so the `\usepackage[utf8]{inputenc}` + `[T1]{fontenc}` preamble is a pdfLaTeX preamble handed to a Unicode engine, and every codepoint past Latin-1 falls off the TFM. Measured, with a **`target_market: nl`** profile:

```
$ python3 scripts/render_cv.py $A/render/pl.yaml --format pdf --out $A/render/pl.pdf; echo EXIT=$?
EXIT=0
$ pdftotext -q $A/render/pl.pdf - | head -8
ukasz Wójcik                                   # "Łukasz Wójcik"
MRI Reconstruction Engineer
Worked at koda and e on rozíení pipelines with Zsófia Kovács.
Engineer, Politechnika lska                    # "Politechnika Śląska"
• Zmniejszyem opónienie o 40 procent.
```
Dropped codepoints (from the discarded log): U+0102 U+0130 U+0141 U+015E U+0163 U+0218 U+021A — Latin **Extended-A**. That is Polish, Czech, Slovak, Croatian, Hungarian, Turkish, Romanian, Latvian names and employers, in the nl/de/uk markets this skill is built for. `cv.md` is intact (`# Łukasz Wójcik`), so the three judges read a name the recruiter never sees. No test compiles a real PDF at all — the only two `render_pdf` tests monkeypatch `find_latex_engine` (test_render_cv.py:78, :89), and `test_latex_preamble_has_unicode_packages` (line 130, docstring "for UTF-8 safety") *pins* the inputenc/fontenc pair that is precisely what fails under the engine actually chosen. Textbook repo-thesis: a green test enforcing the broken thing.

**3. No recorded limit.** Grepped the spec, all five plans, SKILL.md and the baseline `~/.claude/skills/job-application` tree for `font|glyph|latin|diacritic|unicode`: the only recorded font limit is the CJK one (missing engine / missing CJK font), which is handled loudly. Nothing anywhere concedes non-Latin-1 loss. NOT already-recorded.

**What the original finding got wrong (both matter for the fix):**
- **Its astral-CJK claim does not reproduce end-to-end.** A realistic CN profile whose name contains U+2000B renders *correctly* (`pdftotext` → `𠀋田太郎`, EXIT=0), because the rest of the CV is BMP CJK so `profile_has_cjk` is True and the fallback chain lands on a font that covers Ext-B. The finding's `hostile.tex` was hand-written, not produced by the pipeline. Drop that half.
- **Its proposed `_has_cjk` widening — "any codepoint outside Latin-1/Latin-Extended" — would leave the Polish/Czech/Turkish/Romanian case broken**, since those characters *are* Latin-Extended-A. The threshold has to be `ord(ch) > 0xFF`, and the switch must be to a fontspec/TU preamble, not to a second T1 font chain: verified under tectonic that `\usepackage{fontspec}\setmainfont{Helvetica}` renders `Łukasz Wójcik / Politechnika Śląska / Škoda / Ștefan / Иван Петров / Γεωργίου` correctly. Caveat the finding misses: the preamble is chosen before the engine is known, and fontspec needs a Unicode engine — so the branch must be engine-aware (fontspec when tectonic/xelatex/lualatex; keep T1+inputenc, which genuinely handles Latin-Ext-A, only for pdflatex), otherwise the fix trades a silent drop for a hard compile failure on pdflatex-only boxes.
- The rest of the fix is right and is the part with the backstop: scan the captured engine output for `Missing character`, and add a gate asserting `meta.name` and each `experience[].org` appear in the extracted PDF text. Note `render_cv.py` contains zero `journal` calls, so "make it a journalled finding" means giving the renderer a receipt it currently has no mechanism for — cheaper to put the text-coverage assertion in `check_pages.py`, which already holds a receipt and already opens the file.

Two independent holes defeat it. (a) MIN_SOURCE_ID_LEN = 4 (line 56) is far below the threshold its own comment describes: `2026` is 4 characters and appears in every 51job card via `issueDate`, so the verbatim substring search resolves for an id that identifies nothing. (b) The URL check is guarded by `if url:` (line 123) — an empty string skips URL_NOT_FROM_ADAPTER entirely, and unlike title/why_matched/retrieved_at/source_site there is no non-empty check for `url`. A row whose company, title, salary and raw_text are pure invention therefore passes, and it passes with an empty url, which also means the user cannot apply to it.
finding.why_nothing_reports_it: The count-conservation checks (_check_sources) only fire when the shortlist claims MORE rows than the journal recorded — in the ordinary shape, where the adapter returned 25 cards and the run shortlists 3, there is nothing to conserve. verdicts.verdict:
## VERDICT: STANDS-WITH-LOWER-SEVERITY (severity high, not critical — and both named mechanisms are misdiagnosed)

The headline reproduces exactly: a row with an invented title/company/salary/raw_text passes the gate at EXIT=0. But neither of the two mechanisms the finding blames is what makes it possible, and the risk-register scenario the finding invokes is already closed.

**Reproduction (all scripts in `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-donghanglyu/d1ca171b-6798-42dc-9582-87e4635be401/scratchpad/audit/refute/`; repo untouched, `git status --porcelain` shows only the pre-existing untracked json):**

```
$ python3 isolate.py            # each case = repo fixture + ONE mutation
A. untouched fixture                                 EXIT=0 []
B. rows[0].url = ''                                  EXIT=0 []
D. source_id='2026' (4 chars, in issueDate)          EXIT=0 []
H. title/company/raw_text invented only              EXIT=0 []   <-- real source_id, everything else fabricated
```

**Why the diagnosis is wrong, in two runs:**

```
$ python3 prefix.py             # does raising MIN_SOURCE_ID_LEN to 6 help?
6-char PREFIX of a real jobId    sid='173199'    EXIT=0 []
8-char prefix                    sid='17319959'  EXIT=0 []
plausible 9-digit invented id    sid='173201234' EXIT=1 ['SOURCE_ID_NOT_IN_RAW']

$ python3 padding.py            # is the documented fabrication scenario reachable?
PAD: adapter really returned 2, shortlist 5 (honest report) EXIT=1 ['SOURCE_REPORT_COUNT_MISMATCH']
PAD + lie about rows_returned=5 (journal still says 2)      EXIT=1 ['SOURCE_REPORT_COUNT_MISMATCH']
BULK: adapter returned 25, shortlist 2 real + 3 fake        EXIT=0 []
```

The floor is a sideshow — an 8-character prefix of a real id sails through, so the auditor's own fix #1a closes nothing. And case **H** is strictly easier than any substring trick: paste a *real* `source_id` onto a wholly invented row and it passes with no cleverness at all. The only real gap is the one the finding lists last: **nothing but `source_id` is ever compared to the capture.** Meanwhile spec risk row 1 ("平台什么也没返回，模型把空缺填上了") is *not* reachable — an empty capture fires `NO_RAW_CAPTURE_FOR_SITE`, and padding a shortfall fires `SOURCE_REPORT_COUNT_MISMATCH` in both the honest and the lying variant. The hole needs the bulk shape, where the model discards real rows to insert fake ones. Ordinary, but not the named scenario — hence high, not critical.

### What the finding got wrong about the fix

- **Fix #2 (`EMPTY_URL`) should be dropped — it is BY-DESIGN and the fix would make things worse.** `modes/discover.md:410` prescribes, for `URL_NOT_FROM_ADAPTER`: *"replace it with the adapter's URL **or drop the field**"*, and `references/source-policy.md:98` requires `url` be *verbatim from an adapter response*. `python3 urlcases.py` shows dropping the key fires `MISSING_FIELD` while `url: ""` / `url: null` pass — i.e. an empty url is the only way to obey layer 1.5. Requiring non-empty url would contradict the mode doc and push the model to assemble a URL, which is exactly what `URL_NOT_FROM_ADAPTER` exists to forbid. The genuine (minor) defect here is the doc/gate mismatch: the doc says "drop the field", the gate says you may not.
- **Fix #1 (raise floor to 6) buys nothing** — refuted above. The delimiter-bounded half is the only useful part, and it needs `re.escape`: boss `security_id` and linkedin `urn:li:jobPosting:…` shapes carry `~`, `=`, `-`, `:`, so a hand-rolled boundary regex is its own silent-failure risk. Raising the floor is at least *safe* against the enumerated job sources (51job 9-digit, indeed 16-hex, linkedin 10-digit, boss long), but it is not a fix.
- **Fix #3 is the whole finding and should be fix #1.** Cheapest first step it misses: nothing ties row `id` to `<site>-<source_id>`, though `modes/discover.md:244` documents that format — my fabricated row carried `id: 51job-FAKE` with `source_id: 2026` and passed. For the content anchor, prefer `raw_text` over `title`: `title` is legitimately normalised/translated by step 6, so a verbatim title match would false-positive on honest rows, whereas `raw_text` is by definition "the card text the evaluator actually saw".

finding.title: The no-prediction lint misses every natural Chinese way of stating an interview probability, and all full-width digits
finding.what_is_wrong: scripts/lint_no_prediction.py:67-74 bans `%` (ASCII only), `\b\d+\s*/\s*\d+\b` (ASCII digits and slash only) and a word list that in Chinese covers only 概率/通过率/命中率/录取率. It does not cover 可能性 ("likelihood"), 机会 ("chance"), 百分之N (the standard Chinese way to write a percentage), 成 (tenths), Chinese numerals, or the full-width forms ％ ／ ０-９ that a Chinese IME produces by default. The Chinese-language card is a first-class output of this skill (count_coverage renders zh by default; SKILL.md:390 says the card follows the user's language), and SKILL.md:429 states the rule as "No percentages of fit" — 百分之六十 is a percentage of fit.
finding.why_nothing_reports_it: check_assessment.py re-derives the lint by calling prediction.scan_text (line 197), so the composition layer inherits the same blind spot rather than covering it — both the gate and its belt-and-braces re-derivation use one regex set. The lint's 218-line test file contains no full-width character and no Chinese probability phrasing; the tests exercise the four zh tokens that ARE in the pattern and the masking carve-outs around them, which makes the Chinese coverage look tested. The skill's own description promises it "never predicts an interview or offer probability", so in Chinese that promise currently rests entirely on prose.

Extend _PERCENT to `[%％]`, _SCORE to accept full-width digits and ／, and add to _WORDS the Chinese probability idioms that carry a number: 百分之, `[0-9零一二三四五六七八九十]成`, 可能性 and 机会 when adjacent to a quantity, plus 打分/评分 with a 分 score. Add a test file of Chinese phrasings — the current suite's silence in Chinese is what made this invisible.

$ # same file + one line "6. 面试机会 60%，简历打分 8/10。"
PERCENT: fit-assessment.md:8: '%' in '6. 面试机会 60%，简历打分 8/10。'
SCORE_PATTERN: fit-assessment.md:8: '8/10' in '6. 面试机会 60%，简历打分 8/10。'
EXIT=1
```

The gap is real and nothing downstream covers it (`check_assessment.py:196-198` calls `prediction.scan_text` directly, so it inherits the same regex set), the zh path is first-class (`count_coverage.py:131` defaults `--lang zh`), and I found no recorded limit — the docstring enumerates four masking carve-outs and one allowlist but never a coverage boundary, and nothing in the spec or the five plans mentions full-width or Chinese idiom coverage. So DROP and ALREADY-RECORDED are both wrong.

Severity drops to medium because the realistic half is much narrower than claimed. The four tokens an LLM actually reaches for when writing "probability" in Chinese — 概率 first — are already covered, and these surfaces are model-authored, not typed: the finding justifies the full-width case with "a Chinese IME produces by default", an author who does not exist on this path. What genuinely survives is `百分之N` / `N成`, natural Chinese percentages that SKILL.md:429 bans in layer 1 ("No percentages of fit") and layer 3 cannot see — a real layer-1/layer-3 asymmetry, but one narrow phrasing family, not "every natural Chinese way".

## What the finding got wrong about the fix

The proposed word list breaks the skill's own mandated output in two independent places, both reproduced:

**1. `可能性` is in the required disclaimer.** SKILL.md:412 and modes/assess.md:200 mandate `本 skill 不给出面试或录用的可能性估计，也不给 0–100 分。` shipped *unchanged*, and `check_assessment.py` greps for it literally. Applying the fix:

```
### CURRENT lint on the MANDATED zh disclaimer:  EXIT=0 (passes, as required)
### PROPOSED-FIX lint on the SAME disclaimer:
PREDICTION_WORD: fit-assessment.md:7: '可能性' in '> 本 skill 不给出面试或录用的可能性估计，也不给 0–100 分。要不要投，由你决定。'
EXIT=1
$ python3 -m pytest scripts/tests/test_lint_no_prediction.py -q
3 failed, 17 passed          # incl. test_the_required_disclaimer_passes  (baseline: 20 passed)
```

That is a literal repeat of the disclaimer-vs-gate bug this repo already fixed. The finding's hedge ("when adjacent to a quantity") does not save it — `0–100 分` is on the same line. It at least fails loudly, so it is a bad fix rather than a new silent failure.

**2. `机会` and `评分` are in verbatim convention cards.** `check_assessment.py:291` requires market-convention bodies rendered verbatim into `fit-assessment.md`, which is a scanned surface:

```
PREDICTION_WORD: fit-assessment.md:4: '机会' in '…必须注明来源与你讨论，并给你回应的机会。所以：'   (nl.yaml:349)
PREDICTION_WORD: fit-assessment.md:5: '评分' in '…当作一份带评分的鉴定来读'                      (de.yaml:53)
```

**3. NFKC is not length-preserving**, so "keep the unnormalised line for the reported span" is broken by construction — the entire masking layer is documented as length-preserving for exactly this reason. On a JD pasted from a PDF (`ﬁ` ligature), `len 48 → 50`, and the `%` match at NFKC span (42,43) slices `'是'` out of the original line. Normalisation would have to be done with an index map, or restricted to a targeted character-class widening (`[%％]`, full-width digits and `／` in `_SCORE`).

The defensible fix is the narrow one: widen `_PERCENT`/`_SCORE` to their full-width forms, and add only `百分之` and `[0-9零一二三四五六七八九十]成` to `_WORDS` — leaving `可能性`, `机会`, `打分`, `评分` out, since each collides with text the skill is required to emit.

verdicts.verdict:
# VERDICT: STANDS

I tried to break it three ways and could not. It reproduces exactly as written, and the real behaviour is **worse** than the finding describes, so if anything the severity is understated.

**Reproduction (workspace at `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-donghanglyu/d1ca171b-6798-42dc-9582-87e4635be401/scratchpad/audit/refute-check-apply/ws`, built the same way `test_check_apply._good_workspace` does):**

```
$ python3 scripts/check_word_limits.py --workspace $WS
OVER_LIMIT: 'Making Effective Decisions (250 words)' is 660 words against its stated limit of 250 …
EXIT=1
$ python3 scripts/check_pages.py --workspace $WS --today 2026-08-16
CV_TOO_LONG: cv.pdf is 4 pages; the length table in references/cv-craft.md allows 1 for 2 years of experience …
EXIT=1
$ python3 -c "…journal.read_receipts(ws)"
[('check_personal_data','pass'),('check_claims','pass'),('check_render_freshness','pass'),
 ('parse_verdicts','pass'),('lint_cv','pass'),('check_apply','pass'),
 ('check_pages','fail'),('check_word_limits','fail')]
$ python3 scripts/check_apply.py --workspace $WS
check_apply EXIT=0  (0 = the package may be delivered)
```

Deleting the two receipts also gives `EXIT=0`. So both halves hold, and the stronger case is the one the original finding did not test: **the gates do not even have to be skipped.** They can run honestly, print their finding, and write `verdict: fail` into `journal.jsonl`, and `check_apply` — the gate whose docstring is "Composition… this asserts that each of them actually ran, on this workspace, and passed" — writes its own `pass` receipt into the same file, three lines below two `fail`s. The journal contains its own contradiction and the delivery gate signs off.

**Not by design.** I grepped the spec, both plan files and every docstring. Nothing records this as a chosen limit; the evidence runs the other way. Plan Task 19 (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-09-1-migration-and-p0-fixes.md:4677`) states the intent as *"It requires **every upstream gate's receipt**"* and its Interfaces line says *"imports all **eight** upstream gates by name (Tasks 9–18) … so this task must run after them"* — check_pages and check_word_limits are Tasks 17 and 18, they existed when check_apply was written, and six of the eight got required. SKILL.md:707 proves the distinction was consciously modelled: there is a separate heading reading *"`scripts/check_apply.py` does **not** require these"* for the discover gates, and these two were left under the "requires each of these" heading anyway. `test_skill_structure.py:70` only asserts each script is *named somewhere* in the self-check section — it never checks which heading it sits under, which is the same blind spot that let the disclaimer paraphrase live.

**It matters in the realistic path.** `modes/apply.md:215-216` lists both as conditional steps, so skipping one is a normal model slip. For structured applications it is worse: `references/structured-applications.md:52` routes all three judges *away* from the supporting statement, so `check_word_limits` is the only program that ever reads the one artifact that actually gets scored — and no gate requires it. Nothing downstream compensates: the judges read `cv.md`, `lint_cv` reads `cv.md`, `render_cv` reports success on any exit-0 compile.

## What the finding got wrong about the fix

- The two conditional appends are necessary but **not sufficient** — they only close the never-ran hole. Add the cheap, general one first: `check_apply` should fail on **any** gate whose latest receipt is a `fail`, not only the named ones. `journal.read_receipts(ws)` with no gate argument already returns every receipt (verified above), so this is a few lines, needs no file-sniffing, and future-proofs every gate added later including `check_mock`.
- `if application_type == "structured"` requires `check_apply` to parse `posting.yaml`, which it currently never opens. Guard it — a malformed `posting.yaml` must not turn the delivery gate into a `yaml` traceback, and a *missing* `posting.yaml` must not silently mean "not structured". Also note the keying asymmetry: `check_letter` keys on an input (`letter.yaml`), `check_pages` would key on an output (`cv.pdf`), so a degraded run with no tectonic correctly drops the requirement — that part is fine, but it should be written down as the reason, not left implicit.
- The proposed drift test should assert the heading *partition*, not just membership: the "requires each of these" block already lists `check_apply.py` itself and `check_mock.py`, neither of which `check_apply` requires or could. A test that reads the block and compares it to `REQUIRED_GATES` ∪ conditionals will need those two explicitly accounted for, or it will fail for the wrong reason on day one.

verdicts.verdict:
## VERDICT: STANDS-WITH-LOWER-SEVERITY (high → medium)

It reproduces exactly as written, and no recorded limit excuses it — I grepped the spec, all five plans, and every docstring: plan 1 (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-09-1-migration-and-p0-fixes.md:544`) reproduces the CJK test verbatim and says nothing about any other script. But two of the finding's load-bearing claims are inflated: within the five markets the skill actually supports (cn/nl/de/uk/us) **no realistic company or role slugifies empty** — accented Latin only degrades cosmetically and still collides with nothing (`Nestlé→'nestl'`, `Zürich Insurance→'z-rich-insurance'`, `Océ Technologies→'oc-technologies'`) — so the headline "two employers overwrite each other" needs an out-of-scope market *and* two such employers on the same day; and "shared with every other such user" misreads a single-user `~/.claude` install, where the consequence is one user's profile misfiled, not cross-user leakage.

What keeps it alive at medium is a case the finding missed and which is far more reachable than Cyrillic: `slugify`'s own `str(text or "")` makes an empty/None name a first-class input, so `profile_dir(None)`, `profile_dir("")` and `profile_dir("   ")` all return `PROFILES_ROOT`, and the resulting layout silently defeats exactly the two lookups the module docstring exists to protect (verified: the resume glob `job-profiles/*/applications/*` and the reuse glob `job-profiles/*/profile.yaml` both return `[]` against a real on-disk tree, so every run re-interviews from scratch with no error anywhere), and `search_dir('Иван','2026-08-16-поиск')` collapses to `searches/2026-08-16`, colliding two searches on one day.

```
$ python3 -c "...import paths..."
Яндекс -> ''   Ολυμπιακός -> ''   מובילאיי -> ''   Océ -> 'oc'   Zürich -> 'z-rich'   😀Corp -> 'corp'
/…/job-profiles/me/applications/--2026-08-16   (Яндекс)
/…/job-profiles/me/applications/--2026-08-16   (Сбербанк)   same directory? True
profile_dir('Иван Петров') == PROFILES_ROOT -> True ; master_profile -> /…/job-profiles/profile.yaml
None -> '' | profile_dir==ROOT: True      '' -> '' | True      '   ' -> '' | True      '?' -> '' | True
$ # on-disk, PROFILES_ROOT redirected to scratch:
resume-lookup glob  <root>/*/applications/* : []
profile-reuse glob  <root>/*/profile.yaml   : []
```

**What it got wrong about the fix.** (1) `str.isalpha()`-based filtering drops digits — `51job` (a real cn-market employer) becomes `job`, and *no existing test has a digit in it*, so that regression ships green; the filter must be alpha-or-digit. (2) Widening to accented Latin introduces an NFC/NFD hazard the CJK path never had: NFKC keeps `é` composed, but macOS `listdir` can hand back the decomposed form, so a directory written as `océ` may not string-match when the resume lookup reads it — either keep folding Latin accents to ASCII (`Océ→oce`, which is also nicer for a human-browsed path) or normalise on read. (3) The hash fallback is the wrong tool for `name`: the finding is right that `profile_dir()` should raise, and once it does the hash is only needed for company/role, where an unidentifiable `xa1b2c3d4-…` directory trades a collision for a path the human and the "match by company/role" resume step can no longer read — prefer the widened filter plus a short hash suffix only on the genuinely-empty remainder. (4) Minor: astral characters empty a slug only when the whole string is astral (`😀Corp → 'corp'`).

findings.title: Any unrecognised market token silently disables the entire convention path, and the mandated "no convention data" disclosure has no gate and no English wording
findings.what_is_wrong: scripts/check_assessment.py:296 reads `if market in conventions.MARKET_KEYS:` and does nothing at all in the else branch. And the failure is a missing card, which is indistinguishable from a market that legitimately has no table — the two cases were never given different shapes.

findings.title: On a machine without LaTeX the only length gate in the skill silently never runs, and the renderer still exits 0
findings.what_is_wrong: Two things compound. First, scripts/render_cv.py:1199-1206 and scripts/render_letter.py:129-131 print the failure to stderr and then `return` — main() returns None, so the CLI exits 0 on a PDF that was never produced; `render_cv.py --format pdf && echo ok` prints ok. Second, check_pages.py is the only thing in the pipeline that measures the artifact actually submitted (its own docstring says so, and it is the sole enforcement of the hard length table in references/cv-craft.md:224-228), it exits 2 when cv.pdf is absent, and it is NOT in check_apply.py:43 REQUIRED_GATES. So on any machine without tectonic/xelatex — which is every default Linux/Windows box, and macOS without Homebrew — the deliverables are cv.md/cv.tex/cv.docx, no page budget is ever checked, and check_apply reports the package may be delivered with no mention that a gate was skipped. This is the exact shape check_apply's own docstring warns about ("a skipped script produces no output and no output is exactly what a clean run looks like") applied to the one gate left out of the list.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: SKILL.md:691 and modes/apply.md:215 both qualify it as "(if a PDF was produced)" / "only if cv.pdf was produced", which makes the conditional look deliberate — so a reader auditing the checklist sees a documented option, not a hole. And because check_pages is conditional, it cannot be added to REQUIRED_GATES without a rule for the no-PDF case, so the composition backstop that catches every other skipped gate was never wired to it. test_check_pages.py always builds a PDF; nothing in the suite runs the apply gate on a workspace with no PDF at all. The renderer's exit-0 is tested only through render_pdf()'s boolean return (test_render_cv.py), never through main()'s exit status.

produced: ['cv.tex']

$ python3 repro_nopdf_apply.py
check_pages is in REQUIRED_GATES? False
check_apply exit: 0 -> the package may be delivered
check_pages exit: 2 | cannot run check_pages: …/cv.pdf does not exist

(no_engine.py confirms the honest half: with PATH cleared and _ENGINE_DIRS emptied, both renderers write the .tex and say so — 'WARNING: no LaTeX engine (tectonic/pdflatex) found. Wrote …/cv.tex' and 'WARNING: no LaTeX engine found. Wrote …/letter.tex'.)
findings.fix: Two small changes. (1) scripts/render_cv.py main() and scripts/render_letter.py main(): `return 0 if ok else 1` on the pdf branch so a caller can tell, and note the code in the docstring. (2) Add check_pages to check_apply.py REQUIRED_GATES with the no-PDF case handled explicitly rather than by omission: accept a receipt with verdict "could_not_run" AND require the run to have told the user that the length rule could not be enforced (a NO_PAGE_CHECK finding otherwise). Failing that, at minimum have check_apply emit a WARN when cv.pdf is absent and no check_pages receipt exists, so the skipped gate makes a noise instead of looking like a clean one.

findings.title: "opencli is not installed" is classified as a generic transport failure whose prescribed remedy is another opencli command
findings.what_is_wrong: check_opencli_result.py:33-34 defines five classifications — ok, platform_limit, not_logged_in, no_auth_adapter, transport — with no state for "the tool is not on this machine". A `command not found` (exit 127) falls through to `transport`, and the remedy handed back (check_opencli_result.py:208-212, restated at modes/discover.md:224) is "Run `opencli doctor`" — a command that by construction cannot run in this situation. Nothing in modes/discover.md's entry conditions or Step 1 checks that opencli exists before the first call, and README.md documents the LaTeX prerequisite but never mentions opencli at all. The honest degraded output that should follow (references/discovery-sources.md's direction-level shortlist) then runs straight into the Chinese-only disclosure block from the first finding, so the user who most needs an honest degradation is the one who cannot produce one.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: The classification is a wrapper, not a gate — it exits 0 by design ("A `not_logged_in` adapter is information the discover mode acts on, not a failure of the run"), so there is no verdict to be wrong. test_check_opencli_result.py exercises exit codes and stderr bodies but has no case for the tool being absent, because on the machine that wrote it opencli is always installed. And `transport` is a genuinely correct label for a failed invocation, so no consistency check can flag it; what is wrong is only the remedy text, which no program reads.

verdicts.verdict:
## VERDICT: STANDS-WITH-LOWER-SEVERITY (high, not critical)

Both halves reproduce byte-for-byte on the current tree (the given repro needed `--workspace`, which the finding's transcript omits; with the flag it is exact):

```
=== 1. baseline (Chinese fixture, unmodified) ===   exit: 0   (no findings)
=== 2. same workspace, shortlist.md written in English ===   exit: 1
MD_MISSING_PROVISIONAL_STAMP: shortlist.md renders rows without the 「基于卡片信息的初判」 label. …
--- ENGLISH disclosure block -> exit 1
  DEGRADED_WITHOUT_DISCLOSURE: … (本次会话已登录：、Adapter 返回：、收到限制信号后重试：、绕过任何平台控制：、取得真实岗位：、降级输出类型：) …
--- CHINESE disclosure block -> exit 0   (no findings)
```

I could not find a docstring, plan note, or spec row recording this as a chosen limit — and the spec argues the other way harder than the finding does: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-09-job-hunt-skill-design.md:433` (§10 已代为决定的事项) reads `| 语言策略 | CV 跟市场走；评估/shortlist/面试复盘跟用户走 |`, i.e. a user-language shortlist is an explicitly recorded decision, and `indeed`/`linkedin` + `target_market: nl/de/uk/us` make an English user an ordinary case. Severity drops to high because this is a *loud* gate failure with a working escape hatch, not a silent wrong pass: pasting the seven Chinese strings into an English document gates green today, so the shipped harm is a document with Chinese furniture plus a gate round-trip — the "cannot produce an English shortlist" framing overstates it.

### What the finding got wrong about the fix

- **The pair fix breaks two backstops, and repairing them naively opens a new hole.** Applying it verbatim on a copy: `TypeError: 'in <string>' requires string as left operand, not tuple` at `scripts/tests/test_discover_mode_doc.py:51` and `:182`. The obvious repair (`for sp in pair: assert sp in body`) plus an English mirror in `modes/discover.md` — with the English answers left **blank** — passes all 19 mode-doc tests, because the `assert line.split(label,1)[1].strip() == "否"` check at `test_discover_mode_doc.py:52-56` only ever scans the three Chinese labels. The English half would ship without the one backstop whose stated purpose is "concealment has to be an active overwrite, not an omission". That assertion must be extended per spelling as part of the same change.
- **The mirror list is incomplete on the instruction half.** Beyond the two gate literals, `modes/discover.md:361-363` prescribes `## §0 来源与读取质量` / `## §0.1 触发原因` / `## §0.2 披露`, `:365` prescribes `未取详情` (pinned by `test_discover_mode_doc.py:44`), and `:370-371` the degraded bullet labels 目标方向·检索词·…. Pairing only the two gate-checked strings still yields an English document with Chinese scaffolding. Note the gate itself already keys headings on the language-agnostic `§0.1` marker (`check_shortlist.py:368`), so no gate change is needed there — only the mode doc.

Repro scripts: `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-donghanglyu/d1ca171b-6798-42dc-9582-87e4635be401/scratchpad/audit/refute-discover-en/repro_en_shortlist.py`, `.../repro_degraded_en2.py`, patched copy at `.../copy/`.

verdicts.verdict:
## VERDICT: STANDS-WITH-LOWER-SEVERITY (high → medium)

The mechanism reproduces exactly as written — case A (fully English card, in-date convention) returns **zero** findings, proving the English path is otherwise first-class; case B (English card + English banner, expired entry) exits **1** on `MISSING_STALE_BANNER`; case C (same English card, Chinese banner pasted in) exits **0**. `STALE_BANNER` is genuinely the only Chinese-only anchor in the file (`consistency.notices` even carries `anchor_zh`/`anchor_en`), `SKILL.md:390` mandates that the block *"follows the user's language, not the market's"*, 12 shipped entries expire 2026-11-09, and I found **no recorded limit** — plan 2's own anchor-presence check (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-09-2-assess-mode.md:4535-4552`) lists both spellings for every heading and column and simply omits the banner, so this is an oversight, not a decision.

Severity drops to medium because the finding's headline harm is inflated: `MISSING_STALE_BANNER`'s own message quotes the exact required literal, so a model hitting it pastes 「已过复核期」 and the run continues — the passed date does **not** stop the skill working for English users. The real thesis-shaped harm is case C, which the finding under-sold: the gate exits 0 while certifying a banner an English-only reader cannot read, defeating the rule's stated purpose ("the reader has to be told it is stale"). Blast radius is one sentence in one section; `make check` → `check_conventions.py --ci` still fails hard on the date, so only stale *installed* copies (`~/.claude/skills/job-hunt`) are exposed.

### What the finding got wrong about the fix

Applied verbatim to a copy at `/private/tmp/.../scratchpad/audit/refute-stale-banner/fixcopy`, the proposed fix **does not fix case B**:

1. **The English anchor is case-sensitive and does not match its own reproduction.** `"past its review date"` vs. the finding's banner `"> ⚠️ Past its review date — re-check the source."` → `'past its review date' in banner` is `False`; `in banner.casefold()` is `True`. With the fix applied, 37/37 tests pass **and repro B still exits 1**. This matters uniquely here: every other English anchor is a heading (`## Hard blockers`), a column header, a rendered label (`apply verdict:`) or a mid-sentence phrase — the staleness banner is the only anchor whose natural rendering *starts a sentence*. Match against `markdown.casefold()`, or choose a phrase that cannot be sentence-initial.
2. **The tuple breaks the finding message.** Line 322 is `f"…the 「{STALE_BANNER}」 banner…"`, which prints `「('已过复核期', 'past its review date')」`. The fix says "naming both spellings" but its diff omits the f-string change — reproduced.
3. **Minor misquote:** the comment says *"Every heading and column name this gate keys on is a PAIR"*, not "every anchor". `STALE_BANNER` is neither, so the stated invariant isn't literally violated — only its reasoning ("a constant that knows only the Chinese spelling reports a defect on a correct English assessment") generalizes.
4. `any()` also lets an English banner satisfy a Chinese card. That is the same accepted limitation every pair in this file has, but the fix should not be sold as making the banner *readable* — it only widens the accepted set.

finding.title: Any unrecognised market token silently disables the entire convention path, and the mandated "no convention data" disclosure has no gate and no English wording
finding.what_is_wrong: scripts/check_assessment.py:296 reads `if market in conventions.MARKET_KEYS:` and does nothing at all in the else branch. There is no check that `fit-assessment.yaml`'s `market` is one of the six legal tokens (the five in vocab.MARKET_KEYS plus vocab.NO_MARKET = "other"). So `market: usa`, `market: jp`, `market: "United States"`, `market: null` and `market: ""` all pass the gate with zero findings, and all silently produce an assessment with no market card. ## VERDICT: STANDS-WITH-LOWER-SEVERITY (medium, not high)

**The repro is exact.** Re-ran it verbatim — `other`, `jp`, `usa`, `United States`, `None`, `''` all return zero findings from `ca.check`, and `grep -rl 本市场无惯例数据 scripts/` returns nothing. The core defect is real and unrecorded: I grepped the spec, both relevant plans and every named-residual-risk list (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-09-3-discover-mode.md:5129` ff., `…-2-assess-mode.md:2356`) and found no note choosing not to validate the token — plan 2 line 5454 simply specifies `if market in conventions.MARKET_KEYS:` and never considered the else. `BAD_VERDICT` sits 30 lines above in the same function and `check_mock.py:113` gates the identical closed set, so this is an inconsistency the repo's own standard condemns.

**But the harm story does not survive.** The claimed consequence — "every H-1B / I-9 convention is never rendered and the run reports success" — is equally true with the *correct* token: `market='us'` against the real `references/market-conventions/`, zero cards rendered, `conventions_rendered: []` → `PASS (no findings)`. Rendering is `applies_when`-conditional and model-decided, so the gate never had the power the finding says the typo removed; the delta between `usa` and `us` is nil in every reachable case (all five tables ship, so `CONVENTION_TABLE_MISSING` is unreachable), and the *loud* direction is unmentioned: `market='usa'` with a declared id fires `CONVENTION_UNKNOWN_ID: us-at-will-employment is not an entry in usa.yaml`. What is genuinely wrong is a closed set that isn't closed — a schema hole, not a silently-wrong-output hole.

### What the finding got wrong about the fix

- **Sub-claim (b) is a different bug and does not belong here.** `market='us'` (valid), `nl-recognised-sponsor-gate`'s `text_zh` pasted verbatim, `conventions_rendered: []` → `PASS (no findings)`. The borrowing hole is caused by `conventions_rendered` being self-declared, not by the unvalidated token; file it separately or the cross-market scan gets justified by the wrong evidence.
- **The core fix is safe — I ran it.** Patched a copy at `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-donghanglyu/d1ca171b-6798-42dc-9582-87e4635be401/scratchpad/audit/refute-market/repo` with the two-line `BAD_MARKET` check: `795 passed`, same 2 pre-existing `test_install.py` symlink failures as the unpatched copy. Post-patch `usa`/`None` → `BAD_MARKET`, `other`/`us` → PASS.
- **Two corrections to the fix as written.** (1) Do not import `mock_vocab` into the assess gate — `test_vocab.py:73-81` forbids re-declaring and `test_interview_shapes_doc.py:123` pins `mock_vocab`'s naming; add `vocab.ALL_MARKET_KEYS` and have both sites read it. (2) The naive `market not in …` also fires on a `verdict: insufficient_evidence` assessment written without a `market:` key — `modes/assess.md` documents the row schema but never declares `market` a required top-level field, so decide that explicitly or the fix cries wolf on the refusal path.

finding.title: A nurse's or a sales rep's mock fails the gate for correctly using the one defect tag that exists for their family
finding.what_is_wrong: scripts/mock_vocab.py:93 closes the family vocabulary in code — FAMILY_CONDITIONAL = {"NO-NEXT-STEP": ("sales",), "CLINICAL-DRIFT": ("clinical",)} — and check_mock.py:175-180 fires the hard finding TAG_NOT_APPLICABLE whenever `FAMILY:` lowercased is not exactly that bare word. But nothing tells the model what token to write. modes/interview.md:34 says the family comes "from references/role-families.md", whose nine section headings are "Clinical / licensed healthcare", "Sales / business development", "Skilled trades", … — not one of which equals "clinical" or "sales". The only worked example in the mode file is `FAMILY: ml-engineering` (modes/interview.md:242), which is not one of the nine either. references/interview-shapes.md:94/97/147, the file the mode is told to read in full for the tag semantics, describes CLINICAL-DRIFT as the classic failure of an NHS values round and never gives the token. So the non-technical user who does exactly what layer 1.5 says gets a hard exit-1 on the tag designed for them, and the only way to pass is to guess a word that appears nowhere in the documentation. Note the asymmetry inside check_mock itself: ROUND-TYPE is validated against a closed set (line 109) and MARKET against a closed set (line 113), while FAMILY — equally load-bearing — is checked only for non-emptiness (line 118).
finding.why_nothing_reports_it: test_check_mock_core.py:207 pins only the FIRING direction: it puts tag=NO-NEXT-STEP into the fixture, whose FAMILY is `ml-engineering`, and asserts TAG_NOT_APPLICABLE appears. There is no test anywhere that a sales or clinical round emitting its own tag passes — so the suite pins the cry-wolf case and has literally never exercised the quiet one. This is the same shape as the disclaimer-paraphrase defect this repo already fixed: the test enforces the drift rather than merely missing it. test_interview_shapes_doc.py cross-checks the tag NAMES between mock_vocab.py and interview-shapes.md but never the family VALUES, so the one automated doc/code consistency check in the mode steps around exactly this field.

FAMILY: 'Clinical / licensed healthcare'   -> ['TAG_NOT_APPLICABLE: MOCK-ASSESSMENT-V1 line 5: CLINICAL-DRIFT applies only to family clinical, this round is FAMILY: clinical / licensed healthcare']
FAMILY: 'nursing'                          -> ['TAG_NOT_APPLICABLE: ...']
FAMILY: 'clinical-nursing'                 -> ['TAG_NOT_APPLICABLE: ...']

$ python3 repro_sales.py
FAMILY: 'sales'                          CLI exit=0 -> clean
FAMILY: 'Sales / business development'   CLI exit=1 -> ['TAG_NOT_APPLICABLE: MOCK-ASSESSMENT-V1 line 5: NO-NEXT-STEP applies only to family sales, this round is FAMILY: sales / business development']

(Only the FAMILY header text differs between the passing and failing runs. 'Sales / business development' and 'Clinical / licensed healthcare' are verbatim the headings of references/role-families.md §1 and §2.)
finding.fix: Make the family vocabulary closed and visible: add FAMILY_KEYS to scripts/mock_vocab.py enumerating the nine slugs (clinical, sales, trades, legal, finance, public_sector, creative, education, hospitality) plus an `other` token, have check_mock.py:118 emit UNKNOWN_FAMILY against it exactly as it already does for ROUND-TYPE and MARKET, print the slug beside each heading in references/role-families.md and in the modes/interview.md:34 list, change the modes/interview.md:242 example off `ml-engineering` (or add it to the set), and extend scripts/tests/test_interview_shapes_doc.py to assert every FAMILY_KEYS slug is findable in role-families.md. Then add the missing quiet-case tests: a sales round emitting NO-NEXT-STEP and a clinical round emitting CLINICAL-DRIFT must both pass.

verdicts.verdict:
## VERDICT: STANDS-WITH-LOWER-SEVERITY (high → medium)

Both reproductions run exactly as reported, from the repo's own passing fixture:

```
$ python3 .../repro_nurse2.py
FAMILY: 'clinical'                        -> clean  (all findings: [])
FAMILY: 'Clinical / licensed healthcare'  -> ['TAG_NOT_APPLICABLE: MOCK-ASSESSMENT-V1 line 5: CLINICAL-DRIFT applies only to family clinical, this round is FAMILY: clinical / licensed healthcare']
FAMILY: 'nursing'                         -> ['TAG_NOT_APPLICABLE: ...']
FAMILY: 'clinical-nursing'                -> ['TAG_NOT_APPLICABLE: ...']

$ python3 .../repro_sales.py
FAMILY: 'sales'                           CLI exit=0 -> clean
FAMILY: 'Sales / business development'    CLI exit=1 -> TAG_NOT_APPLICABLE: ... NO-NEXT-STEP applies only to family sales ...

$ grep -rn "FAMILY: sales\|FAMILY: clinical" scripts/tests/
NO TEST anywhere sets FAMILY to sales or clinical
```

The structural half of the finding survives every attempt to knock it down: `FAMILY` is the only header of the four that is checked for non-emptiness while `ROUND-TYPE` and `MARKET` are checked against closed sets (`check_mock.py:109/113/118`); the MARKET analogue has a quiet-direction test (`test_the_same_tag_in_the_dutch_market_is_quiet`, test_check_mock_core.py:201) and the FAMILY one has none; `test_interview_shapes_doc.py` cross-checks tag *names* only (`_first_col_tokens`, lines 48–53), never the family cell; and I found **no** recorded limit — the spec mentions role-families once (line 51, a filename list) and plan 4 only restates the dict verbatim at line 365. Not BY-DESIGN.

**But two of the finding's load-bearing claims are false, and they are what inflate the severity.** (1) "The only way to pass is to guess a word that appears nowhere in the documentation" — the token is documented, in the file that actually emits the header: `agents/mock-assessor-transcript.md:55-56` reads `| NO-NEXT-STEP | **FAMILY: sales only** | …` and `| CLINICAL-DRIFT | **FAMILY: clinical only** | …`, i.e. field name plus value, in the same table row the assessor uses to pick the tag. (2) The invoked parallel to the disclaimer-paraphrase defect does not hold: that one *passed* while wrong; this one exits 1 and the failure text names the accepted token verbatim ("applies only to family clinical"), so the gate output is self-repairing. This is a cry-wolf/usability defect, not a member of this repo's dangerous class — unless the model's remediation is to delete the FINDING line (plausible, since `modes/interview.md:229` and the self-check forbid hand-editing the block and the transcript is "never edit"), which would silently drop the one tag that family has. That path is SUSPECTED, not reproduced.

**What the proposed fix gets wrong.** Closing `FAMILY` to role-families.md's nine slugs is the wrong axis and would break the skill's primary use case. `references/interview-shapes.md:86` states it outright: *"This is the interview axis; `references/role-families.md` keeps the CV axis"* — and role-families.md's own opening says it exists for "non-technical and regulated professions", i.e. deliberately excludes SWE/ML/research. The interview-side shape table names families the nine do not contain (SWE, ML eng, quant, research scientist, PhD track, consulting, PM). Under the proposed `FAMILY_KEYS`, every ML/MRI round — the fixture (`mock_fixtures.py:47`), `test_mock_blocks.py:15`, the dry-run fixture `assessment-2.md:10`, and both agent-file examples — is either rejected or forced to `other`, which destroys the field's information and trades a loud failure for an uninformative one. The proposed doc test ("every slug findable in role-families.md") pins that wrong axis and would pass on bare prose words like "legal" and "finance" anyway. The cheap correct fix is smaller: propagate the agent file's exact phrasing (`**FAMILY: sales only**` / `**FAMILY: clinical only**`) into the two rows of `references/interview-shapes.md` that currently say "Sales role-play only" / "Regulated/values interview only" and into `modes/interview.md` §0.2, extend `test_interview_shapes_doc.py` to assert each `FAMILY_CONDITIONAL` value appears in its tag's row (the real doc/code drift, and the check that would have caught this), and add the two missing quiet-direction tests — leaving `FAMILY` open, or matching on token containment, rather than closing it against the CV axis.

findings.title: check_claims matches a claim against the master as an unanchored substring of the whole file, so ten distinct fabrications pass — including credentials the master says are unfinished, expired, or not held
findings.what_is_wrong: check_claims.py line ~175 does `master_text = normalize_term(master.read_text())` — the entire profile.yaml flattened into one lowercase string — and then line ~186 accepts any claim whose normalized term is a raw substring: `if len(key) < 2 or key in master_text: continue`. The docstring one screen above says the opposite: "each is a string that compares exactly." It does not compare exactly and it does not compare against fields; it compares against bytes. Four consequences, each reproduced separately. (a) NEGATION: a master bullet reading "Not yet used: Kubernetes, Terraform, AWS. Planned for next year." licenses `skills.technical: [Kubernetes]`. The one line in the profile that says the candidate does NOT have the skill is the line that sources it. (b) QUALIFIER-STRIPPING: master `degree: "MSc in Applied Physics (in progress, expected 2027)"` licenses tailored `degree: "MSc in Applied Physics"`, and `certifications: ["AWS Cloud Practitioner (expired 2023)"]` licenses `"AWS Cloud Practitioner"`. Dropping the parenthetical is the entire fabrication, and a prefix is always a substring. (c) URLs: `github: "github.com/janedoe/pytorch-cine-recon"` licenses the skill "PyTorch". (d) SUB-WORD: "Go" is a substring of "algorithms", so a candidate whose summary mentions algorithms may claim Go.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: check_claims IS the gate for this, and it is the only one — no other script scans tailored-profile.yaml for provenance (grep for `publications|awards` across scripts/ hits only render_cv.py). The test suite does not merely miss the substring behaviour, it PINS it: test_check_claims.py::test_a_term_the_master_mentions_only_in_a_bullet_is_sourced is written as the cry-wolf guard — "'PyTorch' appears in a master bullet but not in the master's skills list; firing here would make the gate unusable" — and the only implementation that satisfies it as written is whole-file substring. The design intent (surfacing a term from a bullet into Skills is honest reframing) is right; the implementation grants far more than that intent, and the test cannot tell the two apart. Downstream, check_apply.py only reads check_claims' receipt verdict, and the three judges are LLM agents that never see profile.yaml.

findings.title: An assessment where every knockout row is 'strong' on the strength of unrelated blocks passes with zero findings — and the caveat that would tell the reader so is layer-1 prose nothing checks, while the disclaimer that IS enforced over-promises in the other direction
findings.what_is_wrong: check_evidence_refs.py compares `str(item.get('ref','')).strip() in ids` and nothing else; check_assessment.py §2 asks only whether at least one ref resolves. Neither ever opens the cited block's text. So a row can say match=strong for "Ten years of Rust and a CISSP" while citing a CV block that reads "Ran Slurm jobs on a shared cluster", and a row can say strong for "Board certification in radiology" citing "Built a C++ reconstruction pipeline". The whole assessment passes clean. This is not merely theoretical looseness: on a realistic 1228-character posting the packing produces TWO jd blocks, and JD-002 contains BOTH the knockout "An existing EU work permit. We do not sponsor for this role." AND every nice-to-have AND the benefits line — so the citation cannot even distinguish a wall from a bonus, which is the exact axis (`level` vs `screening`) the requirement table is built on. Both SKILL.md L471-474 and modes/assess.md L149-151 state the honest bound and instruct the model to carry it into the output. Nothing checks that it does. Meanwhile the sentence that IS gate-enforced — DISCLAIMER_ANCHORS, 「不是对结果的预判」 / "not a forecast of the outcome" — continues "Every item is printed with its evidence reference so the denominator can be audited row by row," which invites precisely the belief the unenforced sentence exists to prevent. The reader is told, under gate enforcement, that the citations make the count auditable; the walk-back is optional.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: The instruction 'carry the honest boundary into your output' has none of the three backstops the project's own doctrine requires: no required artifact whose shape proves it was read, no lint code, and no checklist item naming it — modes/assess.md §12 (13 items) and SKILL.md's assess self-check both omit it entirely, while listing the disclaimer, the counts block, the disqualifier ids and the convention verbatim rule. The evidence schema in modes/assess.md §6 is `evidence: [{ref: CV-012}]` with no `quote` field, so there is no place a supporting excerpt could even be recorded, and check_evidence_refs.strip_block_ids actively deletes block ids from every non-table line — meaning the reader sees a bare id in a table column and no block text anywhere. The 900/80 packing that makes a citation nearly non-localising is documented only in evidence_blocks.py's own docstring, which the model never loads.

findings.fix: Two changes, in this order. (1) Make the caveat gate-enforced exactly the way the disclaimer is: append one clause to both disclaimer strings in SKILL.md L412-417 and modes/assess.md L202-207 — e.g. 「引用只保证这句话指向了原文里真实存在的一段，不保证那段话支持这个结论」 / "a reference proves the cited text exists, not that it supports the row" — and add its literal substring to check_assessment.py's DISCLAIMER_ANCHORS so a card without it fails NO_DISCLAIMER. Copy the string, do not paraphrase it (this is the exact drift 9809599 just fixed). Add the matching item to modes/assess.md §12. (2) Close the localisation gap where a program can: add an optional-then-required `quote` to the evidence schema in modes/assess.md §6 and have check_assessment.py §2 verify each quote is a whitespace-squeezed substring of the block it names, emitting EVIDENCE_QUOTE_NOT_IN_BLOCK. That converts 'this id exists' into 'this excerpt exists and the reader can see it', which is the only part of 'supports the row' a program can decide.

findings.title: check_claims scans four field families; render_cv.py ships eleven. Fabricated publications, awards, project roles, employer names and institutions are never looked at
findings.what_is_wrong: check_claims.tailored_terms() walks `skills.*`, `certifications[]`, `experience[].title` and `education[].degree`. render_cv.py's section-label map (lines 43-91, in eight languages) renders `projects`, `publications`, `awards`, `volunteer`, plus `experience[].org` and `education[].institution`. Every one of those unscanned fields is a short atomic string of exactly the kind the docstring says the gate is for — they are not the 'free prose' the docstring deliberately excludes. Confirmed passing with exit 0: a fabricated publication ("Doe, J. (2026). Nature 640, 12-19."), a fabricated award ("Turing Award, 2025"), a fabricated project role ("Staff Engineer, Google Brain"), a fabricated employer (org: "Philips Research" on a candidate whose master says LUMC), a fabricated institution ("ETH Zurich" replacing TU Delft), and a fabricated volunteer role. `certifications` is scanned and `awards` is not, though they are the same shape of credential — the boundary is arbitrary, not the one the docstring describes.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: The docstring's justification ("Free prose is deliberately out: rewording prose IS the skill's job") reads as if it accounts for everything outside the four families, so a reviewer checking scope against the rationale finds no gap. Nothing derives the scanned set from the rendered set, so adding a section to render_cv.py's label map — as someone did for eight languages — never forces a decision about whether it is scanned. test_check_claims.py's MASTER fixture has no projects/publications/awards/volunteer keys at all, so no test can notice their absence, and the full_profile.yaml fixture that DOES have them is only used by the renderer tests.

findings.title: The verbatim-convention gate only inspects ids the model volunteers, and only asks whether the bytes exist somewhere in the file — so an invented market rule, or a paraphrase with the real text hidden in an HTML comment, draws zero findings
findings.what_is_wrong: check_assessment.py §9 iterates `for entry_id in assessment.get('conventions_rendered') or []`. Nothing scans fit-assessment.md for convention-shaped assertions. So a model that writes "在荷兰，公司必须是 IND 认可的担保方才能为你申请许可；没有这个资质的公司一律不要投" in prose and leaves conventions_rendered empty — or omits the key — produces zero findings, exit 0. That is exactly the failure check_assessment's own docstring claims to close ("a convention restated by the model is how a 'usually' becomes a 'must' with nothing to check it against") and exactly what modes/assess.md §9 forbids ("You may not author, strengthen or extend an entry ... or invent one"). Second, even for a declared id the check is `_squeeze(text) in _squeeze(markdown)` — presence of bytes anywhere in the file. A paraphrase in the card with the verbatim text parked inside an `<!-- ... -->` comment passes; the verbatim text prefixed with 「这条惯例对你不适用，可以忽略：」 passes; the verbatim text struck through and marked 「已废止」 passes. The gate cannot see framing, and it cannot see whether the reader sees the text at all. Third, modes/assess.md §9 says "Render only entries whose `applies_when` is satisfied" and §12 ticks "`applies_when` was honoured" — but `applies_when` appears in check_conventions.py only in PROSE_FIELDS and REQUIRED_FIELDS (presence lints on the table), never at render time. Rendering a residence-permit convention verbatim to a Dutch citizen passes.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: CONVENTION_PARAPHRASED is named as though it detects paraphrase; it detects absence-of-verbatim, and a paraphrase and the verbatim text coexist happily in one file. Because the loop is keyed on a model-written list, the model's own omission is what disables the check — the failure mode and the detector share a single input. The self-check item "`conventions_rendered` lists their ids" is the only backstop for the undeclared case, i.e. the model remembering, which is the class this project treats as no backstop at all. test_check_assessment.py covers the reflow case and the unknown-id case, both of which require conventions_rendered to be populated, so no test exercises the empty-list path.

The docstring one screen above says the opposite: "each is a string that compares exactly." It does not compare exactly and it does not compare against fields; it compares against bytes. verdicts.verdict:
# VERDICT: STANDS-WITH-LOWER-SEVERITY (critical → high)

The mechanism reproduces exactly — `python3 exp3b_attribute.py` gave me the same line-for-line output, and I confirmed the two lines at `scripts/check_claims.py:175` (`master_text = normalize_term(master.read_text(...))`) and `:186` (`if len(key) < 2 or key in master_text: continue`). It is **not** a recorded limit: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-09-1-migration-and-p0-fixes.md:2711` deliberately records the *scope* choice ("Free prose … is deliberately out of scope") and justifies it, but is silent on how the master side is matched, and nothing downstream catches the consequence (`check_apply.py:43` reads only the receipt verdict; `grep -rn "profile.yaml" agents/` → zero hits, so no judge ever sees the master).

It is in fact **worse than reported on the realistic axis and weaker on the count**. Re-running the same vectors with the repo's *own* canonical master — `assets/profile.example.yaml`, which `modes/apply.md:16` declares "the canonical profile schema" — the qualifier-stripping vector fires on that file's own idiom, and a class the finding never names appears:

```
Languages_Dutch_drops_B1     exit=0  PASS   # master: "Dutch (B1)"  -> tailored: "Dutch"
Languages_English_drops_native exit=0 PASS  # master: "English (native)"
Korean_from_a_YAML_COMMENT   exit=0  PASS   # sourced by line 19: 'Example (Korean)'
Japanese_from_a_YAML_COMMENT exit=0  PASS   # sourced by line 16: 'zh | ja | ko'
cert_Git_from_tools          exit=0  PASS   # credential sourced by a Tools skill
title_Lead_from_projects_role exit=0 PASS   # inflated title sourced by projects[].role
CONTROL_Rust                 exit=1  CAUGHT
```
`master.read_text()` includes **YAML comments**, so the schema's own commented examples license claims — and on a Dutch-market CV (this user's actual case) "Dutch (B1)" → "Dutch" is a material over-claim the model could plausibly make while compressing to one page.

Severity drops because the title's "ten distinct fabrications" is inflated. Five of the ten `PASSED` lines are not this bug: `cc.tailored_terms()` returns `[]` for `projects`, `publications`, `awards`, `summary` and ignores `bullets` — that is the plan-2711 scope decision (explicitly BY-DESIGN for bullets/summary), and those five still pass under any master-side fix. Only five vectors are substring-attributable. Note also a sibling finding in this same run, `check-claims-substring-sourcing`, files the identical root cause at **high**; these need deduping.

## What the finding gets wrong about the fix

- **"The only implementation that satisfies [the cry-wolf test] as written is whole-file substring" is false — the test does not pin the behaviour, it merely misses it.** I patched a copy to a word-boundary match (`re.search(r"(?<![\w+#])" + re.escape(key) + r"(?![\w+#])", master_text)`) and got `11 passed` on `test_check_claims.py` and `795 passed` on the full suite (the only 2 failures are `test_install.py` symlink checks, which fail on any copy). `test_a_term_the_master_mentions_only_in_a_bullet_is_sourced` stays green because "PyTorch" is a whole token in the bullet. The fix is cheap and needs no test rewrite, only additions.
- **But word boundaries alone fix vector (d) and nothing else** — I re-ran all seven vectors against that patched copy and every one still passed. So the cheap patch (which is what the sibling finding proposes) is a trap; the `yaml.safe_load` leaf-parse is the load-bearing part, and it is worth stating that it is what kills the YAML-comment class.
- **`QUALIFIER_STRIPPED` as specified will cry wolf on honest edits.** "A strict prefix/substring of a master leaf but not equal to it" fires on master title `"Senior ML Engineer"` → tailored `"ML Engineer"` (an honest *de*-escalation) and on master skill `"PyTorch Lightning"` → tailored `"PyTorch"`. Given the gate's own doctrine that "a gate that fires on every honest run is a gate nobody reads", it must be narrowed to a trailing parenthetical/status qualifier (`(in progress|expected|expired|B1|planned|…)`), not any substring relation.
- **The URL exclusion list is incomplete**: `projects[].links` (`assets/profile.example.yaml:83`) also holds bare URLs, not just `contact.links`.
- **`NEGATED_SOURCE` is machinery for the weakest vector.** The canonical schema has no field inviting "Not yet used: …", and HONEST-GAPS lives in the workspace tailoring plan (`modes/apply.md:48`), not the master — so (a) is the one vector whose input the schema does not produce.

finding.title: An assessment where every knockout row is 'strong' on the strength of unrelated blocks passes with zero findings — and the caveat that would tell the reader so is layer-1 prose nothing checks, while the disclaimer that IS enforced over-promises in the other direction
finding.what_is_wrong: check_evidence_refs.py compares `str(item.get('ref','')).strip() in ids` and nothing else; check_assessment.py §2 asks only whether at least one ref resolves. Neither ever opens the cited block's text. So a row can say match=strong for "Ten years of Rust and a CISSP" while citing a CV block that reads "Ran Slurm jobs on a shared cluster", and a row can say strong for "Board certification in radiology" citing "Built a C++ reconstruction pipeline". The whole assessment passes clean. This is not merely theoretical looseness: on a realistic 1228-character posting the packing produces TWO jd blocks, and JD-002 contains BOTH the knockout "An existing EU work permit. We do not sponsor for this role." AND every nice-to-have AND the benefits line — so the citation cannot even distinguish a wall from a bonus, which is the exact axis (`level` vs `screening`) the requirement table is built on. Both SKILL.md L471-474 and modes/assess.md L149-151 state the honest bound and instruct the model to carry it into the output. Nothing checks that it does. That much is real and worth one cheap fix.

But the finding's headline scenario is not caused by this gap and is not closed by either proposed change, and its localisation half is a limit the repo already recorded on purpose — commit `11fa76f`, titled *"evidence blocks: record how loose the plausibility bound actually gets"*, measures the same thing on a 1502-char posting ("TWO blocks… the citation resolves, and localises almost nothing… **This is faithful to the port (marketfit packs identically) and the parameters are fixed by the shared contract, so it is a recorded limit rather than a bug to fix here**"). Re-measuring it at 1228 chars re-derives a documented decision rather than exposing a defect, and the same paragraph already prescribes the mitigation ("the requirement row's own quoted wording is what a reader must actually check"), which `modes/assess.md:161` implements as `text: "the requirement in the posting's own words"`.

  --- PROPOSED EVIDENCE_QUOTE gate findings: []
  VERDICT still: strong_apply | knockout rows claiming strong: 2

It buys reader visibility of the excerpt (the already-recorded localisation issue), not one line of protection against the demonstrated failure. Shipping it as the fix for "knockout rows strong on unrelated blocks" would trade a silent failure for a *reassuring* one — a green `EVIDENCE_QUOTE` receipt that reads as verification.
- **"The enforced disclaimer over-promises" is a misreading, not a confirmed defect.** `modes/assess.md:178-180` defines what "auditable" means there — printing each row with its ref "makes the denominator auditable and **lets a reader object to one line rather than to the whole number**" — and SKILL.md L418 scopes it to "every item inside N and K", i.e. completeness of the count, not support for the row. ## VERDICT: DROP — the behaviour is ALREADY-RECORDED, and the §9 contradiction does not survive

The mechanics reproduce exactly (`STRIPPED_ID … line 29`, `check_evidence_refs` exit 0 / verdict `recorded`, `check_assessment` exit 0 / verdict `pass`, sentence rewritten) — but the strip of a block id from **this exact sentence** is a written design decision, not drift: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-09-2-assess-mode.md` L576 — *"Everywhere else — headlines, rationale, the strategy section, the 30/60/90 table's prose cells, **the market-convention standing sentence** — a block id is noise to a reader who never sees the block list, and gets removed. Name the thing itself"* — and L574, *"the drop is the mechanism working, not the assessment failing … so the shipped file is provably clean by the time anyone reads it."* The phrase §9 is accused of contradicting traces to `docs/superpowers/research/brief.md` L379 and plan L2304, where "cites CV blocks like any other claim" is a statement about the claim *class* being traceable to the CV (unlike the convention text, which has nothing to cite), not an instruction to typeset an inline id; the operative rule (§6 and the self-check line) says the opposite, and output that follows it passes — the inverse of the disclaimer bug, where verbatim layer-1 compliance *failed* the gate. "Silently" is also wrong on the facts: the gate prints `STRIPPED_ID: CV-001 appeared in reader-facing prose at line 29; name the thing itself instead` to stdout and stores it in the receipt, i.e. the operator gets the correction and the remedy, it is just not escalated to a build failure.

Two further defects in the finding itself, both run:
- **The order-dependence half is a fixture artifact.** `test_check_assessment.build` pre-writes all five upstream receipts. A real run with `receipts=False` and `check_assessment` first gives `MISSING_RECEIPT` ×5 alongside the `STRIPPED_ID` — exit 1 for reasons unrelated to the id. There is one reachable order, so "fails its gate or gets silently edited, depending on order" is not a real state.
- **The proposed fix is worse than the thing it fixes.** I simulated it on a row carrying an invented `CV-999` next to a resolvable `CV-001`: `check_evidence_refs` drops the ref (`verdict recorded`, findings non-empty), `check_assessment` correctly finds nothing — and the rule "fail on a passing verdict with non-empty findings" evaluates `True`, hard-failing a run the design deliberately lets survive. A `"repaired"` verdict is directly contra-indicated by `check_evidence_refs.py` L21-24 and by `test_the_same_clean_state_never_produces_two_verdicts`. The doc half is also mis-specified: a market-convention stance has no requirement row, so "the citation lives in the requirement table row it belongs to" is unimplementable; the plan's remedy is "name the thing itself".

The only residue worth anything is a one-clause wording nit in `modes/assess.md` L242-243 (make "cites" read as *grounded in*, not *prints the id*) — cosmetic, no gate implications, nowhere near high severity.

finding.title: The two work-authorization consistency notices read fields that no file the model reads defines, and a fabricated citation on those fields is stripped in silence with no ROW_UNSOURCED equivalent
finding.what_is_wrong: consistency.py's NOTICE_WORK_AUTH_CONFLICT and NOTICE_WORK_AUTH_VERIFY are computed from `assessment.get('stated_conditions')` and `assessment.get('declared_work_status')`. Neither field name appears anywhere in SKILL.md, in any modes/*.md, or in any references/*.md — `grep -rln stated_conditions` over the tree hits only the plan doc, two scripts, and two test files. modes/assess.md §4 tells the model to ask the user about work authorization but never says where to record the answer. So the model has no way to know these fields exist, they are never written, `consistency.notices()` returns [] for the work-auth cases, and two of the five notice codes — the two guarding the highest-stakes class in the skill, where the output is a `blocked` verdict about someone's legal eligibility — cannot fire in a real run. Second half: check_evidence_refs DOES walk stated_conditions and drop unresolvable refs, but check_assessment §2's 'at least one resolvable ref' rule covers `requirements` only. A stated_condition citing JD-999 is silently emptied, the gate records verdict "recorded", and check_assessment reports []. The same fabricated ref on a requirement row is caught. A work-authorization stance asserted with no citation at all is the one shape the gate has no opinion about.
finding.why_nothing_reports_it: An empty notice list is what a clean assessment looks like — 'no contradictions found' and 'the fields the detector reads were never written' are byte-identical outputs, and consistency.py records verdict "recorded" either way. test_consistency.py constructs the fields directly in Python, so the detector is well tested against inputs that no run produces; nothing tests that the mode file names the fields the detector consumes. For the dropped ref, DROPPED_REF is printed but lands in a receipt whose verdict is "recorded" (see the previous finding), and check_assessment re-reads the already-cleaned yaml, where the condition now has a legitimately empty evidence list.

verdicts.verdict:
## VERDICT: ALREADY-RECORDED (first half) + DROP (second half) — net: do not file this as a separate finding

**The first half is a verbatim duplicate.** `assess-toplevel-schema-never-landed` (severity `critical`, already in `docs/superpowers/research/2026-08-16-audit-findings.json`) carries the identical claim as its sub-claim (b), with the identical grep, and has already been adjudicated — including an explicit downgrade of (b) to *moderate* because the load-bearing legal-barrier net is not `NOTICE_WORK_AUTH_*`. I re-verified that net independently: `grep -rn 'stated_conditions\|declared_work_status' SKILL.md modes/ references/ agents/` → `exit=1` (fields absent, as claimed), but `modes/assess.md` §4 *does* define where the work-authorization answer is recorded — as a `screening: knockout` row whose `match` is the user's answer (§6), rendered in a `## 硬性阻断项` section, and that is hard-enforced: on a `You must already hold an EU work permit` knockout row at `match: no_evidence` with `stated_conditions` and `declared_work_status` **removed entirely**, `check_assessment.check()` returns `NO_DISQUALIFIER_SECTION: 1 knockout requirement(s) are not met ... a wall the reader is never shown is a wall they walk into`. The mode file's own §4 example row and the test fixture's own default markdown both use the EU work permit as *the* worked example of this path. So "the model has no way to know where to record the answer" is false as written, and `NOTICE_WORK_AUTH_*` is dead redundancy, not the only guard.

**The second half — the novel contribution — should be dropped.** It is unreachable by the finding's own premise: it argues `stated_conditions` is never written in a real run, then reports a validation gap in the contents of that never-written field. Worse, `stated_conditions[].evidence` is read by exactly two call sites (`check_evidence_refs.py:73` which only drops, and `consistency.py:157` which forwards the list to `work_authorization_alignment`, reading only `type` and `stance`) — the ref is write-only data with no consumer and no reader, so dropping it changes nothing observable. And the ref is *not* unconditionally silent: run before the write-mode cleaning pass, `check_assessment` §1 prints `DROPPED_REF: JD-999 in stated_conditions (work_authorization) does not name an existing block` (I reproduced this; the finding's exp5 only tested the post-clean order). The only true gap is "no ref at all", which `check_evidence_refs.py`'s docstring explicitly defends: *"An empty evidence list is not an error: rejecting it discards an honest analysis... Punishing the honest shape and passing the dishonest one is exactly backwards."*

**Also wrong regardless of verdict:** (1) The severity rationale — "the output is a `blocked` verdict about someone's legal eligibility" — misattributes. `blocked` is a verdict the model assigns via `vocab.VERDICTS` (SKILL.md:142); `consistency.notices()` returns advisory dicts whose text is deliberately non-determinative (*"check it with the employer yourself. This skill does not decide anyone's legal eligibility"*), a limit recorded in both the docstring and plan line 1440. (2) The proposed `CONDITION_UNSOURCED` rule has no escape hatch — `requirements` gets one via `match: no_evidence`; `stated_conditions` has no equivalent in the schema, so the rule would fail exactly the honest empty-evidence shape. (3) The proposed test "walk `consistency.NOTICE_CODES` and assert every field each notice reads is named in `modes/assess.md`" cannot be built as described: `NOTICE_CODES` is a bare 5-tuple of strings with no field metadata, so the mapping would be a second hand-maintained list — reintroducing the drift it exists to prevent.

findings.title: Layer 1 orders the model to report a weighted 0–100 coverage percentage every round — the exact number D2 and §9 deleted
findings.what_is_wrong: SKILL.md:156 preserves the ATS screener's coverage formula `(present + 0.5·partial)/total` and manages the collision with prose ("label them distinctly … so the user never sees two unreconciled percentages"). SKILL.md:311 and the self-check at SKILL.md:733 then *require* it: "give the final per-judge verdicts, the ATS coverage % (or `n/a`)" and "All three verdicts and the ATS coverage line, verbatim, each round." modes/apply.md:150 and :152 repeat both. agents/ats-screener.md:38 still computes it and :97 still emits `COVERAGE: <NN>%`. This is precisely what the spec rejected three times: D2 ("不输出任何概率或 0–100 分 … 加权总分同样是假精度"), §9 row 1 ("匹配百分比 … 把 met/partial/missing 压成一个数需要给 partial 一个权重，任何权重都是编的。旧 skill 两个覆盖率公式算同一个 must-have 清单，结果总是不一致，靠散文管着"), and §11 row 8's countermeasure ("count_coverage.py 是唯一产数路径，不存在第二个数与它打架"). SKILL.md:509 asserts that countermeasure in its own gate table — "the only count-producing path; a hand-written second number cannot be reconciled" — 350 lines after mandating the second number.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: `lint_no_prediction.py` bans `%` and would kill this line on sight — but `target_files()` only ever scans `fit-assessment.md`, `shortlist.md`, `cheatsheet.md`, `mock/cheatsheet.md` and `mock/assessment-*.md`. The coverage % is mandated for the chat message and for apply-mode files, neither of which the lint can see, and `check_apply.py` does not require a `lint_no_prediction` receipt. `check_assessment.py`'s COUNT_MISMATCH only checks that `count_coverage`'s block is present, never that a second number is absent. And `test_skill_structure.py` pins the disclaimer, the verdict vocabulary and the banned-word list — but nothing greps layer 1 for the one number layer 1 is not allowed to ask for.

findings.fix: Decide which side of D2 the ATS judge sits on and make layer 1 say one thing. Either (a) keep `COVERAGE` as an internal judge signal and delete the user-facing mandate — strike the ATS-coverage clause from SKILL.md:311, SKILL.md:733, modes/apply.md:150 and :152, and rewrite SKILL.md:156 to say the ATS formula is judge-internal and is never shown; or (b) if the user must see coverage, make `count_coverage.py` the one path that renders it as `X of N` with no percentage and change agents/ats-screener.md:38/:97 to report counts. Then add a test in scripts/tests/test_skill_structure.py asserting that no `%`-bearing coverage instruction exists in SKILL.md or modes/*.md, and extend `lint_no_prediction.target_files` (see next finding) so the rule has a gate rather than a paragraph.

findings.what_is_wrong: SKILL.md:507's gate table advertises `lint_no_prediction.py` as firing on "percentages, `n/m` scores, prediction vocabulary (EN + ZH) **in anything rendered**". Its `target_files()` (scripts/lint_no_prediction.py:166-174) resolves to `fit-assessment.md`, `shortlist.md`, `cheatsheet.md`, `mock/cheatsheet.md` and `mock/assessment-*.md`. The same ablation shows `## Interview brief`, `## Modes` and `## Mode entry` are equally undetected — `## Mode entry` is the only place layer 1 gives the `enter_mode.py --workspace <ws> --mode <mode>` command that D11's entire layer-1.5 backstop depends on. findings.title: A discover run can skip check_no_write.py entirely and check_shortlist.py still writes a `pass`
findings.what_is_wrong: §5.1's gate list for discover is `check_shortlist.py` plus "`check_no_write.py` 零命中", and §11 row 12's countermeasure is "闸门写回执 … 下游闸门要求上游回执". assess implements it (`check_assessment.UPSTREAM_GATES` = five names, `MISSING_RECEIPT` on absence) and apply implements it (`check_apply.REQUIRED_GATES`). discover does not: `check_shortlist.py` requires the `mode_entry` record and `adapter_call` records, but never asks whether `check_no_write` ran. D7 is the strongest promise in the spec ("完全只读，无任何写操作") and the read-only guarantee is the one whose violation cannot be undone.
