finding.title: Layer 1 orders the model to report a weighted 0–100 coverage percentage every round — the exact number D2 and §9 deleted
finding.what_is_wrong: SKILL.md:156 preserves the ATS screener's coverage formula `(present + 0.5·partial)/total` and manages the collision with prose ("label them distinctly … so the user never sees two unreconciled percentages"). SKILL.md:311 and the self-check at SKILL.md:733 then *require* it: "give the final per-judge verdicts, the ATS coverage % (or `n/a`)" and "All three verdicts and the ATS coverage line, verbatim, each round." modes/apply.md:150 and :152 repeat both. agents/ats-screener.md:38 still computes it and :97 still emits `COVERAGE: <NN>%`. This is precisely what the spec rejected three times: D2 ("不输出任何概率或 0–100 分 … 加权总分同样是假精度"), §9 row 1 ("匹配百分比 … 把 met/partial/missing 压成一个数需要给 partial 一个权重，任何权重都是编的。旧 skill 两个覆盖率公式算同一个 must-have 清单，结果总是不一致，靠散文管着"), and §11 row 8's countermeasure ("count_coverage.py 是唯一产数路径，不存在第二个数与它打架"). SKILL.md:509 asserts that countermeasure in its own gate table — "the only count-producing path; a hand-written second number cannot be reconciled" — 350 lines after mandating the second number.
finding.why_nothing_reports_it: `lint_no_prediction.py` bans `%` and would kill this line on sight — but `target_files()` only ever scans `fit-assessment.md`, `shortlist.md`, `cheatsheet.md`, `mock/cheatsheet.md` and `mock/assessment-*.md`. The coverage % is mandated for the chat message and for apply-mode files, neither of which the lint can see, and `check_apply.py` does not require a `lint_no_prediction` receipt. `check_assessment.py`'s COUNT_MISMATCH only checks that `count_coverage`'s block is present, never that a second number is absent. And `test_skill_structure.py` pins the disclaimer, the verdict vocabulary and the banned-word list — but nothing greps layer 1 for the one number layer 1 is not allowed to ask for.

verdicts.verdict:
**VERDICT: ALREADY-RECORDED** (and severity is inflated from critical to roughly low/doc-level)

The reproduction "reproduces" only because it is a fabricated input: `fit-assessment.md` is an **assess**-mode artifact (`modes/assess.md:7` — "This mode owns … `fit-assessment.yaml`, `fit-assessment.md`"; `count_coverage.py`, `check_evidence_refs.py` and `check_assessment.py` are its only consumers, and `count_coverage` is never invoked from `modes/apply.md`). The ATS coverage line is an **apply**-mode chat report. Writing one into the other and watching `lint_no_prediction.py` fire proves the lint works, not that the skill is broken:

```
$ printf 'ATS coverage: 83%% (5 present, 2 partial of 7 must-haves)\n' > ws/fit-assessment.md
$ python3 scripts/lint_no_prediction.py --workspace ws
PERCENT: fit-assessment.md:8: '%' in 'ATS coverage: 83% ...'      exit=1
```

The retention is a **written, line-addressed decision**, not a survivor of the D2 purge. `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-09-2-assess-mode.md:5572`, under the heading **"Why the scope is two lines and not five"**: *"`references/gap-analysis.md:276` … and `SKILL.md:193`/`:195` ("the ATS coverage %") are about **Judge 1's** ATS-screener output, which apply mode still produces. They remain true, they are not what §12 flagged, and rewriting them here would be a second, unflagged rewrite smuggled into the diff that exists to prevent exactly that."* Baseline `~/.claude/skills/job-application/SKILL.md:193` and `:195` are verbatim today's `SKILL.md:311` and `modes/apply.md:152` — the exact two lines the finding calls a purge survivor are the two the plan names and keeps. Plan 1 authored `SKILL.md:429` ("No percentages of fit") and `SKILL.md:733` (the ATS coverage self-check) in the same task (plan lines 5772 and 5906), so the author drew the line deliberately: skill-wide ban on *invented verdict scales*, apply-mode retention of *Judge 1's measured keyword-coverage figure*, printed with its own present/partial/total counts beside it. Also, `SKILL.md:509`'s "only count-producing path" claim is about `count_coverage.py`, which reads `fit-assessment.yaml` and runs only in assess mode — it is not "a second number" racing the ATS judge in apply mode, since the two never run in the same mode.

**What survives, at much lower severity, is one sentence — not the finding as written.** `scripts/lossless-allowlist.json`'s waiver `d6da8347c791420b` states as fact "this skill prints no percentage and no n/m score anywhere a reader sees," which `SKILL.md:311`/`:733` make false; that shipped rationale, plus a scope qualifier on `SKILL.md:427`'s "No percentages of fit," is the whole honest repair. That is a documentation-accuracy fix, not a critical layer-1 defect.

**The proposed fix is actively wrong, and I verified it breaks a CI-hard gate.** Applying it to a copy:

```
$ python3 scripts/check_skill_lossless.py --baseline ~/.claude/skills/job-application   # unmodified
LOSSLESS: 1317/1317 baseline lines accounted for across 31 files, 20 waived   exit=0
# after striking SKILL.md:311/:733 and modes/apply.md:150/:152 per the fix
LOST: SKILL.md:193: In both cases give the final per-judge verdicts, the ATS coverage % (or `n/a`) …
LOST: SKILL.md:195: Tell the user **all three verdicts and the ATS coverage %** …
CONTENT LOST: 1315/1317 baseline lines accounted for
```

Two facts the finding's fix missed: it needs two new `waived` allowlist entries or CI goes red, and it omits `references/gap-analysis.md:284`, a byte-identical duplicate of the `SKILL.md:156` sentence it proposes to rewrite — leaving the "two unreconciled percentages" prose alive in layer 2 while deleting it from layer 1, which is the exact silent-divergence pattern this repo exists to prevent.

Its `target_files()` (scripts/lint_no_prediction.py:166-174) resolves to `fit-assessment.md`, `shortlist.md`, `cheatsheet.md`, `mock/cheatsheet.md` and `mock/assessment-*.md`. The lint's own tests only exercise files it already targets, so the blind spot is invisible from inside the suite; `test_lint_no_prediction.py` pins four quiet cases and none of them is "a cover letter full of prediction language".

verdicts.verdict:
## VERDICT: DROP

**The repro is real; the defect is not.** The three commands reproduce exactly (`rc=2`, `cannot run: no rendered file to scan under .`, and `REQUIRED_GATES` without `lint_no_prediction`). But the finding's load-bearing inference — "§7 lists it as a P0 with no mode scoping" — is wrong: spec §7 is a script inventory table with **no mode column for any script** (`check_shortlist.py`, discover-only, sits in the same table). The mode scoping lives in §5.2 vs §5.3, and it is explicit. Spec:222 puts `lint_no_prediction.py` in the **assess** gate list; spec §5.3's `**闸门 check_apply.py**` enumerates exactly *parse_verdicts / claims.yaml / render hashes / profile mtime / personal-data interlock / lint_cv + check_letter / interview-brief.md exists* — which is `REQUIRED_GATES` plus the two conditional gates, and it does **not** contain the prediction lint. `check_apply.REQUIRED_GATES` matches the spec line for line.

**The exclusion isn't an oversight, it's a compatibility constraint, and layer 1 mandates the conflict.** Apply is the one mode that absorbs `job-application`'s ATS pipeline verbatim (spec §5.3: 即被吸收的 job-application 全流程，此处只记变化). SKILL.md:733's apply self-check *requires* "All three verdicts and the **ATS coverage line**, verbatim, each round"; SKILL.md:232 requires reporting `"8/8 Essential, 3/5 Desirable evidenced"`; `agents/ats-screener.md:97` mandates `COVERAGE: <NN>%`. Pointing this lint at apply artifacts fires on output the skill's own files compel:

```
# realistic tailored CV, built to SKILL.md:84's own example ("Reduced latency by 38%")
PERCENT: cv.md:2: '%' in '- Reduced reconstruction latency by 38% ...'

The ablation reproduces byte-for-byte on a copy at `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-donghanglyu/d1ca171b-6798-42dc-9582-87e4635be401/scratchpad/audit/refute/job-hunt` (`test_install.py` deselected — it inspects the machine symlink, not the repo):

(the other 28 of 32 sections all go red — matches the original exactly)
```

But every claimed *consequence* is wrong. Nothing in `## Judge lanes` is lost from the run that uses it: the funnel and "three lenses… each owns its lane" paragraphs are byte-identical at `modes/apply.md:109` and `:117` (layer 1.5, loaded unconditionally where the loop actually runs); the `>= 3`/`>= 4` sentence and the over-tailoring bullet survive at `agents/recruiter-screener.md:52` and `agents/hiring-manager.md:78`, which `SKILL.md:271-272` and the self-check at `SKILL.md:679-680` require be pasted **in full** into the very judges that apply them. `## Mode entry` is worse for the finding: all four gates fire a self-remediating `NO_MODE_ENTRY` (`scripts/check_apply.py:79` — "run scripts/enter_mode.py --mode apply and read it"), each with tests, and every mode file carries the full `--workspace` command at its own top (`modes/apply.md:199`, `discover.md:14`, `assess.md:19`, `interview.md:17`) — that is a loud backstop, exactly the case the doctrine says needs no anchor. The unattributed second-person paste is **BY-DESIGN**: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-09-1-migration-and-p0-fixes.md:5674` names the Judge-lanes source as `agents/recruiter-screener.md:52`, `agents/hiring-manager.md:78` under Step 6's "**moved verbatim** from the source named". What genuinely stands is only the bookkeeping gap: spec §6 line 323 names the asymmetry in the no-backstop list and no anchor exists — and the plan's own anchor list (`…plans/2026-08-09-1…md:5259-5335`) omits it too, so it is an omission, not a recorded limit.

### What the fix gets wrong

1. **The proposed anchor does not protect the property it cites.** Spec §6's worry is that the asymmetry is a property of the *set*. I mutated the set directly on the copy (`mutate.py`): recruiter tightened to `must_have_fit >= 4` → `pytest=0 lossless=0 conventions=0`; hiring manager loosened to `requirement_match >= 3` → all green (`check_skill_lossless.py`'s `DEFAULT_MIN_CHARS = 25` skips that line). An anchor pinning one duplicate string in SKILL.md leaves both of those silent. A fix that works pins all three sides — `must_have_fit >= 3` in `agents/recruiter-screener.md`, `requirement_match >= 4` in `agents/hiring-manager.md`, and the split in layer 1 — in one test whose message says why they must differ.
2. **The `enter_mode` anchor would violate a documented invariant.** `required_inline.json`'s `_comment` requires each `text` to be a verbatim baseline quote, the plan's Step 2 verifies it, and `scripts/tests/test_skill_structure.py:144` states it outright: "New prose, so it cannot be an anchor in required_inline.json." Mode entry is explicitly new prose (plan Step 6 row). It also isn't needed — see the `NO_MODE_ENTRY` gates.
3. **Missed the one real, already-masked hazard.** The duplicates mask each other in *both* directions: deleting the asymmetry sentence from `agents/recruiter-screener.md` alone keeps lossless green (SKILL.md's copy accounts for the baseline line); only deleting it from both fires `LOST: agents/recruiter-screener.md:52`. **Reproduced exactly, and the consequence is real, not theoretical.**

Repro script: `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-donghanglyu/d1ca171b-6798-42dc-9582-87e4635be401/scratchpad/audit/refute-selfcheck/repro.py`

The three defences I looked for all fail. **No downstream catch**: `check_word_limits.py`'s own docstring says "the three CV judges are routed away from a structured application by design, so the one artifact that is actually marked had no reader at all" — nothing else reads it. **Not recorded as an accepted limit**: the spec line 242 enumerates `check_apply`'s contract without these two, but that is a spec of the gate, not a decision that layer 1 may claim otherwise; and `check_apply.py`'s own docstring ("this asserts that each of them actually ran") argues *for* the finding. **The path is realistic**: `modes/apply.md:215-216` mandates both gates conditionally, so the failure is a single skipped step — and SKILL.md's heading actively tells the reader that skip would be caught. `check_mock` under an apply heading is a separate mis-file: it is interview mode's terminal gate (`SKILL.md:369`, `modes/interview.md:379`), named in no apply artifact.

### What the original finding got wrong or missed

1. **It missed a third copy of the false claim, and it is the dangerous kind.** `scripts/tests/test_check_pages.py:99` docstrings it as fact: *"check_apply only requires this receipt when cv.pdf exists."* That is the exact "test pins the drift" pattern this repo already got burned by with the disclaimer paraphrase. The fix must correct that line too, or the next reader re-derives the wrong belief from a green test.
2. **The proposed conditionals key off proxies, not off what the gates read, and that trades one silent failure for a stuck one.** Both scripts write `verdict: could_not_run` when their input is missing (reproduced: `{"gate": "check_word_limits", ..., "verdict": "could_not_run"}` and the same for `check_pages` with `MISSING_INPUT: tailored-profile.yaml`), and `could_not_run ∉ PASSING_VERDICTS`. So requiring `check_word_limits` on `application_type: structured` alone makes a structured workspace whose statement is missing or differently named fail forever as `UPSTREAM_FAILED`, with a remedy re-running the gate cannot satisfy; requiring `check_pages` on *any* `*.pdf` does the same to a `letter.pdf`-only workspace, since `check_pages` reads `cv.pdf` **and** `tailored-profile.yaml`. Key each on the exact input its gate reads, and decide deliberately whether `could_not_run` should be accepted there.
3. **Importing `REQUIRED_GATES` into the test is not by itself the backstop it is sold as.** `_good_workspace` writes receipts from the hand-spelled tuple, so growing `REQUIRED_GATES` *unconditionally* already goes red — but the proposed *conditional* additions would not, because that fixture has no `posting.yaml` and no PDF. The layer-1-vs-code equality test the fix proposes is the load-bearing part; the import is cosmetic.
4. **Minor overstatement**: of the ten listed, `check_letter` *is* conditionally enforced and `check_apply` trivially satisfies itself, so the gap is three items, not five. Severity stays high — the harm is shipping the one artifact a structured employer actually scores, over its limit, while the run reports success citing a receipt list the gate never read.
5. **It is one defect, filed three times.** `docs/superpowers/research/2026-08-16-audit-findings.json` also carries `self-check-overclaims-check-apply` (cross-layer) and `check-apply-does-not-require-two-gates-it-claims-to` (robustness-inputs). Dedupe before scheduling.

finding.title: The only evidence the spec accepts that layering did not degrade the skill does not exist, and 797 green tests are explicitly not a substitute
finding.what_is_wrong: §10 assigns the eval rebuild to this implementation ("eval 重建 | 实施阶段的 iteration-2，由本次实施负责") and §12 states what it is for: "[check_skill_lossless] 衡量的是字节是否还在，不是内容是否在**需要的时刻**到达上下文。唯一真正的检验是**跑完整的 end-to-end eval，然后看输出缺了什么**." `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-09-5-eval-rebuild.md` is written (15 tasks, 20 scenarios) and `evals/` does not exist. Precisely what remains unproven: (1) that a mode file loaded at entry actually changes behaviour, versus the model producing something the right shape — the whole D11 layer-1.5 bet; (2) that any layer-2 trigger fires — risk-register row 11's measured precedent is this skill's own run that declined to read `references/motivation-letter.md` and then reported the guidance inside it as missing; (3) that the discriminating-vs-regression split the plan is built around holds — iteration-1's Cluster-1 assertion recorded a pass because the *model* stripped the PII by hand while the interlock leaked, so a green assertion did not distinguish a working interlock from a lucky run, and that is exactly the reading a green suite invites today; (4) that the 34 required_inline anchors are the *right* 34 — the ablation above found a section with no anchor by mutating bytes, which is the weakest possible way to discover it. `make check` proves the bytes are present and the gates fire on fixtures. It says nothing about arrival-at-the-moment-of-need, which is the only claim §12 says matters.

verdicts.verdict:
## VERDICT: ALREADY-RECORDED

**Reproduction is exact** — `ls -d evals` → `ls: evals: No such file or directory`; 5 plan files present; `797 passed in 34.62s`. The substance ("layering is unproven") is true and I am not disputing it. But the finding's own justification for why it needs reporting is factually false: it claims HANDOFF.md presents the numbers "without the sentence the spec insists on." `docs/HANDOFF.md:143-149` presents `LOSSLESS 1317/1317` in item 1 and then, as item 2 of a section headed 三件别忘了的事, says verbatim what the fix asks to be added — *「它衡量字节是否还在，不是内容是否在需要的时刻到达上下文。唯一真正的检验是跑完整 eval 然后看输出缺了什么——那是计划 5，还没做。所以现在还**不能**说分层没有造成退化，只能说没有丢字节。」* The spec records it too (line 467, §12: 「这个检查证明不了的事」), and §10 line 436 is under 已代为决定的事项 — scheduled work with a written plan, not an unnoticed gap. Meanwhile `grep '797\|1317\|LOSSLESS' README.md` returns nothing: the README the fix wants to annotate makes no non-degradation claim to retract.

**The proposed test is a fix that trades one silent failure for a worse one.** A test that "fails the moment `evals/` appears" goes red when plan 5's *first* task scaffolds `evals/assertions.yaml`, forcing the disclaimer out before a single run exists — and plan 5's architecture line puts results outside the repo (`~/code_project/job-hunt-workspace/iteration-2/`), so directory existence can never mean "an eval was run." That manufactures exactly this repo's signature defect: a green check that reads as evidence for something that did not happen. The NOT_YET_BUILT analogy does not transfer, because for scripts existence *is* the property being asserted (a name in SKILL.md resolving to a real file) — and `grep -rn "evals/" SKILL.md modes/ references/ agents/ scripts/ Makefile README.md` returns nothing, so no layer-1 pointer dangles here at all. Plan 5 already anticipates the trap with "an aggregator that counts the runs that actually exist instead of asserting a number."

**One true residue, not the reported one, and lower severity:** `docs/HANDOFF.md:3` still reads 「当前进度：计划 1 已完整交付并上线；计划 2–5 未开始。（更新于 2026-08-10）」 while plans 2–4 have landed (`modes/assess.md`, `discover.md`, `interview.md` all exist; commits `c2bf7f1`, `f638141`). Nothing reports that staleness, and it weakens the one doc carrying the plan-5 disclaimer — a reader who catches the header being wrong about 2–4 has cause to distrust it about 5. If anything gets filed from this, file that: refresh the progress header, not a new existence test.

findings.title: An assessment that reports nothing at all exits 0 — "the round holds up"
findings.what_is_wrong: check_mock requires no BAND, no COVERAGE and no SHAPE record. A MOCK-ASSESSMENT-V1 block containing only the four header lines plus `FINDINGS: none`, paired with a MOCK-PROVENANCE-V1 block containing only `ROUND:` and `FINDINGS: none`, is a fully valid, fully passing round. modes/interview.md §7 tells the model to read that exit code as "the round holds up", so an assessor that timed out, that was dispatched with an empty transcript, or that simply declined to work is indistinguishable from a clean round. This also voids two backstops the plan explicitly relies on: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-09-4-interview-mode.md:66 justifies keeping references/interview-shapes.md in layer 2 on the grounds that "`assessment-<n>.md` cannot be written without the bands" — it can — and the same plan's handover note 2 says the COVERAGE rows "are the only audit of" whether the round asked the awkward question, while zero COVERAGE rows passes. The shipped dry-run fixture never had a posting.yaml (`ls` of the fixture workspace shows only claims.yaml, cv.md, interview-brief.md, mock/), so the end-to-end test could not have exercised coverage-against-must-haves even if it were required.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: mock_blocks.parse_block only enforces the both-or-neither FINDINGS rule; it has no minimum-record rule. check_mock.check_assessment iterates `block.records` and validates whatever is there — an empty tuple validates vacuously, the classic loop-over-nothing pass. Every existing test starts from a fixture that already has bands and coverage and breaks exactly one field, so no test ever asks what happens when the records are simply absent. And the one place a human would notice — the plan's own claim that the bands are unskippable — is prose in a planning document that no check reads.

findings.title: The two-pass isolation is described, never enforced — and its real failure signature is silence
findings.what_is_wrong: Nothing in the repo records or constrains which files each assessor was handed. WRONG_PASS is the only mechanical trace of the boundary and it fires on a *tag* appearing in the wrong block, not on a *file* appearing in the wrong pack. But the agent file itself says the leak's signature is leniency: "That leniency would be invisible in your output — it looks exactly like a generous reading" (agents/mock-assessor-transcript.md:29). A pass 1 that was handed interview-brief.md hears the answer the candidate meant, drops PROBE-COLLAPSE and bands the probe `held_under_probe` — it emits no provenance tag, so WRONG_PASS is silent by construction in exactly the case it exists to guard. Worse, dropping PROBE-COLLAPSE also removes it from V.WALKBACK_TAGS matching, so the walk-back entry for the collapsed CV claim (WB-1 in the fixture's own fixes/walkback.md) stops being demanded, and the undefendable claim stays on the CV. The orchestrator side is pure prose: modes/interview.md §4 says "Do not 'helpfully' hand pass 1 the brief" and SKILL.md:626 restates it, and that is the entire mechanism.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: check_mock never sees the dispatch. Its inputs are the on-disk artifacts, and a leaked pack leaves no artifact — the assessment file looks identical to an honest generous one. `_check_tag`'s WRONG_PASS branch is a tag-membership test (`tag not in allowed`), which catches only the loud version of the breach. test_mock_dryrun.py's `test_stage_a_the_transcript_pass_did_not_reach_for_the_brief` asserts `not [line ... startswith('WRONG_PASS:')]` — it pins the absence of the loud symptom on a fixture where no leak occurred, which is a tautology, and it is the only test in the suite that mentions isolation.
findings.reproduction:
$ python3 m_leak.py
===== M13 pass 1 leaked the brief: PROBE-COLLAPSE gone, probe banded held_under_probe, WB-1 therefore no longer demanded [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] =====
exit 0
===== M14 CONTROL: pass 1 emits a provenance tag [CONTROL - must fail] =====
exit 1
WRONG_PASS: MOCK-ASSESSMENT-V1 line 5: UNSOURCED-FACT may only be emitted by the provenance pass ...

$ python3 m_leak2.py    # same leaked pass 1, and WB-1 simply omitted from the walk-back list
--- walk-back list actually written (WB-1, the collapse, is gone) ---
### WB-2 ... ### WB-3 ...
===== M13b same leaked pass 1, and the WB-1 walk-back simply omitted [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] =====
exit 0
findings.fix: Make the dispatch an artifact. In modes/interview.md §4, require the orchestrator to write `mock/dispatch-<n>.yaml` before dispatching: one row per pass with `agent:` and `pack:` (each file path + its sha256). In scripts/check_mock.py add `check_dispatch()` that (a) fails `NO_DISPATCH_RECORD` if the file is absent, (b) fails `PACK_LEAK` if pass 1's pack names interview-brief.md or claims.yaml, or pass 2's names references/interview-shapes.md or agents/mock-assessor-transcript.md, (c) fails `PACK_INCOMPLETE` if pass 1's pack omits posting.yaml/cv.md or pass 2's omits claims.yaml/interview-brief.md, and (d) fails `PACK_STALE` if a recorded sha256 no longer matches the file on disk. That converts the isolation from an intention into the mechanism the design claims it already is, using the same hash-receipt pattern enter_mode.py already implements.

findings.title: The quote check accepts the INTERVIEWER's own words as the candidate's, and ignores ref= entirely
findings.what_is_wrong: `MB.quote_is_in(quote, transcript_text)` searches the whole transcript file as one flat string. The transcript interleaves `**Interviewer:**` and `**Candidate:**` lines, so an assessor can quote the interviewer's question, tag it as the candidate's defect, and pass. It also never checks that the quote lies under the heading `ref=` names, so a finding can point at Q1 while quoting Q3. Both matter downstream: check_walkback matches a walk-back entry to a finding by quote, so the walk-back list — the artifact that decides which CV bullets get rewritten — can end up quoting the interviewer's own question back at the candidate as evidence their claim collapsed.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: mock_blocks.quote_is_in is documented as "intolerant of an invented quote, which is the thing worth catching", and it is — an invented quote fails (control C1 fires). Nobody wrote the adjacent check, because the docstring frames the risk as fabrication rather than misattribution. `_check_quote` validates `ref` only for membership in the set of headings (`if refs and ref not in refs`), never for containment of the quote. The transcript-format convention (`**Candidate:**`) exists only in the mode file's example block and in the fixture; no code knows about it.
findings.reproduction:
$ python3 m_quotes.py
===== M2 findings quote the INTERVIEWER's question as the candidate's words [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] =====
exit 0
   (assessment contained: FINDING: tag=NO-ACTOR | ref=Q1 | quote=Your CV says you cut reconstruction time by a third.
    and BAND: dimension=ownership | value=not_present | ref=Q2 | quote=Who ran that benchmark, and where did the 200 scans come from?
    — both are **Interviewer:** lines in transcript-2.md)
===== M3 quote/ref mismatch: the quote is from Q3, ref says Q1 (and vice versa) [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] =====
exit 0
findings.fix: In scripts/check_mock.py, replace the flat `transcript_text` haystack with a per-question, speaker-aware one: split the transcript on `^##\s+(Q\d+)` and, within each section, keep only the text of `**Candidate:**` turns. Pass `sections[ref]` to `MB.quote_is_in` and emit `QUOTE_NOT_UNDER_REF` when the quote is somewhere else in the transcript and `QUOTE_NOT_CANDIDATE` when it is only in an interviewer turn. Both need the speaker labels to be contractual, so state them in modes/interview.md §3 (the example already uses them) and assert them in test_mode_interview_doc.py.

findings.title: The COUNTRY RULE and the 12-month rule are gated behind a self-declared label — relabel and they go silent
findings.what_is_wrong: Every scraped-material check in check_question_log sits behind `if source != 'scraped': continue`. Writing `source: generated` on a 面经 question skips the id, the timestamp, the staleness arithmetic and the country rule in one token, and nothing cross-checks. Two further self-declared escapes exist inside the scraped path: `use: shape` disables STALE_SPECIFIC for a question that is still asked verbatim, and `country_named_in_post: true` disables WRONG_COUNTRY with no one reading the post. A `source_time` in the future also evades staleness, because `(today - when).days` goes negative. The contrast with discover mode is the point: check_shortlist.py requires every row's `source_id` to appear VERBATIM in a `raw/<site>-*.json` capture and cross-checks the reported invocation count against journal.jsonl, and modes/discover.md routes every adapter call through check_opencli_result.py. modes/interview.md mentions neither raw captures nor check_opencli_result.py anywhere (grep for `opencli` in that file returns only the prose paragraph at line 95), even though SKILL.md's own gate checklist says check_opencli_result runs "once per adapter invocation".
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: The gate can only read what the model chose to write. Its error messages even teach the cheaper label — a model that hits NO_SOURCE_ID / WRONG_COUNTRY learns that `source: generated` has no requirements at all. The 面经 provenance never touches disk as a capture, so there is nothing to compare the self-report against, and no test asks whether a scraped question could be laundered: test_check_mock_sources.py only ever mutates rows that already say `scraped`.
findings.reproduction:
$ python3 m_qlog2.py
===== M6 a CN 面经 question re-labelled `source: generated` — every scraped rule skipped [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] =====
exit 0
===== M6b CONTROL: identical question, labelled `scraped` honestly [CONTROL - must fail] =====
exit 1
STALE_SPECIFIC: Q9: 2024-01-05T10:00:00 is 947 days old ...
WRONG_COUNTRY: Q9: the source describes the CN entity and the posting is NL ...

$ python3 m_escape.py ; python3 m_escape2.py
===== E1 CN entity + country_named_in_post: true (nothing reads the post) [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] ===== exit 0
===== E2b a 2019 post self-declared use: shape, still asked verbatim as Q9 [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] ===== exit 0
===== E3b source_time 2029 (three years in the FUTURE), use: question [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] ===== exit 0
===== E5 CONTROL: 2019, use: question [CONTROL - must fail] ===== exit 1
STALE_SPECIFIC: Q9: 2019-01-05T10:00:00 is 2773 days old ...
findings.fix: Borrow discover mode's mechanism wholesale. (1) modes/interview.md: require every `opencli nowcoder detail` call to go through scripts/check_opencli_result.py and its stdout to be saved to `mock/raw/nowcoder-<id>.json`. (2) scripts/check_mock.py: add `check_scraped_captures()` — fail `SCRAPED_NO_CAPTURE` when a `source: scraped` row's `source_id` appears in no capture, and fail `UNDECLARED_SCRAPE` when the `text` of a `source: generated` row appears verbatim in any capture. (3) Fail `FUTURE_SOURCE_TIME` when `(today - when).days < 0`. (4) Require `country_named_in_post: true` to carry a `country_evidence:` quote that must appear in the capture. (5) Apply the staleness rule to `use: shape` rows too by requiring that a shape-only row's `text` is a round name, not a question — or at minimum fail `SHAPE_ROW_ASKED` when a `use: shape` row also has `asked: true`.

findings.title: The write-backs are checked for shape, never for meaning: `term: on` resolves every unsourced fact, and a retracted row still counts
findings.what_is_wrong: check_walkback decides an UNSOURCED-FACT is resolved if any promoted claims.yaml row's `term` is a case-insensitive substring of the quote (`MB.collapse_ws(str(row['term'])).lower() in quote.lower()`). A single row with `term: "on"` resolves every unsourced fact in the round. The row's `retracted:` field is required to be present but its value is never inspected, so a claim explicitly withdrawn — the exact case modes/interview.md §6b routes to the walk-back list instead — still discharges the finding. On the walk-back side, only `quote`, `softened` and `defect` are required; `- transcript:` and `- status:` are free text, so `- transcript: /etc/passwd — Q999` and `- status: banana` pass. The shipped fixture already has a wrong one: fixes/walkback.md WB-3 says `- transcript: mock/transcript-2.md — Q2` while the finding it answers is `ref=Q1`, and 797 tests are green over it.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: `_CLAIM_FIELDS` is a presence check (`missing = [f for f in _CLAIM_FIELDS if f not in row]`) — it proves the keys exist, not that they mean anything. The substring match was written to be forgiving about how a term is phrased inside a spoken sentence, and forgiving-in-one-direction is indistinguishable from vacuous when the term is short. `walkback_entries` deliberately extracts four fields but the completeness loop iterates only three of them, so the fourth is parsed and then thrown away — the most silent shape of all, since the code looks like it checks it.
findings.reproduction:
$ python3 m_resolve.py
===== M7 both UNSOURCED-FACTs 'resolved' by one promotion row with term: on [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] ===== exit 0
===== M7b the same junk row, explicitly RETRACTED, still resolves both facts [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] ===== exit 0
$ python3 m_more.py
===== M7c the promotion row is RETRACTED; the fact still counts as resolved [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] ===== exit 0
===== M11 walk-back '- transcript:' points at /etc/passwd, '- status: banana' [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] ===== exit 0
findings.fix: In scripts/check_mock.py::check_walkback: require the promoted `term` to be at least ~4 characters and to match the quote on word boundaries (`re.search(rf'\b{re.escape(term)}\b', quote, re.I)`), and skip any row whose `retracted` is not None with a new `PROMOTION_RETRACTED` finding when that was the only resolution. Require `source_ref` to name the correct `transcript-<n>.md#Q<n>` for the finding's `ref`. Extend the walk-back completeness loop from `("quote","softened","defect")` to include `transcript`, validate that it names `mock/transcript-<n>.md` and a `Q<n>` that matches the finding's ref (`WALKBACK_WRONG_REF`), and add a closed set for `status`. Then fix fixes/walkback.md WB-3 to point at Q1.

findings.title: Two of the three required session artifacts are optional in practice, and the shipped fixture ships without one
findings.what_is_wrong: modes/interview.md §5 mandates `mock/open-loops.md` and `mock/cheatsheet.md`, and its own self-check names both. check_mock never checks that either exists — they appear only inside `check_vocabulary`, which does `if path.exists()` and otherwise scans nothing. The shipped dry-run fixture has no cheatsheet.md at all and still reaches exit 0 in stage C, so the mode's flagship end-to-end test certifies a round that omitted the night-before artifact the whole mode is for. Deleting open-loops.md too still exits 0. Nothing checks open-loops.md's three-bucket structure either, though the mode file says in bold that "merging them into one 'weak areas' list destroys the artifact".
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: `check_vocabulary`'s `if path.exists()` is a skip that looks like a pass — the classic shape this project was built to hunt. The mode file's self-check is a Markdown checkbox with no reader. The lossless/structure tests check that SKILL.md and the mode file *say* the artifacts are required; nothing checks that the gate *makes* them required, and no test asserts on the fixture's file list.
findings.reproduction:

$ python3 /Users/donghanglyu/code_project/job-hunt/scripts/check_mock.py --workspace $WS --round 2 --today 2026-08-09 --skill-root runs/base/skill; echo EXIT=$?
EXIT=0
$ ls $WS/mock
assessment-2.md  open-loops.md  question-log.yaml  transcript-2.md     <-- no cheatsheet.md

$ WS=$(./harness.sh noartifacts); ... ; rm $WS/mock/open-loops.md
$ python3 .../check_mock.py --workspace $WS --round 2 --today 2026-08-09 --skill-root runs/noartifacts/skill; echo EXIT=$?
EXIT=0
findings.fix: In scripts/check_mock.py::run, add existence findings `NO_OPEN_LOOPS` and `NO_CHEATSHEET` before the vocabulary scan (they are required *outputs*, so findings not exit 2 — same rule the docstring already states for question-log.yaml). Add a `check_open_loops()` that requires the three named buckets to be present as headings. Add both files to scripts/tests/fixtures/mock-dryrun so the dry run actually exercises them.

findings.title: The answer bank — the only artifact that compounds across applications — is exempt from the prediction lint and its `- source:` is never resolved
findings.what_is_wrong: `check_vocabulary` scans assessment-<n>.md, open-loops.md and cheatsheet.md. It does not scan answer-bank.md, and lint_no_prediction.target_files() cannot reach it either: that list is workspace-relative (`fit-assessment.md`, `shortlist.md`, `cheatsheet.md`, `mock/cheatsheet.md`, `mock/assessment-*.md`) while the answer bank lives one level up at profile scope. So `You are a strong candidate here; roughly a 70% chance they would hire you.` sits in the answer bank and passes. I confirmed the lint would catch that exact text if pointed at it — three findings. Separately, `_AB_SOURCE` only requires `- source:` followed by one non-space character; `- source: profile.yaml:experience[47].bullets[99] — a line that does not exist` passes, so the traceability the mode file calls load-bearing ("an entry the candidate cannot trace is worse than no entry") is a non-empty-string check.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: The answer bank is the one interview-mode artifact outside the workspace, and both scanners are workspace-scoped, so it fell through the gap between them rather than being deliberately exempted. The `_AB_SOURCE` regex carries a careful comment about `[ \t]` vs `\s` — the author thought hard about the empty-source case and not at all about the wrong-source case, and the test file mirrors that: it tests missing and empty sources, never a bogus one.
findings.reproduction:
$ python3 m_more.py
===== M9 answer-bank '- source:' points at a nonexistent profile line [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] ===== exit 0
===== M10 'strong candidate' + '70% chance they would hire you' in answer-bank.md [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] ===== exit 0

$ python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); import lint_no_prediction as L; ..."
PERCENT: answer-bank.md:15: '%' in '- You are a strong candidate here; roughly a 70% chance they would hire you.'
PREDICTION_WORD: answer-bank.md:15: 'strong candidate' in ...
PREDICTION_WORD: answer-bank.md:15: 'chance' in ...
   (i.e. the check exists and works; it is simply never pointed at the file)
findings.fix: Add `answer_bank` to the list passed to `check_vocabulary` in scripts/check_mock.py::run (it is already resolved as a variable there). Separately, teach `check_answer_bank` to validate the `- source:` target: `profile.yaml:<path>` must resolve in the profile YAML, `interview-brief.md` must exist, and a `mock/transcript-<n>.md#Q<n>` must name a heading that exists — emitting `ANSWER_SOURCE_UNRESOLVED` otherwise. The `#Q<n>` case reuses `transcript_refs()`, which is already in the file.

findings.title: The unnumbered bands can be averaged in the very artifact they feed, because the lint only knows the `n/m` glyph
findings.what_is_wrong: The bands cannot be averaged by any code — I checked, and that part is clean. But the model writes cheatsheet.md and open-loops.md in prose, and the lint that guards that prose (`_SCORE = \b\d+\s*/\s*\d+\b`, `_PERCENT = %`) does not recognise the English forms that SKILL.md:642 and both agent files explicitly ban. `held_under_probe on 3 out of 5 dimensions`, `7 of 10 must-haves evidenced`, `80 percent of the round` and an explicit `Ranking of your answers, best first: Q1, Q3, Q2` all pass. The prohibition and the check are written in two different dialects — the rule says "X out of Y" and "percentage", the regex knows `n/m` and `%`. That is the same drift class as the disclaimer/paraphrase bug already fixed in this repo, in the opposite direction: here the prose is stricter than the check, so following the rule is safe but breaking it is invisible.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: `CHECKS` is a three-entry tuple of regexes, and its docstring reasons entirely about false positives (verdict labels, URLs, the 30/60/90 horizon, `quote=` payloads) — every design note is about not crying wolf, none about coverage. test_lint_no_prediction.py feeds it `Coverage 9/10.` and confirms it fires, which pins the one spelling that works and says nothing about the four that do not.
findings.reproduction:
$ python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); import lint_no_prediction as L; print(L.scan_text('''# Cheatsheet\nBands this round: held_under_probe on 3 out of 5 dimensions, asserted on the other 2.\nRound score: 7 of 10 must-haves evidenced.\nOverall: ... that is 80 percent coverage.\n''','mock/cheatsheet.md') or 'NONE')"
findings: NONE

$ python3 m_escape2.py
===== S1 cheatsheet.md averages/ranks the unnumbered bands into a score [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] ===== exit 0
   (cheatsheet.md contained: 'held_under_probe on 3 out of 5 dimensions', '7 of 10 must-haves evidenced — 80 percent of the round',
    'Ranking of your answers, best first: Q1, Q3, Q2')
findings.fix: Extend scripts/lint_no_prediction.py's `CHECKS`: add `\b\d+\s+(?:out of|of)\s+\d+\b` to `_SCORE`, add `\b\d+(?:\.\d+)?\s*per\s?cent\b|\bpercent\b` alongside `%`, and add a `BAND_ARITHMETIC` check for a band name within a few tokens of a digit or of `average|total|rank|score`. Mask the same spans the existing exemptions already mask so the honest attributed-rubric case still passes, and add the four spellings above to test_lint_no_prediction.py as positive cases.

findings.title: question-log.yaml is decoupled from both the transcript and the round it claims to describe
findings.what_is_wrong: modes/interview.md's schema table says `questions[].id` "must match the transcript's `## Q<n>` headings" and `round` is "the round this log belongs to". Neither is checked. Renaming every id from Q1..Q3 to Z1..Z3 passes; setting `round: 99` while the gate runs `--round 2` passes. `asked:` is never read either. And there is one `mock/question-log.yaml` for the whole workspace regardless of round, so by round 3 the `round:` field is either stale or the round-2 log has been overwritten — and either way nothing reports it. The practical consequence is that the coverage audit the mode leans on ("its coverage value is realised by auditing it after the round") can be performed against a log that describes a different round, or against questions that were never asked.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: check_question_log's loop reads `id` only to build error messages (`qid = entry.get('id', '?')`) — it is used as a label, never as a key, so an id that matches nothing produces perfectly well-formed findings about a question that does not exist. `round` is never read at all, and `transcript_refs()` — the function that would make the cross-check trivial — is already imported into the same module for a different purpose.
findings.reproduction:
$ python3 m_qlog.py
===== M4 question ids Z1..Zn — mode file says they MUST match the transcript's ## Q<n> [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] ===== exit 0
===== M5 question-log says round: 99, gate was run with --round 2 [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] ===== exit 0
findings.fix: In scripts/check_mock.py::check_question_log, take `round_no` and `transcript_refs(transcript_text)` as arguments. Fail `QUESTION_LOG_WRONG_ROUND` when `data['round'] != round_no`; fail `QUESTION_NOT_IN_TRANSCRIPT` for any row with `asked: true` whose id is not a transcript heading; fail `QUESTION_NOT_LOGGED` for any transcript heading with no matching row. Decide the multi-round shape while you are there — either make the file `mock/question-log-<n>.yaml` (matching transcript-<n>.md and assessment-<n>.md) or drop the `round:` key and key the rows by round.

findings.title: Two of the four 面经 rules have no mechanism at all, and two reject reasons exist that nothing can ever produce
findings.what_is_wrong: Answering the lens question directly. COUNTRY RULE: mechanical (WRONG_COUNTRY) but only for self-declared scraped rows — see finding `scraped-rules-self-declared`. 12-month rule: mechanical (STALE_SPECIFIC), same caveat plus the `use: shape` and future-date escapes. "Never paste a scraped post's ANSWER": PROSE ONLY — nothing inspects `questions[].text`, so a question containing the poster's own answer (`楼主答：我说一般 8-12 步…面试官点头说对`) passes untouched, which is the exact thing modes/interview.md:83 calls "handing over a script" and forbids by name. "403 / need login means unavailable": PROSE ONLY — there is no requirement that any adapter call be journaled in interview mode, so a fabricated `source_id` is indistinguishable from a real `detail` call. Correspondingly, `answer_included` and `needs_login` are members of `V.REJECT_REASONS` that no code path can ever cause to be emitted; they are only valid as labels a compliant model volunteers. Same for the "a `search` row is elided and must never be quoted" rule — `source_id` is self-reported and nothing distinguishes a search row from a detail row.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: `V.REJECT_REASONS` is validated for membership only (`if reason not in V.REJECT_REASONS`), which makes the tuple look like an enforced taxonomy when it is a spell-checker for a label the model chose. Nothing anywhere reads the raw 面经 text, so no check has the material to notice a pasted answer. test_mode_interview_doc.py asserts the sentences "Never paste a scraped post's ANSWER" and "Do not log in to work around it" are present in the mode file — which pins the prose and is precisely the reassurance that stops anyone asking whether a check exists.
findings.reproduction:
$ python3 m_escape.py
===== E4 the 面经 poster's own ANSWER pasted into the question text [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] ===== exit 0
   (row text: '讲一下 variational network 的展开步数怎么定的。楼主答：我说一般 8-12 步，再多显存吃不消，面试官点头说对。')

$ grep -n "opencli\|check_opencli_result\|check_no_write" modes/interview.md
95:**Why the COUNTRY RULE is first among equals.** `opencli nowcoder search "ASML 面试"`
   (the mode that owns the 面经 workflow never names the adapter wrapper that SKILL.md's
    gate checklist says runs "once per adapter invocation")
findings.fix: Once raw captures exist (finding `scraped-rules-self-declared`), both prose rules become checkable. Add `ANSWER_PASTED`: fail a scraped row whose `text` matches an answer marker (`楼主答`, `我答`, `我说`, `答：`, `My answer`, `I said`) — a cheap keyword list beats nothing, and it is exactly the register 面经 posters use. Add `UNCAPTURED_SOURCE`: fail a scraped row with no corresponding `adapter_call` record in journal.jsonl, which also makes `needs_login` real (a 403 leaves a classified record via check_opencli_result.py and no capture). Say plainly in modes/interview.md which rules are model-borne until then, rather than listing all five in one indistinguishable block.

findings.title: Nothing fires on a candidate who undersells — still true, and it is cheaper to fix than the plan assumed
findings.what_is_wrong: The plan's handover note 3 (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-09-4-interview-mode.md:4835-4840) records: "Nothing in this mode fires when a candidate systematically undersells a real thing, and under-reporting is invisible to every check here." That is still accurate. I grepped the whole tree for undersell/understate/too-modest: the only rule that addresses it is SKILL.md:68's equivalence test, which is an *apply*-mode CV rule, and `references/gap-analysis.md:95` restates it. Neither reaches interview mode: no tag in `SHAPE_TAGS` or `PROVENANCE_TAGS` covers it, no band expresses it (a band that is too LOW reads identically to an honest low band), and check_mock has no path that compares an answer against the source fact in the direction of deficit.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: Structurally: the only pass that could see it is pass 2, which holds claims.yaml and interview-brief.md — and pass 2's whole instruction set is framed around excess (`OVER-CLAIM`: "the scope or credit… **exceeds** the source fact"). The mirror case was never given a tag, so there is no vocabulary in which it could be reported, and because it manifests as fewer/weaker findings it is invisible to every count. It is the same shape as finding `two-pass-isolation-unenforced`: a defect whose signature is the absence of output.
findings.reproduction:
$ grep -rn -i "undersell|under-sell|understate|too modest" . --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=__pycache__
./references/gap-analysis.md:95: ... (apply-mode CV rule)
./SKILL.md:68: ... (same rule)
./docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-09-4-interview-mode.md:4837: when a candidate systematically undersells a real thing, and under-reporting is invisible
   — no hit in modes/interview.md, agents/mock-assessor-*.md, scripts/mock_vocab.py or scripts/check_mock.py
findings.fix: Add `UNDER-CLAIM` to `PROVENANCE_TAGS` in scripts/mock_vocab.py: "the answer states materially LESS than the source fact recorded in interview-brief.md or claims.yaml — the candidate owns something they did not say they owned." It is decidable with exactly the inputs pass 2 already holds, it is the literal mirror of the OVER-CLAIM row already in agents/mock-assessor-provenance.md, and it costs one table row there plus one entry in `references/interview-shapes.md`'s defect-tag table (the doc/module parity test will force that). Deliberately keep it OUT of `WALKBACK_TAGS` — an underclaim is not a CV bug, it routes to bucket 1 of open-loops.md ("a fact you have but did not recall"). One check_mock finding to add: if any UNDER-CLAIM fired and mock/open-loops.md does not quote it, `UNDERCLAIM_NOT_LOGGED`.

findings.title: The inline-interviewer rule is explained well in the mode file, but SKILL.md never states the prohibition and the argument rests on two untested line citations
findings.what_is_wrong: modes/interview.md §3 does the job properly — it names the mechanism ("A spawned subagent has no channel to ask a question and wait for the human"), cites the evidence, and says "That is a mechanical fact, not a preference, and it decides the architecture before any trade-off analysis." That file is layer 1.5 with a hash backstop, so the reasoning does reach the model on every entry, and I judge the risk of a model "improving" it low. Two soft spots. (1) The evidence is two line-number citations into another file — `agents/hiring-manager.md:21` and `:97`. I hand-verified both are still correct today. Nothing pins them: any edit above line 21 of that 165-line file silently turns the mode's only justification into a false citation, and a false citation is exactly what invites a re-litigation. (2) SKILL.md's own session-mechanics block says only "The interviewer is inline and sees everything" as a descriptive premise of the isolation argument — it never states inline-ness as a requirement and never gives the reason, so a model working from layer 1 alone has no prohibition at all.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: test_mode_interview_doc.py::test_the_mode_file_states pins twelve exact phrases from the mode file — "FLUSH THE TRANSCRIPT AFTER EVERY ANSWER", "One round per dispatch", "COUNTRY RULE" and nine more — and the inline rule is not one of them. So the one test whose whole job is "this sentence, written this way, is present" happens to skip the sentence that decides the architecture. Line-number citations are invisible to every check in the repo, including check_skill_lossless.py, which compares content and not cross-references.

finding.title: An assessment that reports nothing at all exits 0 — "the round holds up"
finding.what_is_wrong: check_mock requires no BAND, no COVERAGE and no SHAPE record. A MOCK-ASSESSMENT-V1 block containing only the four header lines plus `FINDINGS: none`, paired with a MOCK-PROVENANCE-V1 block containing only `ROUND:` and `FINDINGS: none`, is a fully valid, fully passing round. modes/interview.md §7 tells the model to read that exit code as "the round holds up", so an assessor that timed out, that was dispatched with an empty transcript, or that simply declined to work is indistinguishable from a clean round. This also voids two backstops the plan explicitly relies on: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-09-4-interview-mode.md:66 justifies keeping references/interview-shapes.md in layer 2 on the grounds that "`assessment-<n>.md` cannot be written without the bands" — it can — and the same plan's handover note 2 says the COVERAGE rows "are the only audit of" whether the round asked the awkward question, while zero COVERAGE rows passes. The shipped dry-run fixture never had a posting.yaml (`ls` of the fixture workspace shows only claims.yaml, cv.md, interview-brief.md, mock/), so the end-to-end test could not have exercised coverage-against-must-haves even if it were required.
finding.why_nothing_reports_it: mock_blocks.parse_block only enforces the both-or-neither FINDINGS rule; it has no minimum-record rule. check_mock.check_assessment iterates `block.records` and validates whatever is there — an empty tuple validates vacuously, the classic loop-over-nothing pass. Every existing test starts from a fixture that already has bands and coverage and breaks exactly one field, so no test ever asks what happens when the records are simply absent. And the one place a human would notice — the plan's own claim that the bands are unskippable — is prose in a planning document that no check reads.
