finding.fix: In scripts/check_mock.py::check_assessment, after parsing the MOCK-ASSESSMENT-V1 block, add: `NO_BANDS` if no BAND record is present, and `NO_COVERAGE` if no COVERAGE record is present. Require at least one SHAPE record too, since `cannot_simulate` is the honest output the mode leans on. Add posting.yaml to `_inputs` and to the fixture, and (cheap version) require the COVERAGE row count to be non-zero rather than trying to match must-haves. Then add a `mock/cheatsheet.md`, `mock/open-loops.md` and a posting.yaml to scripts/tests/fixtures/mock-dryrun so the dry run exercises a complete round.

verdicts.verdict:
# VERDICT: STANDS

## 1. Reproduction

Ran verbatim (harness in `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-donghanglyu/d1ca171b-6798-42dc-9582-87e4635be401/scratchpad/audit/refute-empty-assessment/m_empty.py`, copy-of-fixture only, repo untouched — `git status --short` still shows only the pre-existing `docs/superpowers/research/2026-08-16-audit-findings.json`):

```
===== M1 both assessors reported nothing: no BAND, no COVERAGE, no SHAPE, no finding [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] =====
exit 0
===== BASELINE stage C: fixture + walkback + promotion [SHOULD PASS] =====
exit 0
```

It reproduces exactly, and **it is worse than reported**. `m_worse.py` M2 — empty blocks *plus* a transcript with zero `## Q<n>` headings *plus* `mock/open-loops.md` deleted, i.e. an interview that provably never happened — also prints nothing and exits 0. The `NO_QUESTION_HEADINGS` guard is itself gated on `any(block.records ...)`, so emptying the assessment disarms it (control M3, real assessment + gutted transcript, correctly fires 12 findings and exits 1).

## 2. Why it isn't refutable

I looked for the recorded-limit defence and it is not there. The spec says nothing about assessment content; plan 4's three handover notes cover scraped-post reliability, a too-fair persona, and under-selling — none licenses an empty block. Plan 4:66 says the opposite of by-design: `references/interview-shapes.md` is layer 2 "backstopped by … the fact that `assessment-<n>.md` cannot be written without the bands", which M1 falsifies. `check_mock.py`'s own docstring promises "Never a silent skip: a check that did not run must not look like a check that passed" — this is precisely that. No downstream gate reads the assessment (interview mode writes only `mock/` plus two append-only write-backs), and plan 5's eval harness is not landed (no `evals/` on disk), so nothing else catches the consequence. Reachability is ordinary, not exotic: `modes/interview.md` §4's own worked example ships a block that is headers + `FINDINGS: none` and nothing else, so "emit the marker and stop" is a shape the docs demonstrate.

## 3. What the finding got wrong (fix + framing)

- **"an assessor that timed out … is indistinguishable from a clean round" is false.** A timed-out pass produces no block, and that fires `MISSING_BLOCK` (verified: `check_assessment` on an assessment file missing the provenance block returns `['MISSING_BLOCK: MOCK-PROVENANCE-V1 — …']`). The real reachable inputs are the empty-transcript dispatch and the under-producing assessor; drop the timeout example.
- **`_inputs` enforces nothing.** `_receipt` does `if path.exists()` before hashing, so adding `posting.yaml` to `_inputs` buys a receipt hash and zero requirement. If `posting.yaml` is required it belongs in `run()`'s `InputMissing` loop (`for path in (assessment_path, transcript_path)`) or as an explicit finding.
- **A blind `NO_COVERAGE` (rows ≥ 1) trades a silent pass for a fabrication incentive.** `check_mock` never opens `posting.yaml`, so it cannot tell "assessor skipped coverage" from "posting has no must-haves"; a bare count requirement pressures the model to invent a must-have row. The honest version reads `posting.yaml` and requires one COVERAGE row per must-have (with a distinct finding when the file is absent). `NO_BANDS` (≥1 BAND) and `NO_SHAPE` (≥1 SHAPE) have no such ambiguity — `references/interview-shapes.md` yields ≥1 round for every market×family — so ship those unconditionally.
- **Scope the rule to the assessment block only** — the finding does, but flag it loudly: `MOCK-PROVENANCE-V1` legitimately carries only `ROUND:` + `FINDINGS: none`, and that exact shape is `modes/interview.md`:249–252's example and the shipped `mock_fixtures.ASSESSMENT`. A symmetric "at least one record" rule would break the documented clean round.
- **`mock/open-loops.md` already exists in the fixture**; only `cheatsheet.md` and `posting.yaml` are missing. And separately worth splitting out: `check_vocabulary` reads `open-loops.md` and `cheatsheet.md` but never reports their absence, and neither appears in `check_mock.py`'s docstring list of required *outputs* — deleting them changed nothing in M2, while `modes/interview.md` §5 and its self-check both require them.
- **Handover note 2 was never a live backstop to void.** Its "read the COVERAGE rows, and if every must-have came back `evidenced` the round was too easy" instruction exists only in the plan — `grep -rn "too easy" SKILL.md modes/ references/` is empty, and `modes/interview.md` never tells the model to read the rows at all. That is a second, independent gap, not support for this one.

finding.title: The two-pass isolation is described, never enforced — and its real failure signature is silence
finding.what_is_wrong: Nothing in the repo records or constrains which files each assessor was handed. WRONG_PASS is the only mechanical trace of the boundary and it fires on a *tag* appearing in the wrong block, not on a *file* appearing in the wrong pack. But the agent file itself says the leak's signature is leniency: "That leniency would be invisible in your output — it looks exactly like a generous reading" (agents/mock-assessor-transcript.md:29). A pass 1 that was handed interview-brief.md hears the answer the candidate meant, drops PROBE-COLLAPSE and bands the probe `held_under_probe` — it emits no provenance tag, so WRONG_PASS is silent by construction in exactly the case it exists to guard. Worse, dropping PROBE-COLLAPSE also removes it from V.WALKBACK_TAGS matching, so the walk-back entry for the collapsed CV claim (WB-1 in the fixture's own fixes/walkback.md) stops being demanded, and the undefendable claim stays on the CV. The orchestrator side is pure prose: modes/interview.md §4 says "Do not 'helpfully' hand pass 1 the brief" and SKILL.md:626 restates it, and that is the entire mechanism.
finding.why_nothing_reports_it: check_mock never sees the dispatch. Its inputs are the on-disk artifacts, and a leaked pack leaves no artifact — the assessment file looks identical to an honest generous one. `_check_tag`'s WRONG_PASS branch is a tag-membership test (`tag not in allowed`), which catches only the loud version of the breach. test_mock_dryrun.py's `test_stage_a_the_transcript_pass_did_not_reach_for_the_brief` asserts `not [line ... startswith('WRONG_PASS:')]` — it pins the absence of the loud symptom on a fixture where no leak occurred, which is a tautology, and it is the only test in the suite that mentions isolation.
finding.reproduction:
$ python3 m_leak.py
===== M13 pass 1 leaked the brief: PROBE-COLLAPSE gone, probe banded held_under_probe, WB-1 therefore no longer demanded [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] =====
exit 0
===== M14 CONTROL: pass 1 emits a provenance tag [CONTROL - must fail] =====
exit 1
WRONG_PASS: MOCK-ASSESSMENT-V1 line 5: UNSOURCED-FACT may only be emitted by the provenance pass ...

$ python3 m_leak2.py    # same leaked pass 1, and WB-1 simply omitted from the walk-back list
--- walk-back list actually written (WB-1, the collapse, is gone) ---
### WB-2 ... ### WB-3 ...
===== M13b same leaked pass 1, and the WB-1 walk-back simply omitted [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] =====
exit 0
finding.fix: Make the dispatch an artifact. In modes/interview.md §4, require the orchestrator to write `mock/dispatch-<n>.yaml` before dispatching: one row per pass with `agent:` and `pack:` (each file path + its sha256). In scripts/check_mock.py add `check_dispatch()` that (a) fails `NO_DISPATCH_RECORD` if the file is absent, (b) fails `PACK_LEAK` if pass 1's pack names interview-brief.md or claims.yaml, or pass 2's names references/interview-shapes.md or agents/mock-assessor-transcript.md, (c) fails `PACK_INCOMPLETE` if pass 1's pack omits posting.yaml/cv.md or pass 2's omits claims.yaml/interview-brief.md, and (d) fails `PACK_STALE` if a recorded sha256 no longer matches the file on disk. That converts the isolation from an intention into the mechanism the design claims it already is, using the same hash-receipt pattern enter_mode.py already implements.

verdicts.verdict:
## VERDICT: STANDS-WITH-LOWER-SEVERITY (critical → low)

The mechanics reproduce exactly (the finding shipped no `m_leak.py`, so I rebuilt it from its own description — `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-donghanglyu/d1ca171b-6798-42dc-9582-87e4635be401/scratchpad/audit/refute-isolation/m_leak.py`), and the documentation over-claim is real: the spec at line 260, `modes/interview.md:224`, and both agent files all say feeding the passes different inputs "turns the honesty tripwire from an intention into a mechanism", while the dispatch side is prose only and Plan 4's "Handover notes for whoever runs the mode first" (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-09-4-interview-mode.md:4824`) lists three limits code cannot see without listing this one. But **what reproduces is not a leak detector gap — it is the unavoidable fact that no on-disk gate can demand a walk-back for a defect no assessor reported**, and my control M15 proves the check works the instant the tag exists:

```
M13 leaked pass 1 (PROBE-COLLAPSE dropped, probe → held_under_probe), WB-1 omitted  → exit 0
M15 HONEST pass 1 (PROBE-COLLAPSE present),                            WB-1 omitted  → exit 1
    WALKBACK_NO_ENTRY: PROBE-COLLAPSE at Q3 has no '### WB-' entry quoting 'Honestly it might have been closer to a third, I am not sure'
M14 leaked pass 1 that also emits a provenance tag                                   → exit 1  WRONG_PASS
```

A leaked pass 1, a lazy pass 1, and a pass 1 that honestly judged Q3 not a collapse emit byte-identical artifacts, so "isolation" is not the distinguishing variable — assessor recall is.

Two things the finding got wrong. **First, it missed the defence-in-depth.** Pass 2 is *not* leaked in this scenario — what pass 2 is denied is the rubric, not the brief — and its `CONTRADICTED` ("conflicts with the CV, with `interview-brief.md`, or with an earlier answer in this transcript", `agents/mock-assessor-provenance.md:41`) is the same event as most PROBE-COLLAPSEs that matter, and is in `V.WALKBACK_TAGS`. Reproduced in `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-donghanglyu/d1ca171b-6798-42dc-9582-87e4635be401/scratchpad/audit/refute-isolation/m_pass2.py`:

```
M17 pass 1 leaked, un-leaked pass 2 tags the same Q3 CONTRADICTED → exit 1
    WALKBACK_NO_ENTRY: CONTRADICTED at Q3 has no '### WB-' entry quoting 'Honestly it might have been closer to a third, I am not sure'
```

So "the undefendable claim stays on the CV" needs a *second, independent* miss by a pass that was never leaked; it is not a consequence of the leak alone. (Also, `WRONG_PASS` itself is properly tested in both directions at `scripts/tests/test_check_mock_core.py:158` and `:165` — only the *dispatch* is untested, not the mechanism.)

**Second, the proposed fix does not work and would make things worse.** `mock/dispatch-<n>.yaml` is written by the same orchestrator that leaked, and there is no on-disk trace of what was pasted into a subagent prompt (`agents/mock-assessor-transcript.md:15` — "pasted directly below this prompt when you are dispatched"). `PACK_LEAK` therefore fires only when a leaking orchestrator honestly writes down that it leaked — exactly the loud-version-only property it condemns in `WRONG_PASS`, now bought with a new green light reading "isolation verified". All four sub-checks pass in the M13 case by construction. The appeal to `enter_mode.py` is a false analogy: `enter_mode.py:79` calls `journal.sha256_file(path)` itself and `check_mock.check_mode_entry` re-derives it from disk, so that receipt attests something independently checkable; `PACK_STALE`/`PACK_INCOMPLETE` would hash the files the orchestrator *names*, which says nothing about the prompt. The fix that fits this repo's own doctrine is the cheap one: a fourth Handover note plus a wording change wherever "mechanism" is claimed, recording that pass-1 isolation is an orchestrator discipline whose only mechanical trace is `WRONG_PASS`, which catches the loud version only.

finding.title: The quote check accepts the INTERVIEWER's own words as the candidate's, and ignores ref= entirely
finding.what_is_wrong: `MB.quote_is_in(quote, transcript_text)` searches the whole transcript file as one flat string. The transcript interleaves `**Interviewer:**` and `**Candidate:**` lines, so an assessor can quote the interviewer's question, tag it as the candidate's defect, and pass. It also never checks that the quote lies under the heading `ref=` names, so a finding can point at Q1 while quoting Q3. Both matter downstream: check_walkback matches a walk-back entry to a finding by quote, so the walk-back list — the artifact that decides which CV bullets get rewritten — can end up quoting the interviewer's own question back at the candidate as evidence their claim collapsed.
finding.why_nothing_reports_it: mock_blocks.quote_is_in is documented as "intolerant of an invented quote, which is the thing worth catching", and it is — an invented quote fails (control C1 fires). Nobody wrote the adjacent check, because the docstring frames the risk as fabrication rather than misattribution. `_check_quote` validates `ref` only for membership in the set of headings (`if refs and ref not in refs`), never for containment of the quote. The transcript-format convention (`**Candidate:**`) exists only in the mode file's example block and in the fixture; no code knows about it.
finding.reproduction:
$ python3 m_quotes.py
===== M2 findings quote the INTERVIEWER's question as the candidate's words [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] =====
exit 0
   (assessment contained: FINDING: tag=NO-ACTOR | ref=Q1 | quote=Your CV says you cut reconstruction time by a third.
    and BAND: dimension=ownership | value=not_present | ref=Q2 | quote=Who ran that benchmark, and where did the 200 scans come from?
    — both are **Interviewer:** lines in transcript-2.md)
===== M3 quote/ref mismatch: the quote is from Q3, ref says Q1 (and vice versa) [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] =====
exit 0
finding.fix: In scripts/check_mock.py, replace the flat `transcript_text` haystack with a per-question, speaker-aware one: split the transcript on `^##\s+(Q\d+)` and, within each section, keep only the text of `**Candidate:**` turns. Pass `sections[ref]` to `MB.quote_is_in` and emit `QUOTE_NOT_UNDER_REF` when the quote is somewhere else in the transcript and `QUOTE_NOT_CANDIDATE` when it is only in an interviewer turn. Both need the speaker labels to be contractual, so state them in modes/interview.md §3 (the example already uses them) and assert them in test_mode_interview_doc.py.

verdicts.verdict:
## VERDICT: STANDS

Both mutations reproduce verbatim (`exit 0` on M2 and M3), no recorded limit exists anywhere — `grep -i quote` over `docs/superpowers/specs/` returns **zero** hits, and the only prose on the subject is `quote_is_in`'s docstring, which frames the risk solely as fabrication ("intolerant of an invented quote, which is the thing worth catching"). The "the assessor was instructed not to" defence fails on symmetry: `agents/mock-assessor-transcript.md:61` also says "Copy the words; do not paraphrase them" and the repo still spent `QUOTE_NOT_IN_TRANSCRIPT` on enforcing it — misattribution is the same class of assessor error and got no check. I implemented the proposed fix on a copy: it catches all three mutations and passes **795/795** tests (only the two `test_install.py` failures, which are copy-path artifacts present in the unpatched baseline too).

## What the finding got wrong

**1. Its own reproduction does not demonstrate its own downstream claim.** M2 uses `tag=NO-ACTOR` and a `BAND`. `NO-ACTOR` is a `SHAPE_TAG`, and `WALKBACK_TAGS = ("PROBE-COLLAPSE", "OVER-CLAIM", "CONTRADICTED")` — neither record ever reaches `check_walkback`. The walk-back harm is real but needed a separate case, which I built (`harm.py`, `PROBE-COLLAPSE` + `OVER-CLAIM` quoting interviewer lines, with WB entries echoing them):

```
===== H1 WALK-BACK entries built from the INTERVIEWER's own questions =====
exit 0
```

That is the load-bearing repro; M2 should be demoted to supporting evidence.

**2. The fix needs a third code, or it trades a silent pass for a misdiagnosing wall.** `modes/interview.md` seeds each round with a `Persona: Sanne de Vries, …` line and instructs the model to interview in character, so persona-named labels are a live possibility. Relabelling the shipped fixture's turns `**Sanne:**` / `**Donghang:**` and leaving the (correct) shipped assessment untouched gives:

```
exit 1
QUOTE_NOT_CANDIDATE: MOCK-ASSESSMENT-V1 line 5: 'We benchmarked the new pipeline against the old one' is not a **Candidate:** line under Q1
   … 8 findings, all on quotes that are genuinely the candidate's
```

Fail-loud beats silent-pass, but every message names the wrong defect. The fix must emit one `NO_SPEAKER_LABELS` when a `## Q<n>` section contains zero `**Candidate:**` turns, and only fall through to per-quote codes when labels are present.

**3. "The example already uses them" is not a contract** — by this repo's own layering doctrine an example block is exactly the kind of prose that fails silently. The proposed `test_mode_interview_doc.py` assertion is the right backstop; the mode file needs a normative sentence in §3, not just the example at lines 206–211.

**Bonus caution on fix scope:** do not extend ref-containment to walk-back entries without fixing the fixture first. Shipped `scripts/tests/fixtures/mock-dryrun/fixes/walkback.md` WB-3 reads `transcript: mock/transcript-2.md — Q2` while its quote `on about 200 patient scans` is a **Q1** candidate line and the finding it answers is `ref=Q1`. Nothing checks that field, so the fixture ships an already-wrong pointer — independent evidence that ref bookkeeping is unverified throughout, and a landmine for a broader fix.

Reproduction artifacts: `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-donghanglyu/d1ca171b-6798-42dc-9582-87e4635be401/scratchpad/audit/refute-quote-scope/` (`harm.py`, `mutate.py`, patched copy under `repo/`). The repo at `/Users/donghanglyu/code_project/job-hunt` was not modified.

finding.title: The COUNTRY RULE and the 12-month rule are gated behind a self-declared label — relabel and they go silent
finding.what_is_wrong: Every scraped-material check in check_question_log sits behind `if source != 'scraped': continue`. Writing `source: generated` on a 面经 question skips the id, the timestamp, the staleness arithmetic and the country rule in one token, and nothing cross-checks. Two further self-declared escapes exist inside the scraped path: `use: shape` disables STALE_SPECIFIC for a question that is still asked verbatim, and `country_named_in_post: true` disables WRONG_COUNTRY with no one reading the post. A `source_time` in the future also evades staleness, because `(today - when).days` goes negative. The contrast with discover mode is the point: check_shortlist.py requires every row's `source_id` to appear VERBATIM in a `raw/<site>-*.json` capture and cross-checks the reported invocation count against journal.jsonl, and modes/discover.md routes every adapter call through check_opencli_result.py. modes/interview.md mentions neither raw captures nor check_opencli_result.py anywhere (grep for `opencli` in that file returns only the prose paragraph at line 95), even though SKILL.md's own gate checklist says check_opencli_result runs "once per adapter invocation".
finding.why_nothing_reports_it: The gate can only read what the model chose to write. Its error messages even teach the cheaper label — a model that hits NO_SOURCE_ID / WRONG_COUNTRY learns that `source: generated` has no requirements at all. The 面经 provenance never touches disk as a capture, so there is nothing to compare the self-report against, and no test asks whether a scraped question could be laundered: test_check_mock_sources.py only ever mutates rows that already say `scraped`.
finding.reproduction:
$ python3 m_qlog2.py
===== M6 a CN 面经 question re-labelled `source: generated` — every scraped rule skipped [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] =====
exit 0
===== M6b CONTROL: identical question, labelled `scraped` honestly [CONTROL - must fail] =====
exit 1
STALE_SPECIFIC: Q9: 2024-01-05T10:00:00 is 947 days old ...
WRONG_COUNTRY: Q9: the source describes the CN entity and the posting is NL ...

$ python3 m_escape.py ; python3 m_escape2.py
===== E1 CN entity + country_named_in_post: true (nothing reads the post) [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] ===== exit 0
===== E2b a 2019 post self-declared use: shape, still asked verbatim as Q9 [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] ===== exit 0
===== E3b source_time 2029 (three years in the FUTURE), use: question [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] ===== exit 0
===== E5 CONTROL: 2019, use: question [CONTROL - must fail] ===== exit 1
STALE_SPECIFIC: Q9: 2019-01-05T10:00:00 is 2773 days old ...
finding.fix: Borrow discover mode's mechanism wholesale. (1) modes/interview.md: require every `opencli nowcoder detail` call to go through scripts/check_opencli_result.py and its stdout to be saved to `mock/raw/nowcoder-<id>.json`. (2) scripts/check_mock.py: add `check_scraped_captures()` — fail `SCRAPED_NO_CAPTURE` when a `source: scraped` row's `source_id` appears in no capture, and fail `UNDECLARED_SCRAPE` when the `text` of a `source: generated` row appears verbatim in any capture. (3) Fail `FUTURE_SOURCE_TIME` when `(today - when).days < 0`. (4) Require `country_named_in_post: true` to carry a `country_evidence:` quote that must appear in the capture. (5) Apply the staleness rule to `use: shape` rows too by requiring that a shape-only row's `text` is a round name, not a question — or at minimum fail `SHAPE_ROW_ASKED` when a `use: shape` row also has `asked: true`.

verdicts.verdict:
## VERDICT: STANDS

**It reproduces exactly**, from a workspace I rebuilt independently out of the repo's own `scripts/tests/mock_fixtures.py` (one CN 面经 row asked verbatim as Q9, transcript flushed for it) driven through the real CLI — repro at `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-donghanglyu/d1ca171b-6798-42dc-9582-87e4635be401/scratchpad/audit/refute-scraped/repro.py`:

```
===== M6a  CN 面经 question re-labelled `source: generated` [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] =====  exit 0
===== M6b  CONTROL: identical question, labelled `scraped` honestly =====             exit 1
    STALE_SPECIFIC: Q9: 2024-01-05T10:00:00 is 947 days old …
    WRONG_COUNTRY: Q9: the source describes the CN entity and the posting is NL …
===== E1   CN entity + country_named_in_post: true [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] =====           exit 0
===== E2b  2019 post, use: shape, asked verbatim as Q9 [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] =====       exit 0
===== E3b  source_time 2029 (FUTURE), use: question [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] =====          exit 0
===== E5   CONTROL: 2019, use: question =====                                         exit 1
```

I tried three ways to kill it. **Not recorded** — grepping the spec, `docs/superpowers/plans/`, and every script docstring for `self-declar|takes the model at its word|cannot verify|launder` turns up nothing about `question-log.yaml`; spec §267/§285 only ever require that a 面经 row *carry* a `time` and an id, never that the carriage be checked. **Not caught downstream** — `grep -rn "question-log\|question_log" agents/ scripts/check_claims.py scripts/check_evidence_refs.py scripts/count_coverage.py` returns nothing; `check_mock.py` is the sole reader. **The discover contrast is real** — `check_shortlist.py:119` does the verbatim `source_id in text` search over `raw/<site>-*.json` and cross-checks counts against journal `adapter_call` records, while `grep -n opencli modes/interview.md` returns only the prose at line 95.

Two things push me to keep severity at **high** rather than deflate it. The path is reachable by *compliance*, not only evasion: `modes/interview.md:65` positively teaches "scraped material sets SHAPE; generated material sets CONTENT", and nothing anywhere defines which label a reworded, post-derived question takes — so a model that reads the ASML CN 面经 and writes 交叉面 into its own words is following layer 1.5 and labelling `generated` in good faith. And **the finding under-claims its own worst part**: `SKILL.md:504` tells the layer-1 reader that `check_mock.py` catches "a scraped question with no id, no date, or the wrong country", unqualified — that is the sentence that stops a maintainer from asking whether the country rule is conditional on a token the model chose.

### What the finding gets wrong about the fix

- **(5) `SHAPE_ROW_ASKED` is wrong and would break honest runs silently.** `modes/interview.md:111` documents `questions[].text` as "the question as it will be asked"; rows in `questions:` (versus `rejected:`) are the asked set, and a shape row is exactly one whose question was *written from* the post's structure and then asked. Worse, `grep -rn "asked" scripts/*.py` shows no script reads the field at all (only `COVERAGE_STATUS` in `mock_vocab.py` matches), and the fixture's one scraped row carries `asked: false` — so all 32 tests in `test_check_mock_sources.py` would stay green while real sessions began failing.
- **(3) `(today - when).days < 0` cries wolf on the freshest posts.** Verified: `check_mock._parse_stamp("2026-08-10T02:00:00")` against `today=2026-08-09` gives `-1`. nowcoder stamps are Beijing-local (UTC+8) and `--today` defaults to the system date, so a post from a few hours ago reads as fabricated. Needs a tolerance (≥2 days), not `< 0`.
- **(1)+(2) "borrow discover wholesale" is weaker than advertised.** `check_opencli_result.py` records `stdout_file` as a *path* with no hash of its bytes (`grep -n sha256 scripts/check_opencli_result.py` → no hits), so discover's capture chain is friction, not proof; and `UNDECLARED_SCRAPE` (a `generated` row's `text` appearing verbatim in a capture) only fires when the model already saved a capture *and* did not reword — the sloppy case, not the one demonstrated. The prerequisite the fix skips is a **definition in `modes/interview.md`** of which label a post-derived question takes, keyed to content origin rather than wording; without it the capture check has nothing to compare against. `SKILL.md:504` needs amending in the same change.

finding.title: The write-backs are checked for shape, never for meaning: `term: on` resolves every unsourced fact, and a retracted row still counts
finding.what_is_wrong: check_walkback decides an UNSOURCED-FACT is resolved if any promoted claims.yaml row's `term` is a case-insensitive substring of the quote (`MB.collapse_ws(str(row['term'])).lower() in quote.lower()`). A single row with `term: "on"` resolves every unsourced fact in the round. The row's `retracted:` field is required to be present but its value is never inspected, so a claim explicitly withdrawn — the exact case modes/interview.md §6b routes to the walk-back list instead — still discharges the finding. On the walk-back side, only `quote`, `softened` and `defect` are required; `- transcript:` and `- status:` are free text, so `- transcript: /etc/passwd — Q999` and `- status: banana` pass. The shipped fixture already has a wrong one: fixes/walkback.md WB-3 says `- transcript: mock/transcript-2.md — Q2` while the finding it answers is `ref=Q1`, and 797 tests are green over it.
finding.why_nothing_reports_it: `_CLAIM_FIELDS` is a presence check (`missing = [f for f in _CLAIM_FIELDS if f not in row]`) — it proves the keys exist, not that they mean anything. The substring match was written to be forgiving about how a term is phrased inside a spoken sentence, and forgiving-in-one-direction is indistinguishable from vacuous when the term is short. `walkback_entries` deliberately extracts four fields but the completeness loop iterates only three of them, so the fourth is parsed and then thrown away — the most silent shape of all, since the code looks like it checks it.
finding.reproduction:
$ python3 m_resolve.py
===== M7 both UNSOURCED-FACTs 'resolved' by one promotion row with term: on [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] ===== exit 0
===== M7b the same junk row, explicitly RETRACTED, still resolves both facts [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] ===== exit 0
$ python3 m_more.py
===== M7c the promotion row is RETRACTED; the fact still counts as resolved [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] ===== exit 0
===== M11 walk-back '- transcript:' points at /etc/passwd, '- status: banana' [SHOULD BE CAUGHT] ===== exit 0
finding.fix: In scripts/check_mock.py::check_walkback: require the promoted `term` to be at least ~4 characters and to match the quote on word boundaries (`re.search(rf'\b{re.escape(term)}\b', quote, re.I)`), and skip any row whose `retracted` is not None with a new `PROMOTION_RETRACTED` finding when that was the only resolution. Require `source_ref` to name the correct `transcript-<n>.md#Q<n>` for the finding's `ref`. Extend the walk-back completeness loop from `("quote","softened","defect")` to include `transcript`, validate that it names `mock/transcript-<n>.md` and a `Q<n>` that matches the finding's ref (`WALKBACK_WRONG_REF`), and add a closed set for `status`. Then fix fixes/walkback.md WB-3 to point at Q1.

verdicts.verdict:
## VERDICT: STANDS

I could not refute it. All four mutations reproduce verbatim (`m_resolve.py` → M7/M7b exit 0; `m_more.py` → M7c/M11 exit 0), and the control the original auditor omitted confirms the attribution rather than breaking it: with `walkback.md` applied but no claims row, `/Users/donghanglyu/code_project/job-hunt/scripts/check_mock.py` exits 1 on `UNRESOLVED_FACT: ... at Q2 ('I ran it myself on the department cluster')`, so the junk row is genuinely load-bearing — and with no walk-back section at all, a lone `term: "on"` suppresses *both* `UNRESOLVED_FACT` lines, so even the title's literal claim holds. Far from being a recorded limit, the repo records the opposite in three places: `scripts/tests/test_check_mock_walkback.py:158`'s own docstring names this exact failure mode ("a rule that never says no resolves everything, including the unsourced fact nobody actually asked the candidate about") while only pinning the long-absent-term direction; `scripts/check_claims.py:197` raises `RETRACTED_CLAIM` and `scripts/tests/test_check_claims.py:99` pins that a retracted row does *not* source a claim, so `check_mock` implements semantics its sibling script forbids; and `check_claims.py:193` already carries a `len(key) < 2` floor that `check_mock` lacks. Severity survives on the `retracted` half alone, because `docs/superpowers/research/2026-08-09/brief.md:21` makes `claims.yaml` append-only with retraction-by-marking — retracted rows accumulate in real workspaces by design, and any one naming the transcript silently discharges the gate that keeps fabricated facts out of the answer bank.

### What the finding got wrong about the fix

**Items 1–2 are correct and safe** — I implemented them in a copy at `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-donghanglyu/d1ca171b-6798-42dc-9582-87e4635be401/scratchpad/audit/refute-writebacks/repo/scripts/check_mock.py` (min term length 4, `re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(term)}\b", quote, re.I)`, skip rows where `retracted is not None`). They catch M7/M7b/M7c, keep the shipped honest fixture at exit 0, and the full suite stays at `795 passed` with only the two pre-existing `test_install.py` symlink failures that any copy produces. Note `PACS` in the test fixture is exactly 4 characters, so the floor cannot be raised above 4 without editing that fixture.

**Items 3–4 are wrong and would trade one silent failure for a loud false positive.** Requiring `source_ref`'s `#Q<n>` to equal the finding's `ref` assumes a fact is sourced at the question where it was claimed, which the project's own fixture disproves: `mock/transcript-2.md` puts "on about 200 patient scans" in Q1's answer, and Q2 is literally "Who ran that benchmark, and where did the 200 scans come from?" → "The 200 is from memory." A legitimate promotion for the Q1 fact must be allowed to cite `#Q2`.

**Item 5 over-reaches.** `- transcript:` has no written definition anywhere, and the fixture is inconsistent under either reading: by "question containing the quote" WB-3 should say Q1, but by "question where the claim collapsed" WB-2 should say Q3 (the 40% claim dies at Q3), not Q1. Exactly one of the three is wrong either way, so the defect is the undefined convention — define it in `modes/interview.md` §6a first, then fix whichever entry violates it.

**One addition my lens found that the finding missed**, same root cause and more realistic than `term: on`: the `#Q<n>` fragment is ignored entirely, since the only check is `transcript_name in str(row.get("source_ref", ""))`. Taking the shipped honest promotion row and changing `#Q2` to `#Q1` — an ordinary clerical error, not adversarial input — still resolves the Q2 finding at exit 0.

findings.title: `check_apply.py` can never pass an honest stretch — the branch that exists for it is dead, and the one test covering it asserts on a state the program cannot produce
findings.what_is_wrong: `modes/apply.md` devotes a whole section and a required artifact (`honest-stop.yaml`) to the case where the three-judge loop correctly ends un-passed because the candidate genuinely lacks a must-have. `check_apply.py`'s docstring names this as one of its two reasons to exist: "a stretch candidate told 'failed' abandons an application they should have sent." The honest-stop branch is implemented correctly and validates `honest-stop.yaml` properly. But it is defeated twenty lines earlier: `parse_verdicts` is in `REQUIRED_GATES`, and `parse_verdicts.py:189` writes its receipt as `"pass" if combined == "PASS" else "fail"`. So on any REJECT round the required-gate loop appends `UPSTREAM_FAILED: parse_verdicts verdict=fail`, `findings` is non-empty, and `check_apply` exits 1 regardless of how perfect the honest stop is. `check_apply` can only exit 0 when all three judges PASS. My run was a textbook honest stretch (no Go, no Kubernetes, RabbitMQ not Kafka, all correctly refused entry to the CV) and the mode's completion gate reported failure — indistinguishable from a broken run, and the exact signal that makes a stretch candidate bin a good application.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: `scripts/tests/test_check_apply.py::test_a_rejected_round_with_a_complete_honest_stop_passes` builds its workspace with `_good_workspace()`, which loops over every gate in `REQUIRED` and journals each one with `journal.receipt(ws, gate, {}, "pass")` — including `parse_verdicts` — and only THEN overwrites the round file with `rounds.merge_round(ws, 1, {"combined_verdict": "REJECT"})`. In a real run those two facts cannot come apart: the same script writes both. The fixture therefore constructs a `parse_verdicts receipt=pass` + `combined_verdict=REJECT` state that `parse_verdicts.py` will never emit, and the one test guarding the honest-stop path asserts on it. The test is green, the branch is dead, and nothing else in the suite exercises `check_apply` against a receipt `parse_verdicts` actually wrote.
findings.reproduction:
$ cd <workspace>   # honest stretch: judge-round-1.json REJECT, valid honest-stop.yaml, all other gates pass
$ python3 $REPO/scripts/check_apply.py --workspace .
UPSTREAM_FAILED: parse_verdicts verdict=fail (REJECT: ats returned REJECT; REJECT: recruiter returned REJECT; REJECT: hiring_manager returned REJECT)
rc=1

# same workspace, only the parse_verdicts receipt forced to what the test fixture writes:
$ cp -R <workspace> /tmp/applytest && cd /tmp/applytest
$ python3 -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'$REPO/scripts');import journal; journal.receipt('.', 'parse_verdicts', {}, 'pass', [])"
$ python3 $REPO/scripts/check_apply.py --workspace .
rc=0

# the sole finding is UPSTREAM_FAILED; honest-stop.yaml validated fine (classification honest_stretch,
# verdict blocked, reason and evidence present) and interview-brief.md exists.
# Baseline confirmed green: python3 -m pytest scripts/tests -q -p no:cacheprovider -> 797 passed
findings.fix: In `scripts/check_apply.py`, exclude `parse_verdicts` from the receipt-verdict assertion (keep it in the presence check — its `MISSING_RECEIPT` role against a hand-written `combined_verdict: PASS` is the reason it is listed, and that role is unaffected). Concretely: split `REQUIRED_GATES` into `REQUIRED_PRESENT = (..., "parse_verdicts", ...)` and `REQUIRED_PASSING = ("check_personal_data", "check_claims", "check_render_freshness", "lint_cv")`, run the `MISSING_RECEIPT` loop over the first and the `UPSTREAM_FAILED` check over the second. Then fix `scripts/tests/test_check_apply.py`: give `_good_workspace` a `combined` parameter and journal the `parse_verdicts` receipt as `"pass" if combined == "PASS" else "fail"`, so no fixture can build a state `parse_verdicts.py` cannot emit. Add a test that runs the real `parse_verdicts.main()` over three REJECT judge files and then asserts `check_apply.main() == 0` with a valid `honest-stop.yaml`.

findings.title: The claim-provenance gate does not look at experience bullets, so fabricated technologies and a fabricated metric pass every apply gate
findings.what_is_wrong: `check_claims.py` — the only script enforcing SKILL.md's load-bearing rule — scopes itself to `skills` leaves, `certifications`, `experience[].title` and `education[].degree`. Bullets are excluded. But bullets are where achievements and technologies actually live on a CV, and where SKILL.md's own NOT-ALLOWED examples land ("Adding a posting keyword the candidate has no genuine experience with", "Fabricating metrics ('improved performance by 40%')"). I copied three terms straight out of `posting.yaml.keywords` — Kubernetes, Go, Kafka — into `tailored-profile.yaml` experience bullets, together with an invented number, all absent from `profile.yaml`. `check_claims.py`, `lint_cv.py`, `check_personal_data.py` and `lint_no_prediction.py` all exited 0. Secondary, and part of the same hole: `modes/apply.md` — the mode that must CREATE `claims.yaml` — mentions the file zero times. Its six required keys and the closed set `SOURCE_KINDS = ("profile-line", "session-answer", "fetched-artifact")` exist only in `scripts/check_claims.py:39-40` and, partially, in a single example in `modes/interview.md` §6(b) that a later mode reads. A fresh model in apply mode has no documented way to write the file the gate demands.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: The docstring justifies the exclusion — "Free prose is deliberately out: rewording prose IS the skill's job, and a gate that fires on every honest run is a gate people learn to skip" — so tests assert the current scope and pass. But that rationale defends excluding *rewording*; it does not defend excluding *new proper-noun technology tokens*, which is a different and mechanically separable class. Meanwhile the gate's own finding text ("A keyword that appears in the job description is not evidence the candidate has it — source it or move it to HONEST-GAPS") reads as though it covers exactly the case it does not, so a reader who sees it fire on the Skills section reasonably concludes the CV is covered. And the fallback backstop is a subagent: the ATS screener REWARDS the fabricated keywords, and the hiring-manager judge is the only party that might catch it — a model, with no receipt.
findings.reproduction:
$ cp -R <workspace> /tmp/bullettest && cd /tmp/bullettest
# remove the honest Skills additions, add the fabrications as bullets instead:
#   - "Migrated the order-ingestion services onto Kubernetes and rewrote the hottest two in Go, cutting p99 latency by 60%."
#   - "Owned the Kafka event backbone: topic design, schema evolution and replay tooling."
# Kubernetes / Go / Kafka are all in posting.yaml keywords and NONE appears in profile.yaml.
$ grep -n "Kubernetes\|Kafka" tailored-profile.yaml
30:      - "Migrated the order-ingestion services onto Kubernetes and rewrote the hottest two in Go, cutting p99 latency by 60%."
31:      - "Owned the Kafka event backbone: topic design, schema evolution and replay tooling."
$ python3 $REPO/scripts/check_claims.py --workspace .        ; echo rc=$?   -> rc=0
$ python3 $REPO/scripts/check_personal_data.py --workspace . ; echo rc=$?   -> rc=0
$ python3 $REPO/scripts/render_cv.py tailored-profile.yaml --format md --out cv.md
$ python3 $REPO/scripts/lint_cv.py --workspace .             ; echo rc=$?   -> rc=0
$ python3 $REPO/scripts/lint_no_prediction.py --workspace .  ; echo rc=$?   -> rc=0

# control: the same three terms in skills.Practice ARE caught —
# UNSOURCED: "event-driven architecture" appears in tailored-profile.yaml:skills.Practice, ... rc=1
findings.fix: Add a narrow, high-precision pass to `scripts/check_claims.py`: for each token in `posting.yaml.keywords`, if it appears (normalised, word-boundary) anywhere in a `tailored-profile.yaml` bullet AND appears nowhere in `profile.yaml` AND has no live `claims.yaml` row, emit `UNSOURCED_IN_BULLET`. Scoping the trigger to the posting's own keyword list is what keeps the false-positive rate at essentially zero — an honest bullet mentioning Kafka has Kafka in the master too — so it does not become the every-run gate the docstring is right to fear. It needs `--posting` (default `<ws>/posting.yaml`) and should no-op when that file is absent. Separately, add the `claims.yaml` schema — the six keys and the three `source_kind` tokens, written out — to `modes/apply.md` Step 3 next to the claim-provenance checkpoint, since that is the mode that creates the file.

findings.title: `count_coverage.py` reads three top-level fields that appear in no .md file; omitting them silently prints a refusal verdict, and the command as written in the mode file prints the block in Chinese to an English-speaking user
findings.what_is_wrong: `count_coverage.py:104-106` reads `verdict`, `level_direction` and `effort` from the top level of `fit-assessment.yaml`. `modes/assess.md` §6 explicitly claims to own that schema ("This schema is defined here and nowhere else") and documents none of the three; `effort` appears there only as a PER-ROW key, which actively misleads. `level_direction` appears in no Markdown file anywhere in the repo — its only non-test occurrence is that one line of Python. I built `fit-assessment.yaml` strictly from the mode file and got: `投递建议: 证据不足—不出结论` (`insufficient_evidence`) for a posting and CV that were both fully readable. §8 reserves that value as a refusal floor for unreadable input. Second half: both `count_coverage.py` invocations in `modes/assess.md` (§7 line 185 and §11 line 292) omit `--lang`, whose default is `zh`, and §7's worked example is Chinese. `--lang` is mentioned only at SKILL.md:391. So a model following the mode file literally pastes a Chinese counts block into an English UK candidate's assessment — and §7 plus the self-check both demand it be pasted byte-for-byte, so the model cannot fix it by hand without violating the other rule.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: Both defaults are plausible-looking values rather than errors, so the script exits 0 either way. The refusal default is the worst possible one: `insufficient_evidence` is a legitimate state, so the output looks deliberate rather than broken — and it silently contradicts a fully-populated fourteen-row requirement table sitting directly above it. Nothing cross-checks the block against the table. The tests never catch it because `test_count_coverage.py:17` and `test_check_assessment.py:47` hand-write all three fields into their fixtures, so the fixtures supply knowledge the mode file does not, and the passing tests certify a schema no reader can discover. `check_assessment.py` reads the block as an opaque string and has no opinion on the language.
findings.reproduction:
$ grep -rn "level_direction" --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=docs --exclude-dir=__pycache__ .
./scripts/count_coverage.py:105:    direction = assessment.get("level_direction", "unclear")
./scripts/tests/test_check_assessment.py:47:    "effort": "evening", "level_direction": "lateral",
./scripts/tests/test_count_coverage.py:17:    "verdict": "worth_applying", "effort": "evening", "level_direction": "lateral",
# -> zero .md files.

$ # fit-assessment.yaml built from modes/assess.md alone: market + requirements[] only
$ python3 $REPO/scripts/count_coverage.py --workspace .
must-have 强证据：   4 of 8   （partial 2，gap 1，无证据 1）
核心职责已证实：     3 of 6
职级匹配：           不明
可补缺口所需投入：   补不上
投递建议：           证据不足—不出结论      <-- refusal, on a posting and CV that both read fine
rc=0

$ # after adding verdict/level_direction/effort, still the wrong language for a UK candidate:
$ python3 $REPO/scripts/count_coverage.py --workspace .          # exactly what modes/assess.md:185 says
...
投递建议：           硬性阻断
$ python3 $REPO/scripts/count_coverage.py --workspace . --lang en # --lang is nowhere in modes/
apply verdict:                   blocked

$ grep -rn -- "--lang" modes/    -> (none in modes/)
findings.fix: In `modes/assess.md` §6, add the three top-level fields to the documented schema, above `requirements:` — `verdict:` (the five tokens plus `insufficient_evidence`), `level_direction:` (`step_up|lateral|step_down|unclear`), `effort:` (`quick|evening|multi_day|not_closable`, and say explicitly that this is the whole-assessment field, distinct from the per-row `effort`). In §7 and §11 write the command as `python3 scripts/count_coverage.py --workspace <ws> --lang <en|zh>` with the sentence "the block follows the USER's language, not the market's" from SKILL.md:390 carried inline. In `scripts/count_coverage.py`, stop defaulting `verdict` to `insufficient_evidence`: if the key is absent, exit 2 with `MISSING_VERDICT` — a refusal must be written down, never fallen into. Same for `level_direction` and `effort`.

findings.title: Market-convention verification is opt-in from a list the model writes itself, so a fabricated convention card renders with every gate green
findings.what_is_wrong: SKILL.md's grounding contract singles out market tables as "the one class of claim with no citable source" and says they are "whitelisted by id, and rendered verbatim — the model may not strengthen 'usually' into 'must', may not attach a number to it, and may not invent a row." The enforcement is `check_assessment.py:307`, which iterates `assessment.get("conventions_rendered")` and validates each declared id against the market table. It only ever checks ids the model volunteered. It never looks at the rendered `fit-assessment.md` for convention prose it cannot attribute. I replaced a verbatim GOV.UK card with a model-authored paraphrase that strengthens a real rule into an invented one — "UK employers must always demand a share code before interview, and an employer will reject your application if you cannot produce one within 48 hours", sourced to "standard UK hiring practice" — left `conventions_rendered: []`, and `check_assessment.py` exited 0. That text is factually wrong and would materially mislead a job seeker about a legal process, which is precisely the harm the verbatim rule exists to prevent.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: The check is written in the safe direction only: "you declared X, so X must be real and verbatim." The dangerous direction — "there is convention-shaped prose in the reader-facing document that came from nowhere" — has no check at all, and the model is the one who decides whether to declare. `test_check_assessment.py:396` (`test_a_market_with_no_table_is_fine_only_if_nothing_was_rendered`) even encodes the assumption directly: with `conventions_rendered: []` it asserts NO `CONVENTION*` finding fires, so the test suite locks in the blind spot as intended behaviour. Since a fabricating model will not list an id it invented, the whitelist is a self-report and the gate is a formality. `lint_no_prediction.py` also passed on it, because the fabricated card contains no percentage or probability word.
findings.reproduction:
$ cp -R <workspace> /tmp/convtest && cd /tmp/convtest
$ # replace the verbatim uk-right-to-work card in fit-assessment.md with a fabricated one,
$ # leave conventions_rendered: [] in fit-assessment.yaml
$ grep -n "share code before interview" fit-assessment.md
67:> UK employers must always demand a share code before interview, and an employer will
$ grep -n "conventions_rendered" fit-assessment.yaml
146:conventions_rendered: []
$ python3 $REPO/scripts/check_assessment.py --workspace . ; echo rc=$?
rc=0
$ python3 $REPO/scripts/lint_no_prediction.py --workspace . ; echo rc=$?
rc=0

# for contrast, the safe direction does work: declaring an id that is not in the table
# gives CONVENTION_UNKNOWN_ID, and declaring a real id whose text was paraphrased gives
# CONVENTION_PARAPHRASED. Only the undeclared case is invisible.
findings.fix: Make the check scan the document, not the declaration. In `scripts/check_assessment.py`, locate the market-conventions section of `fit-assessment.md` by heading (`## Market conventions` / `## 市场惯例`, alongside the existing `_first_section` helper) and require that every blockquote line inside it be a substring of some `text_en`/`text_zh` in `references/market-conventions/<market>.yaml`; emit `CONVENTION_UNATTRIBUTED` naming the offending line otherwise. Then derive `conventions_rendered` from the ids actually matched and fail with `CONVENTION_NOT_DECLARED` when the declared list disagrees, so the list becomes a cross-check rather than the sole input. Update `test_a_market_with_no_table_is_fine_only_if_nothing_was_rendered` to also assert that a convention-shaped blockquote with an empty `conventions_rendered` DOES fire.

findings.title: The `indeed` adapter ignores `--location` and only serves the US site, and nothing in discover compares a returned row's location to the brief's market
findings.what_is_wrong: For a UK or US target, `indeed` and `linkedin` are the only two of the four adapters inlined in SKILL.md that are not China-specific, and `modes/discover.md` Step 2 says to prefer the no-login one, which is `indeed`. But `--location "London"` returned 11 rows all in Columbus, Ohio, and `--location "Manchester, United Kingdom"` returned Phoenix AZ, Clarksburg WV, Fort Worth TX, San Francisco CA and Oakland CA. The filter is inert for non-US locations. The adapter's own saved metadata says so — `domain: www.indeed.com`, description "rendered DOM via browser session, **US site**" — and `modes/discover.md` even instructs you to save that file to `raw/opencli-help/<site>.yaml`, but nothing reads it and neither SKILL.md's adapter table nor the mode file mentions the restriction. `check_opencli_result.py` returned `classification: ok` for both calls. Then, separately, I put a row with `location: 330 Rush Aly Ste 800, Columbus, OH 43215` and a `why_matched` that explicitly claims "a London-based hybrid role inside brief.locations" into a shortlist whose `brief.markets` is `["uk"]`, marked it `worth_applying`, and `check_shortlist.py` exited 0. A UK user can therefore be handed a shortlist of American jobs with every receipt green — or, if the model correctly drops the rows, be told "no results" when 16 postings were actually returned.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: `check_opencli_result.py` validates exit code, JSON parse, stop-signals and the identity field — an entirely sound set that happens not to include "are these rows from the market I asked for". `check_shortlist.py` never reads `brief.markets` or `brief.locations` at all: `grep -n -i "location|market|geo|country" scripts/check_shortlist.py` returns exactly one hit, `location` as a required field NAME in `REQUIRED_ROW_FIELDS`. The row's `source_id` genuinely appears verbatim in `raw/indeed-1.json`, so the provenance check — the strongest thing in the gate — passes honestly and correctly, because the posting IS real. It is real and irrelevant, and irrelevance is not a shape the gate can see. `why_matched` is required to be non-empty and is never read for content, which the mode file acknowledges ("An invented `why_matched` is the most persuasive part of a fabricated row") without a check behind it. All of this happens on the Anglophone path, which has no `51job` to fall back on.

$ # against brief.markets: ["uk"] and brief.locations: [London, Manchester, Remote (UK)]:

scripts/check_shortlist.py:38:    "id", "title", "company", "location", "salary", "url", "source_site",
findings.fix: Two changes. (1) In `scripts/check_shortlist.py`, add a `_check_market_fit` pass: for every row, if `brief.markets` is non-empty and the row's `location` matches no entry in `brief.locations` and carries no token consistent with any `brief.markets` value, emit `ROW_OUTSIDE_BRIEF_MARKET` naming the row id, its location and the brief's markets. Make it a finding, not a notice — a shortlist row in the wrong country is not a judgement call. (2) In `scripts/check_opencli_result.py`, read the already-saved `raw/opencli-help/<site>.yaml` and, when the command's `domain` is a single-country host (`www.indeed.com`) and the invocation's `--location` names a place outside it, add a `domain_market_mismatch` warning field to the classification JSON with a remedy that says the filter is inert. Add the restriction to SKILL.md's four-adapter table (`indeed` row: "US site only; `--location` is inert for non-US places — measured 2026-08-16") and to `modes/discover.md` Step 2, so the Anglophone path is told before the first call rather than after.

findings.title: `check_mock.py --workspace .` inverts the answer-bank rule: the correct profile-level location fails the gate and the wrong per-application location passes it
findings.what_is_wrong: `modes/interview.md` §5 is emphatic that `answer-bank.md` is "the profile-level file, not a per-application one. It is the only artifact that compounds across applications." I wrote it exactly there. `check_mock.py --workspace . --round 1` reported `NO_ANSWER_BANK: answer-bank.md is missing`. The cause is `_answer_bank_default()`: it calls `paths.answer_bank_of(workspace)`, which requires `workspace.parent.name == "applications"`; for a relative `.` that is `""`, so `ValueError` is raised and the `except` clause falls back to `workspace / "answer-bank.md"` — inside the application directory. Then the destructive half: copying the bank into the application workspace makes the gate exit 0. So under `--workspace .` the gate fails the right layout and passes the wrong one, and its error message is what pushes you from one to the other. `--workspace .` is not an exotic invocation — it is what I used for every other gate in all four modes (`check_shortlist`, `check_assessment`, `check_apply`, `check_claims`, `lint_cv`, `check_letter`, `check_pages`, `check_render_freshness`, `check_no_write`), and every one of them handled it correctly. `check_mock` is the only gate where it matters, and it is the gate guarding the only cross-application artifact.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: The fallback is deliberate and documented — "The fallback covers a `--workspace` that is not shaped like a workspace at all, which is a user error the answer-bank check should report as NO_ANSWER_BANK rather than crash on" — but the premise is wrong: a relative path to a perfectly well-shaped workspace is not a user error, it is the ordinary way to invoke every other script in the skill. Because the fallback resolves to a real, writable path, the gate reaches a definite verdict either way and never signals that it changed its mind about where to look. The tests pass because they build absolute `tmp_path` workspaces, which is the one case the `try` branch handles; no test invokes any gate with a relative workspace. The result is silent state divergence: after a few applications the user has several per-application answer banks and no compounding one, and `check_mock` says the round is clean each time.
findings.reproduction:
$ ls $HOME/.claude/job-profiles/nathan-reilly/answer-bank.md   # the location modes/interview.md mandates
-rw-r--r--  1417  answer-bank.md

$ cd <workspace> && python3 $REPO/scripts/check_mock.py --workspace . --round 1 ; echo rc=$?
NO_ANSWER_BANK: answer-bank.md is missing — the answer bank is the only artifact that compounds across applications, ...
rc=1

$ cp $HOME/.claude/job-profiles/nathan-reilly/answer-bank.md ./answer-bank.md   # the WRONG place
$ python3 $REPO/scripts/check_mock.py --workspace . --round 1 ; echo rc=$?
rc=0

$ rm ./answer-bank.md
$ cd /tmp && python3 $REPO/scripts/check_mock.py --workspace "<absolute workspace>" --round 1 ; echo rc=$?
rc=0
findings.fix: In `scripts/check_mock.py::_answer_bank_default`, resolve first: `workspace = pathlib.Path(workspace).resolve()` before calling `paths.answer_bank_of`. Better, do it once for every gate — resolve `--workspace` to an absolute path in each script's `main()` immediately after parsing, so relative and absolute invocations can never diverge anywhere in the skill. Then replace the silent fallback: when `paths.answer_bank_of` still raises after resolution, emit a distinct `WORKSPACE_SHAPE: <path> is not <profile>/applications/<company>-<role>-<date>, so the profile-level answer bank cannot be located` instead of a `NO_ANSWER_BANK` that sends the reader to create the file in the wrong place. Add a test that invokes `check_mock.main()` with a relative workspace from inside the workspace directory and asserts the profile-level bank is found.

findings.title: Discover Step 5 mandates a detail call that Step 8's gate then flags, and the gate's remedy text asks for a reason that would be a lie
findings.what_is_wrong: Step 5 is unconditional: `indeed` returns empty `title` on every row, so "Recover each row with `opencli indeed job <id>`" — and `check_opencli_result.py` reinforces it, setting `needs_detail_recovery: true` with the remedy "Recover each one". Step 8 caps detail fetches at the top three verdict bands and `check_shortlist.py` enforces `DETAIL_FETCH_OUT_OF_BAND` on `extraction_method: adapter_detail` or `quality: complete` outside them. These cannot both be satisfied, because the band cannot be assigned until the title is recovered and the title can only be recovered by the call the band controls. Every honestly-recorded indeed row that turns out to be junior, wrong-country or off-track fails the gate. The three escapes are all bad: fabricate a `detail_fetch_exceptions` reason, mislabel `extraction_method` as `adapter_search` (a provenance lie in the one file the gate exists to protect), or drop the row (so indeed rows can only ever appear in a shortlist if they happen to land in the top three bands). The gate's message names only the first and phrases it as "If the user named this row" — which was not true in my run. A truthful non-user reason is accepted, so the honest path exists, but nothing in either the mode file or the message tells you it does.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: Nothing is supposed to report it — it is a contradiction between two prose steps of one mode file, and no test compares Step 5's obligation against Step 8's cap because neither is a program. The tests for `DETAIL_FETCH_OUT_OF_BAND` construct the row directly and assert the finding fires, which is correct in isolation and says nothing about whether a run that followed the file can avoid it. The real risk is downstream: the gate rewards a fabricated exception reason and cannot distinguish it from a true one, so the pressure this creates lands squarely on the shortlist's provenance record.
findings.reproduction:
$ # indeed search returned 11/11 empty titles; Step 5 says recover each one.
$ opencli indeed job 88feeb9f4302f917 --window background -f json
{'id': '88feeb9f4302f917', 'title': 'Lead Forward Deployed Engineer, ServiceNow',
 'company': 'Deloitte', 'location': '330 Rush Aly Ste 800, Columbus, OH 43215', ...}
$ # recorded honestly: extraction_method: adapter_detail, quality: partial, verdict: blocked
$ python3 $REPO/scripts/check_shortlist.py --workspace . ; echo rc=$?
DETAIL_FETCH_OUT_OF_BAND: row 5 (id='indeed-88feeb9f4302f917') carries a detail fetch but verdict 'blocked' is outside the top three (strong_apply, worth_applying, stretch). Detail fan-out is the yellow-layer cap. If the user named this row, record it in shortlist.yaml `detail_fetch_exceptions` with a reason.
rc=1

$ # adding a truthful non-user exception reason does clear it:
$ #   reason: "Step 5 identity recovery, not a user request: the indeed search row came back
$ #            with an empty title, so the band could not be assigned until the detail call had run."
$ python3 $REPO/scripts/check_shortlist.py --workspace . ; echo rc=$?
rc=0
findings.fix: Carve identity recovery out of the cap rather than routing it through the exception list. Add an optional row field `recovery_only: true`, set it when the detail call was made solely because the identity field was empty, and skip that row in `_check_detail_cap` (its `quality` stays `partial`, never `complete`). Cross-check it against the journal: only allow `recovery_only` on a site whose `adapter_call` recorded `needs_detail_recovery: true`, so it cannot be used to launder a discretionary fetch. Document it in `modes/discover.md` Step 5 with one sentence pointing forward to Step 8, and in Step 8 with one pointing back. Widen the finding text to name all three resolutions — recovery-only, a genuine user request, or dropping the row into `shortfall_reason` — instead of only the one that requires asserting the user asked.

findings.title: `check_opencli_result.py` classifies a `detail` call that returned an empty job description as `ok`, because it only checks the identity field
findings.what_is_wrong: The wrapper's integrity check is `identity_field` non-empty — `title` for most adapters, `name` for `boss`. That is the right check for a `search` command, where the identity field is the payload. For a `detail`/`job-detail` command the payload is the description, and the identity field is something the caller already had from the card. `opencli linkedin job-detail` returned exit 0 with `title`, `company`, `location`, `workplace_type`, `applicants` and `apply_url` all populated and `description` of length 0. The wrapper reported `classification: ok`, `empty_result: false`, `needs_detail_recovery: false`, `remedy: null`. In discover Step 8 that is the signal used to upgrade a row to `quality: complete` and `verification: fresh_verified` — the strongest confidence labels the shortlist has — on the strength of a fetch that returned no job text at all. `check_shortlist.py` has no way to notice, since it validates the source id against the raw capture and the id is genuinely there.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: This is the same class as the login-wall problem the skill is otherwise excellent about: the mode files and SKILL.md both hammer "a 200 OK is not proof you have the posting", and `modes/assess.md` §1 turns it into a real gate at the model level — which is what saved me here, since I correctly treated the empty description as a blocked fetch and asked for a paste. But that gate is prose, evaluated by the model, and applies to `WebFetch` in assess mode. The adapter path in discover has a program doing the classification, and that program's notion of "did I get anything" was written for search rows. Nothing compares the command kind to the field that matters for it, and the `columns:` list in the adapter's own saved `--help` metadata — which names `description` for both `indeed job` and `linkedin job-detail` — is captured to disk and never read.
findings.reproduction:
$ opencli linkedin job-detail "https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/4386844250" --window background -f json > raw-jobdetail.json ; echo rc=$?
rc=0
$ python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('raw-jobdetail.json'));d=d[0] if isinstance(d,list) else d;print('title=',d['title']);print('DESC LEN', len(d.get('description') or ''))"
title= Senior Backend Engineer
DESC LEN 0

$ python3 $REPO/scripts/check_opencli_result.py --workspace . --site linkedin --command job-detail \
    --exit-code 0 --stdout-file raw-jobdetail.json --stderr-file raw-jobdetail.err \
    --command-line 'opencli linkedin job-detail https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/4386844250 --window background -f json'
{"auth_state": "unchecked", "classification": "ok", "command": "job-detail", "empty_identity_rows": [],
 "empty_result": false, "needs_detail_recovery": false, "remedy": null, "row_count": 1, "site": "linkedin"}
rc=0
findings.fix: In `scripts/check_opencli_result.py`, add a payload field per command kind alongside `identity_field`: for detail-class commands (`detail`, `job`, `job-detail`, and anything whose saved `--help` `columns:` includes `description`), require `description` to be non-empty. When it is empty, return a new classification `thin_detail` with the remedy "the detail call succeeded and returned no job text — this is the adapter equivalent of a login wall; do not upgrade the row to quality: complete or verification: fresh_verified, and ask the user to paste the posting." Then in `scripts/check_shortlist.py`, fire `QUALITY_UNSUPPORTED` when a row claims `quality: complete` or `verification: fresh_verified` while the journal's `adapter_call` for its detail fetch recorded `thin_detail`.

findings.title: `actions:` and `conventions_rendered:` can both stay empty while the document is full, and the only thing that objects is a notice you satisfy by pasting it
findings.what_is_wrong: `modes/assess.md` §10 says of the 30/60/90 and roadmap tables: "Every row of both tables must also appear in `actions:` in `fit-assessment.yaml`; that list is the single authoritative to-do list, and `consistency.py` compares it against the closable gaps." §9 says "List the ids you rendered in `conventions_rendered:`." The self-check repeats both. I shipped a `fit-assessment.md` with a three-row 30/60/90 table, a four-row roadmap and two fully rendered convention cards, against a `fit-assessment.yaml` with `actions: []` and `conventions_rendered: []`, and `check_assessment.py` exited 0. The only objection anywhere was `consistency.py`'s `NOTICE_GAP_ACTIONS: 4 gaps say they can be closed before applying, but the plan lists 0 actions`. That notice is not a failure — it is a notice, and `check_assessment.py`'s `NOTICE_NOT_ATTACHED` requires only that its text appear somewhere in the markdown. So the way to clear the gate is to paste the sentence saying the actions list is empty into the document, next to the tables that should have populated it. The escape from the notice is to print the notice.
findings.why_nothing_reports_it: `consistency.py` is explicitly a reporter, not a repairer, and that design is right and well-argued ("code can see two fields disagree, it cannot see which one is right"). The problem is the composition: `check_assessment.py` turns "was a notice attached" into the whole obligation, so an unrepaired contradiction and a repaired one become indistinguishable at the gate, and the cheaper of the two is the one that leaves the machine-readable to-do list empty. `conventions_rendered` has no notice at all — it is only ever read as an input to the id-allowlist check (see the convention-cards finding), so leaving it empty removes work rather than creating a finding. Both fields are the machine-readable half of the assessment; a downstream consumer reading `fit-assessment.yaml` sees an assessment with no actions and no conventions, while the human reading `fit-assessment.md` sees seven action rows and two convention cards.
findings.reproduction:
$ tail -2 fit-assessment.yaml
conventions_rendered: []
actions: []
$ grep -c "^| " fit-assessment.md    # 30/60/90 + roadmap rows present
$ python3 $REPO/scripts/consistency.py --workspace .
NOTICE_LOOSE_KNOCKOUTS: 5 requirements are marked hard filters. ...
NOTICE_GAP_ACTIONS: 4 gaps say they can be closed before applying, but the plan lists 0 actions — some of the advice above did not make it into this list.
rc=0
$ python3 $REPO/scripts/check_assessment.py --workspace .
NOTICE_NOT_ATTACHED: NOTICE_GAP_ACTIONS fired and its text is nowhere in fit-assessment.md; attach it beside the thing it qualifies
rc=1
$ # paste the NOTICE_GAP_ACTIONS sentence verbatim into fit-assessment.md, change nothing else:
$ python3 $REPO/scripts/check_assessment.py --workspace . ; echo rc=$?
rc=0
$ # actions: [] and conventions_rendered: [] both still empty.
findings.fix: In `scripts/check_assessment.py`, add a structural check independent of the notice: when `fit-assessment.md` contains a `## 那该怎么办` / `## What to do instead` section, count its table body rows across the 30/60/90 and roadmap tables and fail with `ACTIONS_NOT_MIRRORED` if `fit-assessment.yaml.actions` has fewer entries. Attaching a notice should acknowledge a contradiction, never discharge it. Add the same for conventions once the `CONVENTION_UNATTRIBUTED` scan from the convention-cards finding exists: derive the id set from the document and fail on `conventions_rendered` that does not match it.

finding.title: `check_apply.py` can never pass an honest stretch — the branch that exists for it is dead, and the one test covering it asserts on a state the program cannot produce
finding.what_is_wrong: `modes/apply.md` devotes a whole section and a required artifact (`honest-stop.yaml`) to the case where the three-judge loop correctly ends un-passed because the candidate genuinely lacks a must-have. `check_apply.py`'s docstring names this as one of its two reasons to exist: "a stretch candidate told 'failed' abandons an application they should have sent." The honest-stop branch is implemented correctly and validates `honest-stop.yaml` properly. But it is defeated twenty lines earlier: `parse_verdicts` is in `REQUIRED_GATES`, and `parse_verdicts.py:189` writes its receipt as `"pass" if combined == "PASS" else "fail"`. So on any REJECT round the required-gate loop appends `UPSTREAM_FAILED: parse_verdicts verdict=fail`, `findings` is non-empty, and `check_apply` exits 1 regardless of how perfect the honest stop is. `check_apply` can only exit 0 when all three judges PASS. My run was a textbook honest stretch (no Go, no Kubernetes, RabbitMQ not Kafka, all correctly refused entry to the CV) and the mode's completion gate reported failure — indistinguishable from a broken run, and the exact signal that makes a stretch candidate bin a good application.
finding.why_nothing_reports_it: `scripts/tests/test_check_apply.py::test_a_rejected_round_with_a_complete_honest_stop_passes` builds its workspace with `_good_workspace()`, which loops over every gate in `REQUIRED` and journals each one with `journal.receipt(ws, gate, {}, "pass")` — including `parse_verdicts` — and only THEN overwrites the round file with `rounds.merge_round(ws, 1, {"combined_verdict": "REJECT"})`. In a real run those two facts cannot come apart: the same script writes both. The fixture therefore constructs a `parse_verdicts receipt=pass` + `combined_verdict=REJECT` state that `parse_verdicts.py` will never emit, and the one test guarding the honest-stop path asserts on it. The test is green, the branch is dead, and nothing else in the suite exercises `check_apply` against a receipt `parse_verdicts` actually wrote.
finding.reproduction:
$ cd <workspace>   # honest stretch: judge-round-1.json REJECT, valid honest-stop.yaml, all other gates pass
$ python3 $REPO/scripts/check_apply.py --workspace .
UPSTREAM_FAILED: parse_verdicts verdict=fail (REJECT: ats returned REJECT; REJECT: recruiter returned REJECT; REJECT: hiring_manager returned REJECT)
rc=1

# same workspace, only the parse_verdicts receipt forced to what the test fixture writes:
$ cp -R <workspace> /tmp/applytest && cd /tmp/applytest
$ python3 -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'$REPO/scripts');import journal; journal.receipt('.', 'parse_verdicts', {}, 'pass', [])"
$ python3 $REPO/scripts/check_apply.py --workspace .
rc=0

# the sole finding is UPSTREAM_FAILED; honest-stop.yaml validated fine (classification honest_stretch,
# verdict blocked, reason and evidence present) and interview-brief.md exists.
# Baseline confirmed green: python3 -m pytest scripts/tests -q -p no:cacheprovider -> 797 passed
finding.fix: In `scripts/check_apply.py`, exclude `parse_verdicts` from the receipt-verdict assertion (keep it in the presence check — its `MISSING_RECEIPT` role against a hand-written `combined_verdict: PASS` is the reason it is listed, and that role is unaffected). Concretely: split `REQUIRED_GATES` into `REQUIRED_PRESENT = (..., "parse_verdicts", ...)` and `REQUIRED_PASSING = ("check_personal_data", "check_claims", "check_render_freshness", "lint_cv")`, run the `MISSING_RECEIPT` loop over the first and the `UPSTREAM_FAILED` check over the second. Then fix `scripts/tests/test_check_apply.py`: give `_good_workspace` a `combined` parameter and journal the `parse_verdicts` receipt as `"pass" if combined == "PASS" else "fail"`, so no fixture can build a state `parse_verdicts.py` cannot emit. Add a test that runs the real `parse_verdicts.main()` over three REJECT judge files and then asserts `check_apply.main() == 0` with a valid `honest-stop.yaml`.

verdicts.verdict:
## VERDICT: STANDS-WITH-LOWER-SEVERITY (high, not critical) — and the proposed fix is wrong

**It reproduces, exactly as written.** Real `enter_mode` + real `parse_verdicts.main()` over three REJECT judge files + a valid `honest-stop.yaml`:

```
$ python3 $REPO/scripts/parse_verdicts.py --workspace $W --round 1 --ats ... --recruiter ... --hiring-manager ...
REJECT: ats returned REJECT
REJECT: recruiter returned REJECT
REJECT: hiring_manager returned REJECT
parse_verdicts rc=1
$ python3 $REPO/scripts/check_apply.py --workspace $W
UPSTREAM_FAILED: parse_verdicts verdict=fail (REJECT: ats returned REJECT; REJECT: recruiter returned REJECT; REJECT: hiring_manager returned REJECT)
rc=1
# same workspace, parse_verdicts receipt forced to what the fixture writes:
$ python3 -c "...journal.receipt('.', 'parse_verdicts', {}, 'pass', [])" && python3 $REPO/scripts/check_apply.py --workspace .
rc=0
```
Baseline confirmed: `python3 -m pytest scripts/tests -q -p no:cacheprovider` → **797 passed**. And it is not a recorded limit: the plan states the requirement disjunctively — "the round's PASS **or** a classified honest stop" (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-09-1-migration-and-p0-fixes.md:5232`, same at :4677), `SKILL.md:503` lists `check_apply`'s fire conditions as "a missing receipt, an unclassified stop, a missing brief" — no rejected round — and the plan's own `REQUIRED_GATES` block (:5110) contains the bug verbatim, so nobody chose this. Nothing consumes `check_apply`'s receipt downstream (`grep -rn "check_apply" scripts/*.py` → only comments), so no automation is blocked; the harm is that the mode's completion gate tells an honest-stretch run "do not deliver", which is what apply.md:148 exists to prevent.

**Two things the finding overstates.** "The branch is dead" is wrong — the honest-stop branch *executes and validates* on a real REJECT round; I broke the stop file and got `BAD_STOP_CLASSIFICATION`, `BAD_STOP_VERDICT`, and both `INCOMPLETE_STOP` findings printed alongside `UPSTREAM_FAILED`. What is unreachable is only the rc=0/silent outcome. "Indistinguishable from a broken run" is also soft: the finding line names all three REJECTs. Net: a false *fail*, in a codebase whose stated thesis is false *passes* — real, but high, not critical.

**The fix as written trades one silent failure for another, which the house rules say is not a fix.** `parse_verdicts.combine()` returns `AMBIGUOUS` — not REJECT — when a judge emits no `VERDICT:` line, and `check_apply` treats every non-`PASS` combined verdict identically. I applied the proposed `REQUIRED_PRESENT`/`REQUIRED_PASSING` split to a copy and ran it against a round where the ATS judge's reply was truncated before its verdict block:

```
NO_VERDICT: ats emitted no VERDICT: line — re-dispatch this judge
combined_verdict = AMBIGUOUS
--- proposed-fix check_apply on an AMBIGUOUS round ---
rc=0        # silent, no output
```
A judge that never judged, papered over by a hand-written `honest_stretch`, now exits 0 clean. Two repairs that don't open that hole: (a) in `check_apply`, accept a `parse_verdicts` `fail` receipt only when the recorded `combined_verdict == "REJECT"` *and* `honest-stop.yaml` validated — keep `UPSTREAM_FAILED` for `AMBIGUOUS`; or (b) better, follow the codebase's own established pattern (`consistency.py`, `check_evidence_refs.py`: "this script reports, it does not judge" → verdict `"recorded"`, which is already in `PASSING_VERDICTS`) and have `parse_verdicts` write `"recorded"` for a *cleanly parsed* round and `"fail"` only for `AMBIGUOUS`/`NO_VERDICT`; `MISSING_RECEIPT` and the `combined != PASS` honest-stop demand both survive untouched. The finding's test half is right and should be kept: `_good_workspace` must not be able to journal a `parse_verdicts` state the script cannot emit.

finding.title: The claim-provenance gate does not look at experience bullets, so fabricated technologies and a fabricated metric pass every apply gate
finding.what_is_wrong: `check_claims.py` — the only script enforcing SKILL.md's load-bearing rule — scopes itself to `skills` leaves, `certifications`, `experience[].title` and `education[].degree`. Bullets are excluded. But bullets are where achievements and technologies actually live on a CV, and where SKILL.md's own NOT-ALLOWED examples land ("Adding a posting keyword the candidate has no genuine experience with", "Fabricating metrics ('improved performance by 40%')"). I copied three terms straight out of `posting.yaml.keywords` — Kubernetes, Go, Kafka — into `tailored-profile.yaml` experience bullets, together with an invented number, all absent from `profile.yaml`. `check_claims.py`, `lint_cv.py`, `check_personal_data.py` and `lint_no_prediction.py` all exited 0. Secondary, and part of the same hole: `modes/apply.md` — the mode that must CREATE `claims.yaml` — mentions the file zero times. Its six required keys and the closed set `SOURCE_KINDS = ("profile-line", "session-answer", "fetched-artifact")` exist only in `scripts/check_claims.py:39-40` and, partially, in a single example in `modes/interview.md` §6(b) that a later mode reads. A fresh model in apply mode has no documented way to write the file the gate demands.
finding.why_nothing_reports_it: The docstring justifies the exclusion — "Free prose is deliberately out: rewording prose IS the skill's job, and a gate that fires on every honest run is a gate people learn to skip" — so tests assert the current scope and pass. But that rationale defends excluding *rewording*; it does not defend excluding *new proper-noun technology tokens*, which is a different and mechanically separable class. Meanwhile the gate's own finding text ("A keyword that appears in the job description is not evidence the candidate has it — source it or move it to HONEST-GAPS") reads as though it covers exactly the case it does not, so a reader who sees it fire on the Skills section reasonably concludes the CV is covered. And the fallback backstop is a subagent: the ATS screener REWARDS the fabricated keywords, and the hiring-manager judge is the only party that might catch it — a model, with no receipt.
